city.act.savings.prompt: E — go to the savings bank window
city.act.tickets.prompt: E — ask at the box office
city.bed.nap.1: I shut my eyes for a minute. When I opened them the window's shadow had crept onto the other wall.
city.bed.nap.2: I dozed to the ticking of the clock in the corridor. The dream was short and warm, like a sandwich.
city.bed.nap.3: A nurse looked in, tucked the blanket round me and left without a word.
city.bed.night.1: The sheets crackled with starch. The sea was murmuring outside, and then I heard nothing at all.
city.bed.night.2: I dreamt I was climbing an endless staircase to the sun and not getting tired at all.
city.bed.night.3: I woke to spoons ringing in glasses in the corridor: someone was bringing tea.
city.bed.private.1: This is someone's bed. The cover's been smoothed by a hand, there's a dent in the pillow. No.
city.bed.private.2: A stranger's bed smells of a stranger's soap. I just stood next to it.
city.bed.private.3: Someone else sleeps here. I have to find a place of my own.
city.cafe.book.0: The first page, the ink faded: "Open at last. The coffee smells, the stair spirals, and we seem to be sitting inside a saucer. Thanks to the architect. — The first guests."
city.cafe.book.1: "Came with my daughter. She demanded ice cream three times, and three times we didn't mind." Next to it, a cone with three scoops.
city.cafe.book.2: In green ink, in a hurry: "The parrot told me 'Mind the doors, please' and I stepped back. There are no doors here. Thank you, Kesha!"
city.cafe.book.3: "Played chess with the Professor. Lost in seven moves. He said: 'Never mind, you resigned in good time.' A good school."
city.cafe.book.4: In a different pen: "Lighthouse keeper on duty. Dropped in off my watch. I confirm: my beam can be seen from your window. It looks better from here than from my side."
city.cafe.book.5: Two hands side by side, two pens: "We both came. Sat by the window until closing. One told about the static, the other about how long it had been since he'd heard a voice without noise. Paid half and half. No static. — I. and G."
city.cafe.book.6: In a corner of the page someone has drawn a saucer with eyes and written: "This is us." Below, in the barista's hand: "Leaving it as it is."
city.cafe.book.7: A fresh entry by the manager: "The pages are running out, we'll start a new book soon. The pen is next to the book, and if you've no thoughts, draw a saucer. We love saucers."
city.cafe.cake.fri: Friday: the "Anthill", a brown mound with nuts. A small boy at the case has already chosen and is waiting for his mother to.
city.cafe.cake.mon: Monday: the case holds a chocolate "Potato" and two eclairs. The eclairs, judging by the price tag, hope to last until Tuesday.
city.cafe.cake.sat: Saturday: the "Saucer" cake, round, glazed, with a small spiral wafer on top like the stair. People take it whole, for tea.
city.cafe.cake.sun: Sunday: pastries for everyone on a tray with a red rim. A card: "One each, please. In exceptional cases, two."
city.cafe.cake.thu: Thursday: apple puffs. A hand-written line on the price tag: "The last one, don't be shy."
city.cafe.cake.tue: Tuesday: Napoleon cake. The layers are so thin it looks as if someone counted them with tweezers.
city.cafe.cake.wed: Wednesday: little cream baskets with a berry. Each berry sits exactly in the middle, like a seal.
city.cafe.chess.1: I took the Captain's place at the board: he said he had "business at the lighthouse", though he was probably just tired of losing. The Professor moves his pawns as if apologising. Twenty moves later I was the one apologising.
city.cafe.chess.2: After school the board belongs to two schoolboys. They play fast and loud, whispering at every move. They let me into the third game as a newcomer from outside.
city.cafe.chess.3: At weekends the chess moves to the nearest table: here they play for coffee. The loser orders. I lost, but the Captain ordered himself: "A newcomer's first coffee is on us."
city.cafe.chess.4: The Professor mates me on the ninth move, silently, without taking off his hat. Then, just as silently, he sets the pieces back and shows where I could have won. It turns out, on the sixth.
city.cafe.chess.5: The Captain plays only black and only one opening. He calls it the "Lighthouse Defence". He doesn't explain what it means, and wins in such a way that you can't take offence.
city.cafe.chess.6: The game was interrupted by the parrot announcing "Terminus". We finished in a draw: everyone looked at Kesha and forgot whose move it was.
city.cafe.chess.prompt: E — sit down with the chess players
city.cafe.cook.fri: "Friday: curd fritters. Sour cream comes with them, but only whoever remembers to ask gets it."
city.cafe.cook.mon: The cook, without turning round: "Monday, noodle soup. My grandmother's recipe; don't ask my grandmother."
city.cafe.cook.prompt: E — ask the cook about the dish of the day
city.cafe.cook.sat: "Saturday: pilaf for everyone. Whoever comes first gets the bottom of the pot, the best part."
city.cafe.cook.sun: "On Sundays I don't cook. I only warm up what I left from Saturday and call it home cooking."
city.cafe.cook.thu: "Thursday: stuffed cabbage. Probably the best in the district today. Tomorrow merely good."
city.cafe.cook.tue: "Tuesday: rissoles and mash. I make the mash myself and don't spare the butter; dieticians are asked not to look."
city.cafe.cook.wed: "Wednesday: fish and potatoes. The fish came from the pier this morning, still arguing."
city.cafe.crate.1: A crate of sleeves: the records stand on edge like books in a library. On the spines, in pencil, the button numbers. The numbers stopped matching the buttons long ago.
city.cafe.crate.2: A sleeve marked "Left behind in April". Inside, a postcard of the sea and a record of the same sea, only audible.
city.cafe.crate.3: One record is labelled "D-3 (by request, do not take away)". Someone has underlined "do not take away" twice. So it has been taken away.
city.cafe.crate.4: Deep in the crate, a shabby sleeve: "To the Saucer's best listener. Thank you for never interrupting. — The Sanatorium Orchestra."
city.cafe.crate.5: A note is stuck on the side: "The machine takes coins. Not buttons: Kesha tested it." Next to it, a beak print.
city.cafe.esp.d1: At lunchtime the machine never stops: steam, click, steam, click. The cups leave on a tray and come back empty, with spoons in the saucers.
city.cafe.esp.d2: A dark thread creeps slowly from the spout. Watch it for over a minute and you want a glass of water and a second cup.
city.cafe.esp.e1: By evening the coffee is made less often and the steam lasts longer. While the stream runs, the barista looks out of the window: that is where the best part is now.
city.cafe.esp.e2: A note is taped to the machine's panel: "Don't tap the gauge. It's nervous." The needle trembles as if it has heard everything.
city.cafe.esp.m1: By eight everything is ready: the bar wiped, the machine warm, the chairs down on their legs. Now the barista silently watches the pressure gauge like a barometer before a long journey.
city.cafe.esp.m2: The first cup of the morning is not for the guests. It is set on the edge of the bar on its saucer and left to cool until the first visitor comes in. They say the café treats itself first.
city.cafe.esp.m3: The grounds are tamped with one short, level press. A click of the lever, a hiss, and the hall smells so good the chairs seem to shuffle closer.
city.cafe.esp.n: The machine cools, ticking softly. In the morning it will be woken again.
city.cafe.espresso.prompt: E — watch the coffee being made
city.cafe.feed.1: I poured the seeds into the saucer and said "Terminus". Kesha waited until I had finished, cracked one, thought, and announced: "Please vacate the cars." The barista laughed and took a pastry from the case: "Finder gets one on the house. You've found him again, more or less."
city.cafe.feed.2: Kesha pecked a seed and said: "Thank you for travelling with us." He never used to say that. The barista set a pastry on a saucer in front of me.
city.cafe.feed.3: Kesha ate one seed and hid the rest under his perch "until the next stop". The pastry on the house is already waiting on the bar.
city.cafe.feed.prompt: E — treat Kesha to sunflower seeds
city.cafe.guestbook.prompt: E — leaf through the guest book
city.cafe.juke.a1: Button A-1: a waltz on a record worn to silver. The machine sighs, creaks, then gives out the waltz as if it had never done anything else.
city.cafe.juke.a4: A-4, a march. Without looking up, the barista turns it down a notch: someone by the window is reading the paper and the drum is in his way.
city.cafe.juke.b1: B-1: a song about the sea in a foreign language. An elderly couple at a table falls silent on the second line and listens to the end, holding on to their cups.
city.cafe.juke.b5: B-5: a twist. The chairs at the nearest table suddenly start tapping along by themselves, and there are shoes underneath them too.
city.cafe.juke.c2: C-2: instead of music, an announcer's voice reading the coastal weather. Someone must have mixed up the sleeve. I listened to the end: no rain tomorrow.
city.cafe.juke.c6: C-6. Next to it, by hand: "DO NOT PRESS". I pressed. A flute began, very quietly, as if from far away. Now I see why nobody presses it.
city.cafe.juke.d3: The third button from the left, D-3: the tune I was looking for plays whole, with no static, to the last note. The barista nods: "It's the most requested. They say someone taped it off the air."
city.cafe.juke.g1: In the morning the jukebox is quiet: G-1, a soft little waltz under the hiss of the coffee machine. The barista nods along without noticing.
city.cafe.juke.g3: In the evening the jukebox is louder: G-3, a foxtrot, and someone by the stairs is already tapping a foot, pretending to tie a shoelace.
city.cafe.kesha.0: Kesha sits on his perch at the end of the bar and looks with one eye as if checking a ticket. Then he announces: "Next stop, the Saucer." We're already on it, but I didn't argue.
city.cafe.kesha.1: Today Kesha is silent and only bobs his head to the jukebox. The barista whispers: "He's on leave after the tour."
city.cafe.kesha.2: "Mind the doors, please!" Kesha announces when someone heads for the stairs. There are no doors in the hall, but everyone ducks a little.
city.cafe.kesha.3: Kesha has learned a new word and says it only when nobody asks. The word is "Horizon". I think he just likes the sound of it.
city.cafe.kesha.4: Kesha studies me for a long time, then says very clearly: "Ticket." I show him my empty palms. Kesha turns away, disappointed.
city.cafe.kesha.5: Beside the perch is a saucer, marked in felt pen: "For Kesha. Sunflower seeds. But first say 'Terminus'." Kesha waits without blinking.
city.cafe.kesha.6: Kesha has got used to me: he no longer turns away but tilts his head a little. The barista says he does that for people who bring seeds.
city.cafe.ledge.d1: By day the glass is warm as a stove, and the spoons on their saucers throw sunbeams on the ceiling. It is hot and very cheerful to sit here.
city.cafe.ledge.d2: On a paper napkin, in pencil: "The window is best at seven in the evening. Do come." No signature.
city.cafe.ledge.m1: The ledge by the glass is still cool, the light grey and soft. Below, the promenade wakes: first the street-washing truck, then the first bicycle.
city.cafe.ledge.m2: Somebody has left a glass of water with a twig in it on the ledge. The twig has already put out a white root.
city.cafe.ledge.n1: At night the ledge is the quietest place in the Saucer. The lamps reflect in the glass, and it seems another hall hangs outside, empty and upside down.
city.cafe.ledge.n2: Below, the promenade lights; above, the stars; between them a black strip of sea. One far-off boat crawls along it, and I feel like waving my glass at it.
city.cafe.ledge.s1: There it is. By seven the glass turns copper, then pink, and every cup throws a long shadow all the way to the stairs. At the nearby tables everyone falls quiet at once.
city.cafe.ledge.s2: A disc of sun lies in my palm, still warm. In a minute it will slide to the floor and go toward the stairs, and I'll sit beside it a little longer.
city.cafe.ledge.s3: The ledge lamp is on but not needed yet: there is light enough. The barista has quietened the machine so as not to disturb it. Nobody says it aloud, but this is called "the minute of sunset".
city.cafe.pen.1: I wrote: "Was here. It's good for thinking, with a staircase underfoot." Thought a moment and added the date.
city.cafe.pen.2: I didn't know what to write, so I drew a saucer. It came out more like a hat. I captioned it: "Saucer (view from below)."
city.cafe.pen.3: I added in a corner: "Hi, Kesha!" with an exclamation mark. Thought and added a second.
city.cafe.pen.4: Under someone else's entry I wrote: "Agreed." What with, I only worked out as I closed the book, but I didn't rub it out.
city.cafe.tel.d1: By day the town in the lens is a scale model: the cable car crawls from station to station, and a tiny cyclist on the promenade never reaches the corner while I watch.
city.cafe.tel.d2: I found the sanatorium roof in the lens. Something is drying on it: washing or flags, I can't tell from here. Maybe both.
city.cafe.tel.m1: In the morning the telescope shows the fishing boats coming home, each with a white thread of gulls behind it. One gull sits on a bow and is in no hurry at all.
city.cafe.tel.m2: Down on the promenade someone is hosing the paving. Through the telescope it shines like a freshly washed plate.
city.cafe.tel.n1: At night the lighthouse beam crosses the lens slowly, like a clock hand. I count: four seconds until the next sweep.
city.cafe.tel.n2: The windows on the hillside burn in different ways: warm ones, blue ones from a TV, and one that blinks. Is somebody signalling? Most likely a bad bulb.
city.cafe.tel.n3: No moon, but for a second the dark eyepiece reflects the whole Saucer from inside: the lamps, the tables, and me with my eye to the tube.
city.cafe.tel.s1: Toward evening the sun settles on the water like a yolk on a saucer, and the water around it turns pink. The coin ran out before the sunset did.
city.cafe.tel.s2: The lighthouse lamp is lit while the sky is still bright. In the lens the beam looks like a thread just pulled through a needle.
city.closed.cafe.bar: The bar is empty, the coffee machine under a towel. A note on the till: "Open at eight."
city.closed.cafe.chairs: The chairs are up on the tables, legs in the air. The floor is still damp from the mop.
city.closed.cafe.machine: The plug is pulled and hung neatly on a hook. The music is asleep.
city.closed.club.counter: The window is latched shut. A card on the glass: "Closed till tomorrow."
city.closed.club.screen: The screen is behind its velvet curtain. The next show is tomorrow.
city.closed.club.seats: The hall is empty, the seats folded up. It smells of curtain dust and, faintly, of tangerines.
city.closed.cog.games: Everything is under covers, the balls and pieces locked away in the cupboard.
city.closed.cog.seats: The chairs are pushed under the tables in neat rows. Someone left a scarf on one.
city.closed.library.desk: The lamp on the lending desk is out, the date stamp put away in the drawer. Waiting for morning.
city.closed.library.shelf: A cord with a card is strung across the shelf: "The library is closed. The books are asleep too."
city.closed.market.stall: The stall is under a tarpaulin weighed down with a brick. The scales went home.
city.closed.store.counter: The department is closed. The display case is under grey cloth with a card: "Stocktaking."
city.cm.boardA.1: Notice: on Wednesday at 19:00 the house committee meets in the hall. Agenda: 1) the leak from 3-05 into 1-05, 2) the kettle in the hall, 3) any other business. There will be tea.
city.cm.boardA.2: Added by hand: "In 1-05 it drips from the ceiling onto the piano. The piano is in tune, the ceiling is not. Please take measures. The neighbours below."
city.cm.boardA.3: Reply: "Nobody in 3-05 poured anything. It is condensation. The residents of 3-05." Below, in another hand: "Condensation does not come with soap suds."
city.cm.boardA.4: Minutes of the meeting: the commission went up to 3-05 with a basin. Established: the bath tap was shut, but not quite, and the sink drain was shut quite, but not where it should. The parties made peace over tea.
city.cm.boardA.5: The committee reports: the tap in 3-05 has been replaced and the stain on the ceiling in 1-05 whitewashed. The person on duty drew a small cloud on the whitewash with her palm: "Let it stay as a keepsake." Thanks to all.
city.cm.boardA.6: Notice: on Saturday at 19:00, a joint evening at the television. A film about sailors will be shown. Bring your own chairs: we have very few.
city.cm.boardA.7: The committee's note: "On Saturday please do not talk, do not rattle the chairs and do not comment on the sailors. Latecomers stand by the wall. The little cloud on the ceiling may be viewed after the film."
city.cm.boardB.1: A cat is missing. Grey, with a white shirt-front, answers to "Markiz" and to the sound of a tin being opened. Last seen in the hall near the kitchen. If you find him, don't feed him, call flat 3-07: he is on a diet.
city.cm.boardB.2: Markiz has been seen: 1) in the cellar, Lidia is sure; 2) on the roof, the boy from 3-07 is not sure; 3) in the canteen by the fish-soup pot, the cook is upset. Three versions, one cat.
city.cm.boardB.3: Added: "If Markiz is not back by Thursday, he has gone to the fishermen. Don't be cross with the cat: he has taste."
city.cm.boardB.4: A girl from 1-03 brought a drawing: a cat in a fur hat and a sign "I'm not lost, I'm out for a walk." The committee accepted the drawing and hung it up. The search goes on.
city.cm.boardB.5: The committee is glad to announce: Markiz the cat has been found! He was asleep in the laundry basket by the folding table, on somebody's sailor vest. The vest is in the lost-property box; let its owner collect it.
city.cm.boardB.6: Notice: on Saturday at 19:00, a joint evening at the television, a film about sailors. Markiz the cat is invited; his place is on the committee's bench. Bring your own chairs.
city.cm.boardB.7: The committee's note: "Please don't talk, rattle the chairs or wake Markiz during the finale. He watches the sailors more closely than anyone."
city.cm.book.1: The complaints and suggestions book, first page: "Please bring the raisins back into the compote. Flat 3-02." The cook's reply in pen: "The raisins boiled down. They are in there, only in a scattered form."
city.cm.book.2: "The cutlets are good. But the cook sings too loudly at the serving line, and his voice, forgive me, is better than the cutlets. Flat 1-06." Reply: "Thank you. I'll sing quieter. I make no promise for the cutlets, they are quiet enough."
city.cm.book.3: "I suggest pancakes on Saturdays. Lyova, flat 3-07, aged 11." Beside it in blue ink: "We support it! The whole third staircase." The cook: "Pancakes will come when somebody gives me a bigger pan."
city.cm.book.4: "Thanks to the cook for Thursday's fish soup: after it, life gets better. Pyotr Semyonovich and the chess section." The cook added: "Passed your regards to the fishermen."
city.cm.chess.1: In the morning the board is taken: Pyotr Semyonovich plays white against Uncle Gena from the third floor, both in slippers. I sat opposite the winner. The game was long and ended in a draw "on account of age".
city.cm.chess.2: In the afternoon Pyotr Semyonovich sits alone at the board, playing himself. "When there is no opponent, one must be honest on both sides," he said, and slid the black pieces to me. I lost with dignity.
city.cm.chess.3: Towards evening spectators gather at the board: all of them know how one ought to move, none of them knows how to play. I was advised from three sides and made a fourth move, my own. I lost beautifully.
city.cm.chess.4: At night the main light is put out and only the lamp over the chess table stays on. We don't finish the game: we set the clock to "till morning". The pieces won't go anywhere.
city.cm.chess.prompt: E — sit down with the chess players
city.cm.duty.extra: A note in red pencil: "We are preparing a general clean for the clean-up day. Wash the hall windows only from the inside. Outside, they are washed by those not afraid of heights: Lidia Arkadyevna and the wind."
city.cm.duty.fri: Friday, flat 1-08: get the hall ready for the weekend, wipe the board by the door, take forgotten mittens to the lost-property box.
city.cm.duty.mon: The hall duty rota. Monday, flat 1-03: sweep, wipe the tables, check the water heater. Signed: "Lidia Arkadyevna. Already swept, already checked."
city.cm.duty.sat: Saturday. The general clean-up at 10:00: buckets and rags by the kitchen. Whoever is on duty is in command; the rest obey at least until lunch.
city.cm.duty.sun: Sunday, the hall rests, nobody is on duty. The rule from the wall: "Whoever made the mess cleans it up. Whoever didn't, take a rag anyway if one is near."
city.cm.duty.thu: Thursday, flat 3-02: fish day, air the hall before lunch and after. A note: "Twice. I am not joking."
city.cm.duty.tue: Tuesday, flat 3-06: the hall, the windows, the flowers. Water the flowers from a kettle, but not the one people drink from. The signature is a child's, with a tail on the letter D.
city.cm.duty.wed: Wednesday, flat 1-07: take out the paper, fold the chairs after the committee meeting. Count the chairs by heads and by legs.
city.cm.fold.1: I fold somebody's sheets: two corners in one hand, two in the other, as Lidia Arkadyevna showed me. It comes out as neat as in a shop.
city.cm.fold.2: A striped sleeve sticks out of the basket. I pulled it out: a sailor's vest, a big one, smelling of the sea and laundry soap. I put it back and laid a pillowcase over it like a blanket.
city.cm.fold.3: The folding table creaks on one leg. I put a folded newspaper under it. Now it creaks on two, but in a different key.
city.cm.gymtt.1: The "Health" section. Monday and Wednesday, 19:00: exercises for all who make it. Led by Zinaida Pavlovna; she has one whistle for everybody.
city.cm.gymtt.2: Tuesday and Thursday, 18:00: wall bars and pull-ups for schoolchildren. Pencilled underneath: "Whoever can't pull up will explain why afterwards."
city.cm.gymtt.3: Friday and Sunday: the gym is free. One mat, one wall of bars, a shared conscience.
city.cm.gymtt.4: Saturday, 9:00: the pensioners. Gently, no jerking, tea afterwards. Everyone else, do not disturb until ten.
city.cm.kids.1: Children's drawings: a house on legs, big, with a red roof. From every window somebody looks out with a cup. The caption: "Us." Lyova, aged 11.
city.cm.kids.2: The second drawing: the hall and a samovar as huge as a lighthouse. Little people in hats stand around it. The caption: "We drink tea. The tea never runs out."
city.cm.kids.3: A very small sheet: a cat in a fur hat. The caption "Markiz", with one letter turned the wrong way.
city.cm.kids.4: A charcoal drawing: a cable car over the sea, three gulls and one person in the cabin. The person is waving. The gulls look dignified.
city.cm.lostA.1: The lost-property box. On top: one red-striped mitten, a scarf with no owner, a child's boot for the right foot and a tag "Lyova, 3-07". Let him collect it. We'll wait for the second mitten.
city.cm.lostA.2: A blue basin has appeared in the box with a tag "from 3-05". Added: "The basin walked about the floors until it found the way down. Its owner asks forgiveness and wants it back."
city.cm.lostA.3: The basin has been returned. In its place a jar of cherry jam, on the lid: "For the ceiling." A jar is not lost property, but it was put in the box for the kindest of reasons. Let it stand.
city.cm.lostB.1: The lost-property box: one mitten, an umbrella without spokes and a collar with a tag "Markiz, flat 3-07". The collar is empty. That is worrying.
city.cm.lostB.2: A note lies by the collar: "Found in the laundry basket by the table, asleep on a sailor's vest." The vest itself is next to it: big, striped, smelling of the sea and a little of cat.
city.cm.lostB.3: The vest was collected by its owner from 1-04, a retired sailor. In its place sits Markiz the cat, looking at everyone like a commission. A note on the box: "A cat is not lost property. But let him sit."
city.cm.menu.fri: Friday. Pea soup, sausages with cabbage, compote. "On Fridays the cook promises pies. If he doesn't forget."
city.cm.menu.mon: Monday. Cabbage soup with sour cream, meatballs with buckwheat, stewed-fruit compote. In chalk underneath: "Bread is free, seconds by conscience."
city.cm.menu.sat: Saturday, short menu: the soup of the day, a pie, tea. We close at 19:00, as always, and not a minute later.
city.cm.menu.sun: Sunday. The canteen is closed. Hot water is in the hall, at the samovar, free. Come on Monday, hungry.
city.cm.menu.thu: Thursday is fish day. Fish soup, hake with potatoes, fruit jelly. Added by hand: "Open the windows early! This is not a joke."
city.cm.menu.tue: Tuesday. Borscht, navy-style pasta, fruit jelly. Added by hand: "Borscht on Tuesdays is a law, not a wish."
city.cm.menu.wed: Wednesday. Pickle soup, a chicken leg with rice, tea with lemon. "One slice of lemon per person. We are counting."
city.cm.menu2.1: Breakfast 8 to 11: porridge (semolina or millet, as luck has it), a cheese sandwich, tea. Bread is on the tray; no need to count it.
city.cm.menu2.2: Lunch 11 to 15: the set meal. Soup, a main, compote. Take a tray on the left, walk along the line; the cook will say what's gone.
city.cm.menu2.3: Supper 15 to 19: a bake, a pie, kefir. Whoever comes five minutes before closing gets what is left, and a smile.
city.cm.menu2.4: Closed. Breakfast from 8:00. In pencil at the bottom: "The cook is a person too. The kettle is in the hall, don't knock."
city.cm.menu2.5: Today is Sunday and the canteen rests. The cook left a note on Saturday: "Pots washed, spoons counted, see you Monday."
city.cm.news.1: The wall newspaper "Our House". "The month in numbers: 16 flats, 41 residents, 1 chess section and 0 quiet evenings. The editors consider this a success."
city.cm.news.2: The column "Our Talents": Lyova from 3-07 drew a house on legs, just like ours, only with paws. The drawing hangs in the hall by the window.
city.cm.news.3: The sports column: pull-ups in the hall. Lidia Arkadyevna, 14 times, on a bet with her grandson. The grandson counted aloud but lost count out of respect.
city.cm.news.4: Poems by residents. "Our house is long as a station hall, / with soup in it, and chess, and all, / and a row of washers in a line, / and water for tea, boiling fine." Flat 1-04, an amateur poet.
city.cm.news.5: The editors ask residents to hand in notes about the television evening: how we sat, what we argued about, who fell asleep first. The winner gets a seat in the front row.
city.cm.queue.1: The laundry list. Mon, Wed, Fri: floors one and two. 1) flat 1-02, "everything"; 2) flat 1-05, pillowcases; 3) flat 1-07, said he'd come, but he need not be believed.
city.cm.queue.2: Tue, Thu: floors three and four. 1) flat 3-04, towels; 2) flat 3-06, children's things, urgent; 3) flat 3-01, curtains. At the bottom: "Machine No. 3 hums. That is normal."
city.cm.queue.3: Sat, Sun: whoever gets there first. The sheet hangs, the pen is on a string, the string is chewed through. Sign up by word of mouth, and we'll remember together.
city.cm.sam.1: The samovar has been warm since the morning. I poured hot water from the tap into a mug and blew on it. The mug is on a chain, burnt into it: "COMMON".
city.cm.sam.2: The hot water in the hall stays hot all day; the person on duty sees to it. The tea leaves are in a tin "for everyone". Thank you, tin.
city.cm.sam.3: The samovar has cooled. On the tap, a note: "It is not necessary to wake the person on duty, but you may."
city.cm.sew.1: A treadle machine, black, with a golden beast on its side. I hemmed trousers: straight at first, then crooked, then I unpicked it and did it again. The trousers agree to be shorter.
city.cm.sew.2: I stitch a torn edge of a curtain. A note on the basket: "From 3-01, urgent." Now the curtain will have a seam and a story.
city.cm.sew.3: Beside it a biscuit tin: buttons of every size, one golden with an anchor. On the lid: "Take what fits. Lidia Arkadyevna."
city.cm.tv.1: Morning exercises. The presenter in a blue leotard counts: "And one, and two..." and the whole hall, without standing up, raises its right arm. Someone by the wall has already breathed in on "three".
city.cm.tv.2: A school broadcast: geography, the Baltic. A map, a pointer, a sea the colour of overcast. The announcer says: "This is where we live." And so we do.
city.cm.tv.3: "The Film Travellers' Club": the host in a scarf walks across a desert and complains of the heat. The hall sympathises, though outside there is a wind from the sea.
city.cm.tv.4: An interval. On the screen a striped test card and a soft tune. Nobody switches over: there are only two channels, and both are on a break.
city.cm.tv.5: A cartoon: a hare and a bear swap hats. The children go quiet. The grown-ups pretend to look out of the window, but they are watching too.
city.cm.tv.6: The news. The announcer reads sternly about the harvest and the Baltic fishermen. Then the weather: "North-westerly wind, sea state three." The hall nods as if it were about their own walk.
city.cm.tv.7: The evening film: black and white, about sailors and letters. The plot is clear from the third minute, and still everyone waits for the end.
city.cm.tv.8: Saturday, the television evening. The hall is full: chairs carried down from the flats, latecomers standing along the wall. Lidia Arkadyevna comments under her breath, Pyotr Semyonovich "is not asleep, he is thinking". When the heroes embrace, somebody sighs loudly. This is what the television in the hall is for.
city.cm.tv.9: The screen is grey and hissing, a test card in the middle. The announcer said good night at eleven. The television does not sleep, but the hall must, and somebody switched it off with a click.
city.cm.wash.1: I loaded the washing and pulled the lever. The machine sighed, took in water and began to rattle like a small tractor. On the stool beside it, somebody's dry shirt waits for its turn.
city.cm.wash.2: While it washes I watch the little window: a striped shirt, my vest, a stripe again. A strange machine: it gives back exactly what it took, and a bit of soapy air.
city.cm.wash.3: Evening wash. The hall smells of washing powder and soup at the same time. Someone at the next machine is quietly counting socks, and seems to be losing.
city.cm.wash.4: At night the drum thunders through the whole house, so I left the washing to soak in a basin. I'll fetch it in the morning. Above the machines, a sheet: "The committee is asleep."
city.cog.bench.boat.1: Today we cut. Lev Arkadyevich laid a sheet of plywood on the bench and pencilled the frames on it. I cut three with the fretsaw. The fourth came out with character. Tomorrow we glue.
city.cog.bench.boat.2: Today we glue. The frames stand on the keel like a fish's ribs. I spread glue on the joints and clamped them with clothes-pegs. The glue smells of apples, which is odd. Now it dries until tomorrow.
city.cog.bench.boat.3: Today we paint. The hull is skinned in veneer and smooth as a pebble. Red below, white deck, blue wheelhouse. Paint up to my elbows. Lev Arkadyevich said that is the first sign of a good model-maker.
city.cog.bench.boat.prompt: E — work on the model launch
city.cog.bench.glider.1: Glider: today the ribs. Thin as kindling. I broke one and cut a new one. Lev Arkadyevich believes a glider loves the patient.
city.cog.bench.glider.2: Glider: today we cover the wing in tissue paper. Glue on every rib, paper without a single wrinkle. A wrinkle, they say, is an air pocket.
city.cog.bench.glider.3: Glider: today we spray the paper with water so it tightens. I watch it dry and breathe, and I know nothing duller or more fascinating.
city.cog.bench.glider.4: Glider: test day. We launched it from the stair landing into the foyer. It made a circle and landed on a bench. The cloakroom attendant, without getting up, gave it a "good".
city.cog.bench.glider.prompt: E — work on the glider's wing
city.cog.bil.1: On Tuesday and Thursday evenings the table belongs to the juniors' section: five of them walk round it counting angles. I was let in last. I learned that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection even when the ball doesn't want it to.
city.cog.bil.2: Friday evenings the league plays: men from the shipyard with their sleeves rolled up. The loser buys tea from the buffet. They poured me one for nothing: witnesses, they say, always get tea.
city.cog.bil.3: On Saturday they play in pairs, two against two, and all four argue over whose ball it was. I stood aside with a cue feeling like a referee. Nobody asked me once.
city.cog.bil.4: Sunday afternoon at the table: fathers with their children. The children stretch on tiptoe, the fathers pretend to miss. I potted two and was a little proud.
city.cog.bil.5: The league final is near. The cushions have been wiped to a shine and the table looks solemn, as before an oath.
city.cog.cart.1: The returns trolley: the books lie with their spines every which way, and you can tell who read what. On top, "Chess for Beginners" with a bookmark at page forty-one. He clearly got no further.
city.cog.cart.2: On Monday the trolley is full: after the weekend everyone returned everything at once. Tamara Ilyinichna sorts without lifting her head or losing count.
city.cog.cart.3: By the weekend the trolley is nearly empty: readers take books away and bring them back later, on Monday. A law of nature.
city.cog.cart.4: In the pile, someone's note: "I didn't take the clock, I only took 'Photography for Amateurs'." On that book's spine, the photo circle's stamp.
city.cog.chess.1: We played on the hourglass from the first-aid room. The sand runs as it pleases. They said it's an ancient method: whoever is faster, the sand is theirs.
city.cog.chess.2: Thursday evening is blitz at the tables. At each, two play and one watches with an opinion. The opinion is louder than the chess.
city.cog.chess.3: Today they play more quietly than usual. Someone is listening for a chess clock to tick somewhere. None does.
city.cog.chess.4: A game with the clock: the left dial cracked, the right whole, both ticking a bit faster than you'd like. I won on time but not on position. They say that counts too.
city.cog.chess.5: A five-minute blitz: the pieces fly, the hand can't keep up with the thought nor the thought with the hand. I lost on the last second and smiled. Tamara Ilyinichna wrote in the log: "Clock in place."
city.cog.clock.1: A chess clock with two dials. The left one has a crack like a lightning bolt. It is ticking. It turns out they use it as a stopwatch: press, the exposure runs, press again, stop.
city.cog.clock.2: Under the clock a note: "Borrowed for a while, will return Thursday. S. G." "Thursday" is crossed out and another Thursday written. Then another.
city.cog.clock.3: The clock ticks as before, but a little sheepishly. Seryozha said he would have taken it back himself but was ashamed, and asked: "Maybe you could carry it? They won't scold you." I thought I would.
city.cog.clock.prompt: E — look at the clock on the bench
city.cog.cues.1: The cues stand by height and by temper. The first was too light. The second was too proud. The third, worn at the tip like an old friend, turned out to be mine.
city.cog.cues.2: On the rail there is a tin of chalk. I chalked the cue and blew on the tip the way the older ones do. At once I felt part of the league.
city.cog.cues.3: At weekends the duty member hands out the cues: "One cue, one person. No waving." I didn't wave.
city.cog.dark.1: Today, negatives. We wind the film in total darkness, by touch, counting in whispers. Seryozha says the dark is where he manages best to stay calm.
city.cog.dark.2: Today, contact sheets: all the frames on one sheet, small as stamps. We choose one. I chose the lighthouse frame; it was the only one not blurred.
city.cog.dark.3: Today, printing. The sheet under the enlarger, red light. We count the exposure on the clock on the second bench: click the left button, click the right; at twelve we lift the frame.
city.cog.dark.4: Today, drying. The prints hang on the line and drip, and it smells of vinegar. Someone is already arguing whether gloss or matt is better.
city.cog.dark.prompt: E — work in the photo lab
city.cog.draft.1: On the drafting board is a drawing: a cable-car lift at 1:20. The angle of the cable is written twice, the second time in red with a question mark.
city.cog.draft.2: A note in the margin: "Seryozha from the photo circle's idea: a mirror in the cabin so passengers see the sea from both sides." Lev Arkadyevich disagreed and agreed.
city.cog.draft.3: A new sheet: "Cabin, model 1:20." The window is cut round, like a porthole. They argued whether it needs a wheel. Those for the wheel won.
city.cog.dry.1: Two finished little boats dry side by side. One has its red side to the very edge, on the other the paint has run a little onto the deck. A card: "Paint takes a day to dry. A day, not five minutes." Underlined twice.
city.cog.dry.2: The little boats on the shelf are dry now and stand upright. A note: "Collect by Sunday or they go to the club fund." Whether anyone will is unknown.
city.cog.dry.3: The shelf is taken up by paint tins: red, white, blue, all open and covered with gauze. It smells like a small harbour.
city.cog.league.1: The Cog Club billiards league: a table in chalk. The top three places belong to the shipyard, fourth to "Unknown", and fifth is a bottle of kefir someone put there for tidiness.
city.cog.league.2: Under the table: "Semi-final on Friday evening. Spectators, please don't stand by the pockets: the pockets get nervous."
city.cog.league.3: The semi-final has been played: a fitter from the shipyard won 3-2 on the last ball. The loser bought tea for everyone, and twice for the witnesses.
city.cog.league.4: "Final on Saturday evening. Spectators sign up with Tamara Ilyinichna. The more people, the quieter they play."
city.cog.league.5: The final has been played. The cup, a bent cog on a stand, sits by the buffet. The winner forgot about it and came back an hour later.
city.cog.lounge.1: "Please do not screw either players or attachments to the table football. Players especially."
city.cog.lounge.2: The machine takes only five-rouble coins and angrily gives back everything else. If anyone knows why, please share.
city.cog.lounge.3: In the photo lab in the evenings something ticks, as if a chess game were being played with nobody there. Anyone in the know, tell Tamara Ilyinichna.
city.cog.meet.1: Circles' meeting on the first Saturday of the month. Agenda: tea. Additionally: the kettle.
city.cog.meet.2: Minutes of the meeting: the clock is to be fixed to the chess table with a chain, and the photographers are to buy a stopwatch. Signed by all, including the stopwatch, which does not exist.
city.cog.models.1: On the stand is yesterday's launch: painted, shining, drying. Next to it a pencilled card: "Don't touch, sticky."
city.cog.models.2: The shelf is almost empty: the launch has gone to the bench, leaving its drawing and an empty stand.
city.cog.models.3: On the stand the launch is unpainted, pale, smelling of pine and glue. Today it gets painted, and tomorrow it will be red.
city.cog.models.4: Next to the launch stands a glider covered in russet paper. On its wing: "Flew. Came back by itself."
city.cog.place.1: On the cloth by the board there is a pale rectangle where the clock stood and a slip: "The clock stood here." For now it's empty.
city.cog.place.2: I pictured the cracked clock coming back to the pale rectangle. For now its only home is the photographers' bench, where it counts the seconds of other people's pictures.
city.cog.place.3: I set the clock on the pale rectangle and the cloth under it seemed to sigh. Tamara Ilyinichna, without getting up, wrote in the log: "Clock in place." There will be a blitz on Thursday.
city.cog.place.prompt: E — look at the clock's place
city.cog.prints.1: A strip of film hangs on the line with wet frames, like a tiny movie. The frames are dark, the faces light: it's always like that with negatives.
city.cog.prints.2: On the line hangs a contact sheet: thirty-six frames in rows. The best are ringed in red. One is ringed three times.
city.cog.prints.3: A large print on the line, still wet: a lighthouse, a dune, a girl with a string bag. The edges curl like pages in a damp book.
city.cog.prints.4: The print has dried and flattened. A pencilled caption: "Dune, six in the evening. S. Gusev." Next to it an empty space for the next one.
city.cog.prints.prompt: E — look at the line of prints
city.cog.rd.1: Tamara Ilyinichna: there is no chess clock in the reading room, we looked under the cupboards. We found a button. The button is waiting for its owner at the cloakroom.
city.cog.rd.2: "The clock is loud: it ticks like a grasshopper. If you've heard a grasshopper in the club, please report to the cloakroom before 7 p.m."
city.cog.rd.3: The Thursday blitz is back on! Sign up with Tamara Ilyinichna. We play on any clock that ticks. Not the hourglass, though.
city.cog.reh.1: The rehearsal schedule on squared paper: Tuesday, Thursday, drama circle, 5 p.m. Wednesday, dance, 4 p.m. Saturday, amateur evening, 5 p.m. Sunday: "the stage rests."
city.cog.reh.2: Today the drama circle rehearses at 5 p.m. Added: "Latecomers play the trees."
city.cog.reh.3: Today dance at 4 p.m. Added: "Indoor shoes required. Socks are not shoes."
city.cog.reh.4: Tonight, the amateur evening. A hand-lettered poster: "Choir, accordion, verse. Entrance free, exit too."
city.cog.reh.5: Today the stage is free. Added: "If you want to rehearse, sign up with the cloakroom attendant."
city.cog.reh.6: A notice: "On Thursday after the blitz, the prize-giving on stage. The drama circle has promised to present the cup with expression."
city.cog.sh.art.1: An album, "Painting of the Baltic." Under the dunes someone has written: "Went there yesterday. Just the same, only no mosquitoes." You can tell the painting was checked against the shore.
city.cog.sh.art.2: An exhibition catalogue. On the print of the lighthouse there is a tea stain shaped like a small cloud. Tamara Ilyinichna said the stain now counts as part of the display.
city.cog.sh.birds.1: "Birds of the Baltic", the borrower's slip on the last page: "Returned. The gull turned out not to be a gull." The pages about gulls are the most thumbed.
city.cog.sh.birds.2: In the margin by the chaffinch, in big letters: "Saw one in our yard! Tamara Ilyinichna, this is for you." Below, the reply: "I saw it. Thank you."
city.cog.sh.chess.1: In the margins of a textbook a hand marks the moves and writes: "Blundered the queen here, never playing again. See you Thursday." Judging by the number of such notes, Thursday has come round more than once.
city.cog.sh.chess.2: A sheet sticks out of the book: the Thursday blitz schedule. The last line: "The clock belongs to the club, take care of it." Below, in another hand: "(if it turns up)."
city.cog.sh.eng.1: "Photography for Amateurs." On the page about exposure someone has written: "Don't count aloud, you cheat. You need a clock that ticks evenly." Good advice.
city.cog.sh.eng.2: A model-maker's magazine with a drawing of a motor launch. The sizes are pencilled in, and on the last page there is a thumbprint in glue.
city.cog.sh.local.1: A bound run of the town paper. In the piece on the club's opening the word "cog" is circled: "It isn't a wheel," the architect explained, "it's hands taking hold of one another."
city.cog.sh.local.2: An old map of the town, the club still on the outskirts. Beside it a dotted line, a road to come that does not exist yet. Someone has carefully drawn it in pencil across the margins.
city.cog.sh.poetry.1: On the flyleaf of the collection is the stamp "Cog Club. Library" and in pencil: "Reading aloud: whispers only." I read it in a whisper. It came out even better.
city.cog.sh.poetry.2: A bookmark between the pages: last year's buffet coupon. The poem on this page is about winter, so the coupon is probably not there by accident.
city.cog.sh.science.1: A popular-science magazine. In an article on the pendulum, in the margin: "A chess clock is a pendulum too. Tested." The signature is illegible, the handwriting hurried.
city.cog.sh.science.2: A physicist's handbook. On the page about light and shadow a developed print is tucked in: the reading-room window with a gull's silhouette on the glass. On the back, the photo circle's stamp.
city.cog.sh.sea.1: A Baltic pilot book, the corners worn. The bookmark is a thread with a bit of sea glass. In the sun the glass puts a green patch on the page.
city.cog.sh.sea.2: A book on sailing ships. Next to a drawing of a schooner, in a child's hand: "We'll build one like this in the workshop." Signed: "Lev Arkadyevich doesn't mind."
city.cog.stage.1: A rehearsal is on: the drama circle works through the farewell scene at the lighthouse. The director claps after every line and the line has to be said again. Not once did it sound the same.
city.cog.stage.2: Saturday evening: a choir of nine, an accordion and a girl who recites verse looking at the ceiling, so as not to be afraid. The hall claps longer than she recited.
city.cog.stage.3: Wednesday, the dance circle. To the piano and a count of "one-two-three" the girls go round the stage in circles. A boy drags a chair: he is the scenery. He tries very hard to be a chair.
city.cog.stagen.1: Dear audience: please do not move the chairs, they stand by rank. Whoever sits in the wrong seat sits in somebody else's.
city.cog.stagen.2: After the Thursday blitz the photo circle will show slides on stage. Do not turn off the light: we see everything anyway.
city.cog.swap.1: Above the rack a slip: "Bring one, take one; take one, bring one." The magazines have gone round here for years. I took the one on top.
city.cog.swap.2: On Mondays the rack has something new: a man from the workshops leaves a stack of popular-science magazines with drawings on the inserts. I took the top one.
city.cog.swap.3: By the weekend the rack is almost bare: everything's gone. One magazine is left, covered in glue stains. It must have been read at the workbench.
city.cog.swap.4: On Sundays the rack isn't restocked. A note on it: "Out of magazines, come on Tuesday." But one turned up anyway, under the note.
city.cog.swap.prompt: E — take a magazine from the swap rack
city.cog.tray.1: The tray is empty, the last drop of developer shining on the bottom. The print hasn't been made yet.
city.cog.tray.2: On the white sheet in the tray outlines are surfacing: two vertical strokes and a horizon. It isn't clear yet what it is, but it will be soon.
city.cog.tray.3: The print is clear now: the lighthouse against the evening sky and a gull that got into the frame by accident and now won't leave. Seryozha swears he didn't feed it.
city.cog.tray.4: The trays are empty. The print has gone to dry and hangs last on the left of the line. It dried lighter than it looked in the red light.
city.cog.tt.1: On Mondays and Wednesdays the circle trains here: the coach puts a tin can on the table and teaches them to hit it with a serve. The can is covered in dents and seems proud of it.
city.cog.tt.2: Tuesday and Thursday evenings they play round-robin: lose, and you go to the end of the queue on the bench. The queue, the old-timers say, is the main part of the game.
city.cog.tt.3: On Friday and Saturday the older pupils come and play knockout. The noise carries to the reading room, and Tamara Ilyinichna knocks on the pipe. The pipe answers.
city.cog.tt.4: On Sunday morning the table is free and the ball is in no hurry. I practised my serve until it worked twice in a row, and stopped on that high note.
city.cog.wsb.1: Today in the workshop: cutting. Plywood on the bench, fretsaws with Lev Arkadyevich. Whoever has no fretsaw draws.
city.cog.wsb.2: Today in the workshop: gluing. Clothes-pegs issued against a signature. Please do not glue the pegs to your sleeves.
city.cog.wsb.3: Today in the workshop: painting. Aprons on the nail. Whoever has no apron paints to one side, and quietly.
city.cog.wsb.4: Please do not bring the chess clock to the workshop: we don't have it, we looked. Lev Arkadyevich.

city.do.aquarium.1: The guppies dart in a shoal, and the catfish lies on the bottom pretending to be a stone. He's good at it.
city.do.aquarium.2: One fish swam up to the glass and looked at me. I'm not sure which of us is in the tank.
city.do.aquarium.3: Bubbles rise steadily from the little castle on the bottom. Watch long enough and you start breathing in time.
city.do.aquarium.4: A sign on the tank: "Do not feed the fish. They are on a diet. Especially Boris." I couldn't find Boris.
city.do.arcade.1: "Sea Battle": I sank two ships out of five. The periscope smells of rubber and other people's foreheads.
city.do.arcade.2: Racing: on the third lap my car went into the ditch and stayed there. The machine beeped something sympathetic.
city.do.arcade.3: "Sniper": nine out of ten. The machine gave me a token for a free game, but the token rolled away somewhere.
city.do.arcade.4: I played "Goalkeeper" until three boys were queuing behind me. Gave way. They played worse.
city.do.barbell.1: I took off all the plates but two small ones. Lifted ten times. The plates weren't that small after all.
city.do.barbell.2: The coach straightened my back and said: "The strength is in your legs, not your face." I stopped grimacing.
city.do.barbell.3: The bar is cold and smells of iron. After the third set my arms hummed like wires.
city.do.barbell.4: Up, down, up. In the wall mirror, a boy with red ears and a very determined look.
city.do.basketball.1: Three out of ten. Every time the ball went thoughtfully round the rim, deciding whether to drop.
city.do.basketball.2: The net is torn, so you can hardly hear a basket. You have to take your own word for it.
city.do.basketball.3: A tall lad showed me how to put backspin on it. The ball obeyed him, and then me.
city.do.basketball.4: The ball thuds on the tarmac like a big heart. I kept going till the sun dropped behind the hoop.
city.do.billiards.1: Aimed for five minutes, struck, and the ball went round every cushion and quietly dropped in. I pretended I'd meant it.
city.do.billiards.2: A man in braces showed me how to chalk the cue and said: "It's not the ball that matters, it's the pause before the shot."
city.do.billiards.3: I'd have torn the cloth if they hadn't stopped me in time. They did. Let me play again, from a safe distance.
city.do.billiards.4: The balls click like chattering teeth. I potted two. Not bad, they say, for the first time in my life.
city.do.binoculars_post.1: Through the binoculars: the buoys, and nobody beyond them. Good. The lifeguard said: "If only it were always like this."
city.do.binoculars_post.2: I found a gull sitting on a buoy looking my way. We stared at each other for a long time.
city.do.binoculars_post.3: Far out a swimmer in a red cap goes steadily, unhurried, as if he knows where.
city.do.binoculars_post.4: The eyepieces are warm from other people's eyes. The sea is closer through them, but quieter, somehow.
city.do.binoculars_post.prompt: E — look through the lifeguard's binoculars
city.do.blackboard.1: I chalked "2 + 2 =" and paused. The chalk squeaked by itself, as if prompting.
city.do.blackboard.2: Left on the board from the last lesson: "On duty: Lebedev." I added: "and me".
city.do.blackboard.3: I drew a sun, rubbed it out, then drew it again, bigger. The cloth smells of chalk and wet wool.
city.do.blackboard.4: I wrote my name and looked at it a long time. On the board it looked like someone else's.
city.do.checkup.1: The doctor listened with a cold stethoscope and said: "Your heart works. Sometimes overtime."
city.do.checkup.2: "Say 'ah'." "Ahh." "Good. More sun, fewer sweets, and sleep at night."
city.do.checkup.3: The doctor tapped my knee with a little hammer and my leg jerked. "Reflexes fine. We'll check your thoughts another time."
city.do.checkup.4: They wrote "Practically healthy" on my card. I asked what "practically" means. The doctor smiled and didn't say.
city.do.chess.1: I lost to an old man in a beret. But he showed me the Sicilian defence and said I had "honest moves".
city.do.chess.2: Drew with a girl of about nine. She thought a long time over every move and swung her legs.
city.do.chess.3: I won! My opponent shook my hand and said he'd let me. Then he thought and said he hadn't.
city.do.chess.4: We both forgot whose move it was and started over. Then again. The game never really began, but it was nice.
city.do.chess.prompt: E — play a game of chess
city.do.choir.1: The choir sang without words, just voices, and the vaults overhead hummed like a vast seashell.
city.do.choir.2: The choir leader stopped them: "Altos, you're singing about the sun as if it were the bus timetable. Again!"
city.do.choir.3: An old man in the back row sang slightly off, but so happily that nobody corrected him.
city.do.choir.4: They went over the song about ten times, and on the tenth I caught myself quietly singing along.
city.do.choir.prompt: E — listen to the choir rehearsal
city.do.cinema.1: The Man Who Waited for the Lighthouse. He waited forty years, and all that time the lighthouse waited for him. The whole hall cried at the end. Me too, a bit.
city.do.cinema.2: A comedy about a holidaymaker whose hat blew away. The hat flew round the whole town and came back. We laughed so hard the screen shook.
city.do.cinema.3: Before the film, a science reel: "The Sun Is Our Home". The film snapped at the best bit, and for a minute we all watched white light.
city.do.cinema.4: The film was old and silent, with a pianist playing along. By the end I felt it was me up there on the screen, walking down an empty street.
city.do.cooking.1: They trusted me with the potatoes. The peel came off in one long spiral, and the cook said, "There's a husband in the making."
city.do.cooking.2: I chopped onions and cried while the cook told me about her first husband, and I couldn't tell which was making me cry.
city.do.cooking.3: I stirred the kissel with a big wooden spoon so it wouldn't go lumpy. It went lumpy anyway, but less than it might have.
city.do.cooking.4: I laid the cutlets on the tray in neat rows, like toy soldiers. They let me taste the first one. It was the general.
city.do.dance.1: I shuffled about to a waltz, counting one-two-three under my breath. On "three" I always trod on my own foot.
city.do.dance.2: An old couple turned so lightly the floor might have been water. I tried it: the floor turned out to be parquet.
city.do.dance.3: The dance teacher clapped: "Straighten your back, young man! You're not picking mushrooms!"
city.do.dance.4: The music stopped and I turned a little longer. Nobody laughed. That's how it's done here.
city.do.darkroom.1: In the red light the pier slowly surfaced on the white paper. As if someone were remembering it.
city.do.darkroom.2: Left it too long in the developer and the print went black. The club leader said: "Night photography. Conceptual."
city.do.darkroom.3: On someone else's film that we developed, there was me. From behind, on the promenade. I don't remember being photographed.
city.do.darkroom.4: It smells of vinegar and secrets. The prints dry on a line with clothes-pegs, like washing.
city.do.darkroom.prompt: E — develop prints in the darkroom
city.do.darts.1: First dart in the wall, second in the two, third dead in the bull. I stopped there so as not to spoil it.
city.do.darts.2: The board is full of holes like a night sky. I added three more stars.
city.do.darts.3: Someone behind me said: "Don't aim with your eye, aim with your elbow." I tried. Hit the door frame with my elbow.
city.do.darts.4: Forty-one points. Someone chalked my name on the board. Spelt wrong, but still nice.
city.do.easel.1: I painted the sea. It looks like the sea, if you really want it to. The studio leader said: "Bold."
city.do.easel.2: I mixed blue and yellow and got green. Mixed everything and got a puddle. That's a discovery too.
city.do.easel.3: I drew the sun in the corner like a little kid, with stick rays. Someone beside me sighed: "Like everyone does. And rightly so."
city.do.easel.4: I spent an hour on one cup. The cup came out crooked, but its shadow looks real.
city.do.exercise_bike.1: I rode three kilometres on the exercise bike and stayed where I was. Like in a dream.
city.do.exercise_bike.2: The counter's broken and always shows "12". I pedalled until twelve started to feel like a lot.
city.do.exercise_bike.3: The bike faces a window onto the sea. I imagined riding the promenade to the lighthouse, overtaking the bus.
city.do.exercise_bike.4: The pedals creak in waltz time. One-two-three, one-two-three. My legs got tired; the tune stayed.
city.do.eye_chart.1: E, F, P… T, O, Z… I read the bottom line by heart: it's the same in every clinic in the world.
city.do.eye_chart.2: I covered my left eye with the spoon. The right sees better, but the left seems to see something else.
city.do.eye_chart.3: "Twenty-twenty!" said the nurse. I was alarmed at first, then understood it was good.
city.do.eye_chart.4: The last line blurs and forms a word that isn't on the chart. I blinked, and everything was as it should be.
city.do.fortune.1: The mechanical fortune-teller nodded and gave me a card: "Soon you will be where you have already been."
city.do.fortune.2: The card: "Your sun is rising. Don't oversleep." In small print: "The machine accepts no responsibility."
city.do.fortune.3: The fortune-teller froze with her hand raised, thought, and gave me a blank card. Probably a good sign.
city.do.fortune.4: "The person you seek is seeking you too. Meet in the middle." The middle of what, it doesn't say.
city.do.fountain.1: The water's so cold my teeth ached. The jet squirts sideways, so I washed my face as well.
city.do.fountain.2: I drank and felt the water going down, as if someone had drawn a cool ruler through me.
city.do.fountain.3: The fountain tastes of iron and childhood. I don't know how I know what childhood tastes like.
city.do.fountain.4: A pigeon waited beside me while I drank. I stepped away and it didn't drink. Maybe it just wanted to stand there.
city.do.haircut.1: "How do you want it?" "However." "Short back and sides, then." Half an hour later I looked like a photo on a notice board.
city.do.haircut.2: The barber talked about fishing and never once looked at the scissors. It came out even. Nearly.
city.do.haircut.3: They sprayed me with cologne, and all evening I smell like someone's grandad at a party.
city.do.haircut.4: In the mirror facing the mirror I saw an endless corridor of me. In the furthest one I think I was smiling.
city.do.jukebox.1: I pressed B7 and A3 started playing. The machine knows best. A song about a gull who didn't come back.
city.do.jukebox.2: The record hisses like sea on shingle. A woman sings of a summer that "isn't over yet but is already remembered".
city.do.jukebox.3: I put on a foxtrot. Two old ladies by the window got up and went once round the floor, then sat down as if nothing had happened.
city.do.jukebox.4: The jukebox swallowed the coin and pondered. A minute later it played a march, loud and out of place.
city.do.lottery.1: I unrolled the ticket: "A postcard." No-lose means honest. A postcard of the lighthouse.
city.do.lottery.2: On the back of the winning ticket, handwritten: "And a little extra luck." They gave me no luck, just a postcard.
city.do.lottery.3: Three of us turned the ticket drum: me, the woman and the wind. Out came a postcard of the promenade.
city.do.lottery.4: "The top prize is a bicycle," the woman said. "Nobody's ever won it. Maybe it doesn't exist. Here's a postcard."
city.do.lottery.prompt: E — draw a no-lose lottery ticket
city.do.mats.1: Forward roll, backward roll. On the third the world slid a little, so I lay there until it came back.
city.do.mats.2: The mats smell of rubber, dust and other people's victories. Lying on them is nice and a little shameful.
city.do.mats.3: I tried a handstand. Held it a second, just long enough to see the hall upside down. I liked it.
city.do.mats.4: I did a cartwheel. Crooked as a squiggle, but a cartwheel. The mat sighed under me with all its foam.
city.do.microphone.1: "One, two, testing." My voice flew round the hall and came back someone else's, grown up.
city.do.microphone.2: The mic howled, and the cleaner in the doorway shook her mop at me. I pretended it was intentional.
city.do.microphone.3: I said "Hello" to the empty hall. The hall didn't answer, but it seemed to be listening.
city.do.microphone.4: I wanted to sing but only remembered the chorus. Sang the chorus. The echo sang it again, better.
city.do.microphone.prompt: E — say something into the microphone
city.do.misc.1: I fiddled with it, prodded it, broke nothing. A success already.
city.do.misc.2: I didn't work out how it works, but I looked very serious.
city.do.misc.3: Someone had left a note on it: "Don't touch. Touched. Broken." I didn't touch it.
city.do.payphone.1: I dialled a number at random. A woman answered, said "Hello, hello", fell silent and said softly: "Is that you?" I hung up.
city.do.payphone.2: I rang the speaking clock. "The time is exactly…" and the voice faltered. Then went on brightly.
city.do.payphone.3: Long rings in the receiver, and between them a faraway murmur, like in a seashell.
city.do.payphone.4: The phone ate the coin and didn't connect. I thumped it, the way everyone does. It returned my coin and someone else's.
city.do.photo_booth.1: Four flashes. In the first I'm blinking, in the second serious, in the third smiling, in the fourth I'm not there.
city.do.photo_booth.2: The photographer ducked under the black cloth and said "watch the birdie". A real sparrow flew out from under the roof.
city.do.photo_booth.3: The prints were ready in ten minutes. I look more like myself in them than in a mirror. They're going in my diary.
city.do.photo_booth.4: The photographer stood me against a painted sea. The real one was right outside, but the painted one, he says, comes out better.
city.do.photo_portrait.1: "Chin up a little. Don't blink. Think of something nice." Click. "Ready on Thursday."
city.do.photo_portrait.2: The photographer moves the lamp, then me, then the lamp again. In the picture I'll look as if I'd lived here for years.
city.do.photo_portrait.3: Behind me a pale blue backdrop, like the sky over a calm sea. "Smile, young man, this is a resort."
city.do.piano.1: I played "Chopsticks" with one finger. Behind a door someone joined in on a violin, in a different key.
city.do.piano.2: One key sticks and sounds like a cough. I played the whole tune so as to avoid it.
city.do.piano.3: I pressed three white keys in a row and got something like a sunrise. Couldn't do it again.
city.do.piano.4: The music on the stand says "play as if no one is listening". I did. And no one was.
city.do.pool.1: I swam four lengths of crawl and two of doggy paddle. The lifeguard whistled, approvingly I think.
city.do.pool.2: Underwater everything is green and echoing. I lay on the bottom and watched the light dance over the tiles in a net.
city.do.pool.3: It smells of chlorine and wet towels. I got out and my body felt heavy and happy.
city.do.pool.4: A granny in a flowery cap swam beside me and lapped me twice. She said she'd been swimming like that for fifty years.
city.do.potters_wheel.1: The clay spun and wriggled out of my hands like a live fish. It ended up an ashtray. I'd wanted a vase.
city.do.potters_wheel.2: The potter laid her hands over mine and the walls rose by themselves. "Like that. Don't press. Persuade."
city.do.potters_wheel.3: Clay up to my elbows. The little bowl is lopsided, but it's mine. They promised to fire it by Thursday.
city.do.potters_wheel.4: The wheel hums like a bumblebee, and to that hum I stopped thinking entirely. Very useful.
city.do.potters_wheel.prompt: E — sit at the potter's wheel
city.do.pump_room.1: I filled a bottle at the tap. The water smells of iron and a bit of egg. "Good for you," said a guest in a sun hat.
city.do.pump_room.2: In the pump room everyone sips from the spouts of china mugs and looks out of the window as if at a screen.
city.do.pump_room.3: A sign by the spring: "Temperature 12°. High mineral content. Drink slowly, think of good things."
city.do.pump_room.4: The water runs warm from the tap, as if it passed something hot underground. The sun, probably.
city.do.pump_room.prompt: E — fill a bottle with mineral water
city.do.punching_bag.1: The bag swung and came back, like a grudge. I hit it until it was just a bag.
city.do.punching_bag.2: An old coach showed me a one-two and said: "Punch as if you're knocking on a door you really need."
city.do.punching_bag.3: The gloves are too big and smell of other people's victories. The bag is old leather, all patches.
city.do.punching_bag.4: After ten minutes I was puffing like a steam engine, and inside it went quiet and empty, like a gym in the evening.
city.do.radio.1: "…wind north-westerly, five to seven metres a second, clear on the coast, fog in places in the mountains…" I'm fog in places too.
city.do.radio.2: Between stations I caught a rustling silence, as if someone very far away were breathing into a phone.
city.do.radio.3: A request show: "For Nina Petrovna on the third floor, from the neighbours who promise to stop drilling."
city.do.radio.4: The time signal: six short pips. Every clock in the room suddenly felt guilty.
city.do.radio_set.1: "CQ, CQ, this is Lyudmilovsk." Through the crackle someone in Tiksi answered: they have snow and are in good spirits.
city.do.radio_set.2: The meter needle trembles, the valves glow orange. The Morse in the headphones sounds like rain on a tin roof.
city.do.radio_set.3: On the wall, QSL cards from all over the world. One from a Japanese schoolboy: a mountain and a hundred signatures.
city.do.radio_set.4: I called for half an hour. Only the sea answered: an even hiss on every frequency at once.
city.do.record_player.1: I lowered the needle. Crackle first, then a violin, then crackle again, as if the music were coming through rain.
city.do.record_player.2: On the sleeve, an orchestra on a beach, all in tailcoats and barefoot.
city.do.record_player.3: The record stuck on one phrase: "…and the sun, and the sun, and the sun…" I didn't fix it.
city.do.record_player.4: A fairy-tale record. The narrator's voice is so kind I listened to the whole of "The Runaway Bun", though I know how it ends.
city.do.ring_toss.1: One ring landed on a bottle and slid straight off. The woman said: "I'll count it, you tried."
city.do.ring_toss.2: The rings are as light as pancakes and fly where they like. One went into the ice cream kiosk next door.
city.do.ring_toss.3: Three out of three! The prize was a paper flower. I tucked it in my breast pocket. It looks good there.
city.do.ring_toss.4: The boy next to me scored every time and dutifully gave the prizes to his little sister. I watched instead of throwing.
city.do.scales.1: The nurse slid the weight along and wrote down a number. "You're growing," she said. I didn't know I was.
city.do.scales.2: The scales showed the same as yesterday, though I wasn't here yesterday. The nurse wasn't surprised.
city.do.scales.3: I took my trainers off to make it fairer. Three hundred grams lighter, and one small worry less.
city.do.scales.4: Height and weight went into a card in beautiful handwriting. The card, it turned out, already had my name on it.
city.do.school_desk.1: Geography. The teacher pointed on the map to where we live, and there was only blue paint there.
city.do.school_desk.2: Literature: poems about autumn. The boy by the window read so well that it clouded over outside for a minute.
city.do.school_desk.3: Carved on the desk: "Whoever reads this is great." I read it. Astronomy, topic: "Our Sun". I listened without breathing.
city.do.school_desk.4: Nobody asked who I was. They gave me a squared exercise book and said: "Take notes, you'll be asked later."
city.do.school_desk.prompt: E — sit in on a lesson
city.do.sewing_machine.1: The machine chirred like a grasshopper. The seam went zigzag though I wanted straight. Zigzag is a style too.
city.do.sewing_machine.2: I sewed a sun-shaped patch on my jacket. The women in the circle said that's what's in this season.
city.do.sewing_machine.3: The thread snapped, the needle broke, and the machine, an old Seagull older than my mum, carried on as if nothing had happened.
city.do.sewing_machine.4: I learnt to thread a needle. On the twelfth try it worked, and I felt like a surgeon.
city.do.shooting_gallery.1: I knocked down the duck, the windmill and the bear. The bear played a tune as it fell. The man said it hadn't done that in ages.
city.do.shooting_gallery.2: The rifle pulls left. I aimed further right, and it took offence and started pulling right.
city.do.shooting_gallery.3: Five shots, no hits. But now I know exactly where their light bulb hangs.
city.do.shooting_gallery.4: I hit the little sun on the backdrop. It didn't fall, just swayed. The man went pale for some reason.
city.do.sink.1: The tap coughed first, then gave water as cold as a mountain stream. I washed my face and woke up a second time.
city.do.sink.2: A mountain of cups in the sink. I washed three and set them upside down. Someone will be surprised later.
city.do.sink.3: The water smells of iron and a little of the sea. Probably everything here smells a little of the sea.
city.do.sink.4: A sign above the sink: "Save water: there's little of it and many of us." I turned the tap tighter.
city.do.slide_projector.1: A filmstrip, "The Journey of a Droplet". It evaporated, became a cloud, fell as rain and went back to the sea. Happy ending.
city.do.slide_projector.2: A frame jammed and a surprised-looking owl hung on the wall for ages. Everyone laughed; the owl went on being surprised.
city.do.slide_projector.3: Slides from someone's trip north: a geyser, snow, tents, people in jumpers squinting at the sun.
city.do.slide_projector.4: Click, a new frame. Click, another. The projector hums warmly like a cat and smells of heated dust.
city.do.stage.1: They were rehearsing a play about fishermen. An actor in a pea coat forgot his lines, and the prompter whispered them to the whole hall.
city.do.stage.2: A conjurer pulled a pigeon from his hat, then another, then another. They settled on the chandelier and stayed.
city.do.stage.3: A children's troupe danced the sailors' hornpipe. The smallest sailor was always a beat behind and the best of them all.
city.do.stage.4: The stage is empty, one spotlight on. Somehow watching an empty stage is as interesting as a full one.
city.do.stove.1: The gas caught in a blue crown with a soft "pff". The kettle thought about it and began to hum.
city.do.stove.2: On the stove, a pan with painted words: "Kompot. Don't touch. This means you, Valera." I'm not Valera.
city.do.stove.3: The kettle whistled like a little steam engine, and everyone in the corridor turned round as if someone had arrived.
city.do.stove.4: I waited by the stove. My face was reflected in the oven window, warm and a little bit someone else's.
city.do.strongman.1: The needle crawled up to "Schoolboy". Fair enough. I am one.
city.do.strongman.2: I hit it so hard the bell at the top rang. Everyone turned. I turned too, to see who'd done it.
city.do.strongman.3: Missed. The mallet slipped, and the tester showed "Dreamer". There's no such mark on it, actually.
city.do.strongman.4: "Hero"! Well, nearly: "Nearly Hero". My palm stings, but the pride is stronger.
city.do.study_desk.1: In the exercise book, a problem about two trains heading towards each other. I decided they'd better just wave.
city.do.study_desk.2: The lamp warms the top of my head, the pen leaks, outside someone calls someone out to the yard. Not me.
city.do.study_desk.3: In the margin someone has drawn a little man running from the word "TEST". I drew him a bicycle.
city.do.study_desk.4: I learned four lines by heart. The fifth kept running off, like a cat called in for a bath.
city.do.table_football.1: I spun the rods so hard the goalie did a somersault. I let the goal in anyway.
city.do.table_football.2: One player has a chipped nose and always misses. I named him Senya and cheered for him.
city.do.table_football.3: Five–three! The boys round the table clapped as if it were a World Cup final.
city.do.table_football.4: The ball got stuck in a corner and the two of us shook the table for a minute. Best part of the game.
city.do.table_tennis.1: We played to eleven. The ball went under the radiator twice, and both times the cleaner fished it out with her mop.
city.do.table_tennis.2: My opponent served with so much spin the ball seemed to go back to him on its own. Lost, but learnt the stance.
city.do.table_tennis.3: Tock-tock-tock. In five minutes I forgot everything but the white ball. Better than sleep.
city.do.table_tennis.4: The net sagged, the bat was sticky and the ball had a dent. 11–9 to me. Not fair, but nice.
city.do.telescope.1: The coin clinked and the shutter opened. I saw a barge, on the barge a dog, and the dog looking very important.
city.do.telescope.2: I pointed the telescope at the horizon. Where the sea ends something glints: a wave or a window.
city.do.telescope.3: I found our lighthouse through it, then my own footprints on the sand, then my time ran out.
city.do.telescope.4: I looked north at the mountains. On one slope something is steaming, thin as a kettle in a faraway kitchen.
city.do.track.1: I ran on the roof, with the whole town and the whole sea below. It felt as if with a big enough run-up I could take off.
city.do.track.2: Three laps. At every bend the wind changed: at my back, in my face, from the side smelling of fried fish.
city.do.track.3: Painted on the track: starts, finishes and, for some reason, a little sun. I finished on the sun.
city.do.track.4: An old resident jogged beside me in tracksuit bottoms and said he'd run here since the building went up. He wasn't even out of breath.
city.do.track.prompt: E — run a lap of the roof track
city.do.tv.1: A wildlife programme was on. A pelican swallowed a fish and looked into the camera as if waiting for applause.
city.do.tv.2: The weather: "Sunny tomorrow. Sunny the day after. Beyond that we haven't looked yet."
city.do.tv.3: The set showed only snow, and the guests watched it anyway, swaying their heads as if it were the sea.
city.do.tv.4: A request concert was on. Someone from Lyudmilovsk asked for a song "for the one who'll come back". It was a song about summer.
city.do.vaulting_horse.1: I ran up, pushed off the springboard and landed sitting astride the horse, like a real rider. The horse didn't mind.
city.do.vaulting_horse.2: I cleared it! Landed on the mat, palms burning, and everything inside me ringing like the last bell of the day.
city.do.vaulting_horse.3: The leather on the horse is rubbed shiny in one spot: thousands of palms before mine pushed off right here.
city.do.vaulting_horse.4: The coach gave me a thumbs-up from across the hall. Or he was fixing his whistle. I decided it was the thumb.
city.do.wall_bars.1: I climbed right up to the ceiling. From there you can see a volleyball on top of the cupboard, lost about five years ago.
city.do.wall_bars.2: I hung and raised my legs in an L. My stomach protested, but my head cleared.
city.do.wall_bars.3: The rungs are smooth as river pebbles: so many hands have held them.
city.do.wall_bars.4: I hung upside down and the world turned over. It's not bad that way either, it turns out.
city.do.wall_bars.prompt: E — hang on the wall bars
city.do.washing_machine.1: Someone's socks circle in the round window like fish in a tank. The blue one keeps falling behind.
city.do.washing_machine.2: On the spin cycle the machine hops across the floor like a living thing. I held it with my hand and it calmed down.
city.do.washing_machine.3: A rota above the machines: "Mon: 2nd floor, Tue: 3rd…" For Sunday: "Whoever gets up first."
city.do.washing_machine.4: It smells of warm laundry and Lotus washing powder. I'd like to climb into the basket and sleep.
city.do.washing_machine.prompt: E — look into the washing machine
city.do.watch.1: I watched until I forgot I was watching. That only happens with the sea and fire.
city.do.watch.2: Nothing special happened, and that was good.
city.do.watch.3: Time went past me like a tram past an empty stop.
city.do.workbench.1: I planed a block of wood. The shavings curled like the hair of the girl on a postcard. Smells of pine and summer.
city.do.workbench.2: Got the nail in on the third try. The first two went into my thumb. The shop teacher said: "Happens. You'll remember now."
city.do.workbench.3: I made a nesting box. Crooked, but they say birds prefer them that way: cosier.
city.do.workbench.4: Carved into the bench: "Vitya was here, 1979." I thought about it and carved nothing.
city.door.any.1: Locked. Behind the door a tap is dripping.
city.door.any.2: The door won't give. Not today, probably.
city.door.gallery.1: The lift to the viewing gallery, 32 metres. A sign: "Ride: 40 seconds. View: free. Dizziness: at your own expense."
city.door.gallery.2: The GALLERY button is rubbed shiny, the floor buttons look new. Everyone here rides up to look at the sea.
city.door.gallery.3: The lift attendant knits on a stool by the doors. "It's windy up top. Hold on to your hat or it'll fly off to the lighthouse. It's happened."
city.door.roof.1: "Roof access. No unauthorised persons." The caretaker probably has the key.
city.door.roof.2: Wind and sunlight seep from under the door. Up there you must see the whole sea.
city.door.staff.1: "Staff only." Behind the door someone is laughing and clinking cups.
city.door.staff.2: A sign: "Knock before entering." I knocked. Nobody answered.
city.fest.cashier.1: The cashier in a paper crown: "Happy holiday! If I run out of coins, your change comes in sweets today."
city.fest.cinema.1: "Holiday screening: an old comedy, one ticket lets two in. Bring the person you laugh with."
city.fest.cinema.2: "December 31: a midnight screening of Carnival Night. No champagne inside. Tangerines are fine."
city.fest.cloakroom.1: "Happy holiday! Don't lose your tag: half the town's here today, and all the hats look the same."
city.fest.club.1: "Holiday today! No clubs, the choir sings on the square at seven. The chess tournament is postponed: the pieces are resting too."
city.fest.club.2: "Lantern night: we're gluing paper lanterns in the foyer from four. Glue and paper are ours, the candle is yours."
city.fest.counter.1: Happy holiday! We're open till the last customer today, and then everyone's off to the square.
city.fest.counter.2: The tangerines ran out this morning. Happy New Year all the same! Come early on the thirty-first.
city.fest.health.1: "On holidays the doctor on duty sees patients. Don't overeat, keep your ears away from the crackers and your eyes away from the sparklers."
city.fest.lost.1: "Found on the square after the holiday: three mittens, a little flag, a toy pipe and someone's brand-new hat. Ask at the kiosk."
city.fest.prices.1: Chalked at the top: "For the holiday, pies at the old price, free tea with any pie."
city.fest.prices.2: "Sea Festival: fresh herring straight from the boats, smoked by lunchtime. Queue from the lamppost."
city.fest.tickets.1: "No tickets left for the holiday concert, but the square is free to everyone, and you hear it better there anyway."
