city.lg.whistle.1: A brass whistle on a cord, worn to a shine. I blew very softly, just in case. Two gulls turned their heads anyway.
city.lg.whistle.2: A clear, very confident whistle. Somebody on the beach quickly pulled a foot out of the water, though it was not for him.
city.lg.whistle.3: The whistle sways quietly on its nail. No whistling at night: the sea is asleep and the tower guards its sleep.
city.look.birds.1: A poster, "Feed the birds!": a tit, a bullfinch, a nuthatch. Below: "Bird guide at the town library, feed on the first floor, Garden department."
city.look.birds.2: A chart, "What to offer": unsalted suet for tits, rowan for bullfinches, and for sparrows anything not nailed down.
city.look.birds.3: A photo: a grey-haired man in glasses holding a tiny bird on his palm, both very serious. Caption: "Ornithologist. Our town."
city.look.birds.4: How to make a feeder from a kefir carton, in six pictures. In the sixth a bird is already sitting there looking at you reproachfully: where's the food?
city.look.catalogue.1: I pulled out the catalogue drawer for S. Cards: "Steamers", "Sand", "Seabirds", "Sea, see also Memory".
city.look.catalogue.2: A handwritten card: "The book everyone's looking for. Shelf mark: none. Location: with whoever is reading it."
city.look.catalogue.3: In the drawer for S there are more cards on the sun than on anything else. The drawer won't shut properly.
city.look.catalogue.4: A card marked "On loan" has been in the catalogue for twenty years. To whom isn't written.
city.look.catalogue.5: The drawers smell of glue and wood. Run a finger along the cards and they rustle like dry grass in the northern meadows.
city.look.cinema.1: A poster: The Man Who Waited for the Lighthouse. Drama. A grey fisherman and a huge yellow beam that looks right at you.
city.look.cinema.2: "Children's show: The Hedgehog's Cable Car Adventure. Sundays at 11:00. Under sixes with a parent or a hedgehog."
city.look.cinema.3: The comedy "Unpaid Leave": on the poster a holidaymaker chases his flying hat across the whole town.
city.look.cinema.4: "Before the film, a science reel: 'The Sun Is Our Home'." Someone added underneath: "And we're the guests."
city.look.cinema.5: The week's programme: the same film every day. Under the table: "By popular demand."
city.look.club.1: "Amateur photography circle. Thursday, 18:00. Bring film and a good mood. Film is a must."
city.look.club.2: "Dances for the over… for anyone. Saturday, 19:00. Waltz, foxtrot, slow ones on request."
city.look.club.3: "Chess tournament. The winner gets a cup, the losers get tea. The tea's better, we've checked."
city.look.club.4: "The choir needs basses. No tenors, please: our tenors already sing for everyone."
city.look.club.5: "Lecture: 'Why do we love the sun?' Free entry. Questions from the floor welcome; answers not guaranteed."
city.look.exhibit.1: A plaque: "Anchor of the schooner Lyudmila, 18—. Found by divers in 19—. The schooner itself has never been found."
city.look.exhibit.2: "Model of the first cable car cabin, scale 1:10." Inside sits a tiny passenger with a newspaper.
city.look.exhibit.3: A case of amber. In one piece a mosquito is frozen, looking as if it's about to say something.
city.look.exhibit.4: "Sundial from the old Sun Square. The shadow tells the time to the nearest quarter hour, and mood."
city.look.exhibit.5: Trophies of the Surf sports society. The smallest is engraved: "For the will to win. Nearly won."
city.look.fair.1: "Wave Fair: carousel, shooting gallery, ice cream, a lottery where nobody loses. Fri–Sun, noon till dark." "Till dark" is underlined.
city.look.fair.2: A notice: "Found: a child's sandal, the right one. Left one, where are you?"
city.look.fair.3: A hand-painted poster: dancing under the canopy on Saturday night, "in any weather except a hurricane".
city.look.fair.4: Carousel rules: "Hold the horse's neck, not your neighbour. Feeling dizzy? See the ice-cream lady, she knows a cure."
city.look.garden.1: Seedlings on the table in sour-cream pots. Each is labelled: "Tomato, Ox Heart. Don't water on Tuesdays."
city.look.garden.2: Seed packets: asters, dill, "early radish". The pictures are so lovely the vegetable patch will be ashamed.
city.look.garden.3: The rubber plant in the tub has outlived three directors. It has its own sign: "Don't touch. Old-timer."
city.look.garden.4: A long-spouted watering can, a rake, a ball of twine. It smells of earth and of something about to grow.
city.look.health.1: A poster: "Wash your hands before meals!" The drawn boy washes them with such joy you'd think it was the sea.
city.look.health.2: "Sunbathing: no more than 20 minutes. The sun isn't going anywhere, but you'll burn."
city.look.health.3: "A holidaymaker's day": rise, exercises, breakfast, sea, lunch, quiet hour, sea, supper, sea, sleep.
city.look.health.4: A chart: "How to breathe sea air properly." In on a count of four, out on the count of a wave.
city.look.health.5: "Vaccinations on Wednesdays. Crying is permitted any day."
city.look.kids.1: In the window, a doll's house with a wall that opens. In the kitchen a doll is frying a button. Smells good, probably.
city.look.kids.2: A wind-up chick on the counter pecks at the glass. Its key is lost, so it pecks forever.
city.look.kids.3: A "Young Chemist" set, stickered "Temporarily not for sale" after the business with the neighbour's cat.
city.look.kids.4: A wooden rocking horse with a real mane. I'd have a go if nobody were looking. Somebody's looking.
city.look.local.1: Under the glass: "Lyudmilovsk 900 years" badges, shells saying "Greetings from the sea!" and a stone that looks like an admiral's head.
city.look.local.2: An old photo of the promenade: ladies with parasols, a boy with a hoop, and the same lighthouse, only younger.
city.look.local.3: A hand-drawn map of the town. In the north, at the edge: "Meadows. Beyond: the mountains' smoke." In the west: "Topi. Don't go."
city.look.local.4: A drop of amber with a gnat inside that didn't make it anywhere forty million years ago. It probably wanted to get to the sea too.
city.look.logbook.1: The lighthouse log: "02:10. Light normal. Fog. Heard a horn, answered." The handwriting is as even as the surf.
city.look.logbook.2: "Clear night. The freighter Akademik passed, blinked. Blinked back." And underneath: "I miss you."
city.look.logbook.3: Every page starts with the weather and ends with one word: "Shone." Thirty years in a row.
city.look.logbook.4: A pencilled entry: "An owl spent the night on the gallery. Flew north at dawn. Light normal." The owl got logged too.
city.look.lost.1: "Found: horn-rimmed glasses. Good eyesight. Ask at the cloakroom."
city.look.lost.2: "Lost: Barsik the cat, ginger, answers to a rustling bag. Finder gets eternal gratitude and pies."
city.look.lost.3: "Whoever took my striped deckchair from the beach, please bring it back: it remembers my back."
city.look.lost.4: "Found: a key on a blue ribbon. What it opens is unknown. Possibly something important."
city.look.lost.5: "Lost: the feeling that everything is still ahead. If found, keep it, you need it more." Unsigned.
city.look.medicine.1: The teaching skeleton in the corner is holding someone's forgotten mitten. Just in case, apparently.
city.look.medicine.2: A poster, "Structure of the ear". The ear is drawn so huge it seems to be eavesdropping right now.
city.look.medicine.3: Someone has put a sun hat on the skeleton. The nurse has been pretending not to notice for two weeks.
city.look.medicine.4: A chart, "The 206 bones of the human body". So far I've found about twenty on myself. The rest must be somewhere inside.
city.look.misc.1: Notices pasted one over another like layers of paint. The bottom one has gone the colour of tea.
city.look.misc.2: "Whoever found a blue umbrella: it means a lot to me. Ask for Tamara Ilyinichna."
city.look.misc.3: The drawing pins are all colours, and one is shaped like a little sun. Nobody seems to touch that one.
city.look.misc.4: I read everything, down to "Notices are kept for 10 days." This one's been up about ten years.
city.look.painting.1: A painting, "Morning on the Pier": fishermen, gulls, mist. In the corner a boy in a hood is looking not at the sea but straight at me.
city.look.painting.2: A still life: a watermelon, a knife, tea in a glass holder. The tea is painted so you can see it going cold.
city.look.painting.3: A huge panel: people reach their hands towards the sun, and the sun reaches back. The fingers almost touch.
city.look.painting.4: A watercolour, "The Northern Meadows". The grass is a single brushstroke, and it seems to sway in the wind right now.
city.look.painting.5: A portrait of a woman in blue. The label: "Unknown artist. Unknown sitter. Very familiar."
city.look.prices.1: "Apples 5 rub., corn 14, seeds 9. The seller's smile: free, but not always in stock."
city.look.prices.2: In chalk on a board: "Adyghe cheese. Fresh. Yesterday's is fresh too, just less so."
city.look.prices.3: "Check scales. Weigh your purchase!" Beside it, old scales with weights; one weight has a chipped edge.
city.look.prices.4: "Fish bought from the public from 6 to 9 a.m. Fish with stories, any time."
city.look.prices.5: Market rules: "Trading until 18:00. After 18:00, conversation only."
city.look.rules.1: "Library rules. 1: Keep quiet. 2: Especially in the capsules. 3: Whispering counts as quiet."
city.look.rules.2: "Books are lent for 14 days. Poetry for as long as you need."
city.look.rules.3: "Don't fold the corners of pages. That's what bookmarks, memory and the librarian are for."
city.look.rules.4: "A library card is issued on showing a passport or an honest face."
city.look.rules.5: "Taking books out of the reading room is forbidden. Taking thoughts out is encouraged."
city.look.store.1: Store directory: "Ground floor: grocery, confectionery, haberdashery, drinks. First floor: books, sports, garden, souvenirs. Second floor: none."
city.look.store.2: "Dear customers! First choose, then pay at the till, then collect. The order matters, as in life."
city.look.store.3: "The complaints and suggestions book is kept by the manager." Below, in small print: "There are more suggestions."
city.look.store.4: "Fresh bread delivered at 9:00 and 16:00. Pies when you're lucky."
city.look.store.5: A poster, "Summer Is Holiday Time!": a family with a rubber ring and a ball. The dad is very tanned and the mum very happy.
city.look.sun.1: The roof solarium: deckchairs, striped awnings and a sign: "Sunbathe no longer than 15 minutes. Our sun is strong."
city.look.sun.2: A sundial on the parapet. The shadow says almost the same as my watch. One of us is right.
city.look.sun.3: I squint into the sun. Through my eyelids everything is red and warm, like looking out from inside an orange.
city.look.sun.4: Someone has chalked a circle on the concrete: "Here the sun stands at noon on 22 June." I stood in the circle. Nothing happened. Yet.
city.look.timetable.1: "Bus No. 3: Promenade, School, Sanatorium. Every 20 minutes, or however it works out."
city.look.timetable.2: Cable car times: first cabin 6:00, last 23:40. Added underneath: "The last one is for those in no hurry to get home."
city.look.timetable.3: A week's tide table. Someone crossed out Thursday and wrote: "On Thursdays the sea rests."
city.look.timetable.4: The local train "to the Northern Meadows" leaves on Saturdays at 7:15. A dry blade of grass is pinned beside it.
city.look.timetable.5: Opening hours for the bathhouse, the post office and the lighthouse. For the lighthouse: "Always. Especially at night."
city.look.travel.1: A world map with pins: red for "been", blue for "want to". Three times as many blue. One is stuck right in the sea.
city.look.travel.2: A cable-car diagram. From our station a thin line is drawn north to the volcanoes, marked "someday".
city.look.travel.3: A sea chart with depths. The figures are tiny as poppy seeds. The deepest spot is circled and labelled: "Quiet."
city.look.travel.4: A route drawn in pencil: from the door to the sea, from the sea to the mountains, from the mountains "home, but another way".
city.look.view.1: The sea is striped today: turquoise by the shore, blue further out, nearly silver at the horizon.
city.look.view.2: Down below a tiny bus crawls along the promenade, and above it a cable car cabin, as if they were racing.
city.look.view.3: To the north, beyond the roofs, the mountains go blue, and on one summit lies a patch of snow. In summer. Strange and beautiful.
city.look.view.4: West of town the sand rolls away in waves to the edge of the world. Somehow I can't look that way for long.
city.look.view.5: The sun lies on the water in a path straight to me. Wherever I stand, the path turns to follow.
city.look.wallpaper.1: The school wall newspaper, "Young Lyudmilovian": class 7B on cleaning the beach and finding a message in a bottle. The note is in a foreign language.
city.look.wallpaper.2: "Our Top Pupils": the photos smile; one boy has his eyes shut. Underneath: "Blinked at the crucial moment."
city.look.wallpaper.3: A poem by a girl in 5A: "The sun sits down in the sea / as if in a warm bath. / Tomorrow it'll wake up early / with rosy cheeks."
city.look.wallpaper.4: A cartoon: the physics teacher as a pendulum. Caption: "Wavers, but holds on." They say the teacher liked it.
city.look.wallpaper.5: From the pupils' council: "Waste paper drive. The heaviest class gets a cake. Don't hand in encyclopaedias, it's a shame."
city.mk.butcher_deli.1: The sausage man slices a thin round to try and holds it out on the knife tip: "Tell me what you taste." I say: "Garlic." "Correct."
city.mk.butcher_deli.2: "Smoked since last night, ripe by morning. Sniff from a distance, then come closer."
city.mk.butcher_deli.3: "Cold it slices better, warm it tastes better. Choose: pretty or tasty."
city.mk.butcher_deli.4: "For Saturday we make three batches. Still not enough for Sunday."
city.mk.butcher_old.1: The butcher wipes his hands on his apron: "A cutlet for the boy? Joking. For the boy, advice: take what smells good to you."
city.mk.butcher_old.2: "Fresh, this morning. The mince will be gone by ten; don't say I didn't warn you."
city.mk.butcher_old.3: "We close at three. The leftovers go to the cats, and our cats are orderly, they know their queue."
city.mk.butcher_old.4: "Saturday, up to my neck in work. If you're not buying, step back a little, that's my elbow there."
city.mk.cat.1: The market cat eats from its bowl. The bowl goes down before the rows open: it was decided at the general meeting.
city.mk.cat.2: The cat sleeps on its crate, curled so tight you can't tell what is where. It doesn't flick an ear at the noise: it's on its lunch break.
city.mk.cat.3: The cat does its rounds. The fishwives nod to it, the butcher tosses a scrap. It takes not from everyone, only from those who show respect.
city.mk.cat.4: The crate is empty, the bowl empty and washed clean. The cat is on its night round. Somewhere it dreams of fish.
city.mk.cat.5: Painted on the bowl: "Market cat. Feed by the timetable, stroke by the cat's mood. The Board."
city.mk.cat.prompt: E — look at the market cat
city.mk.catch.1: On the ice: flounder, sprats and a dozen gobies. Fresh: clear eyes, red gills, tails that haven't given up yet.
city.mk.catch.2: The ice has thinned. Some of the fish went into the shade, some onto plates: "For fish soup."
city.mk.catch.3: The trays are empty, washed and turned over. On one a scrap of paper: "Tomorrow from six."
city.mk.catch.4: The last fish has a golden flank. Tag: "Not for sale. It's for a bet."
city.mk.catch.5: A note beside it: "Fish from townsfolk bought from six to nine. Beyond that, only stories." The anglers in the queue nod.
city.mk.complaints.1: The complaints book. First entry, in a child's hand: "I complain about an apple. It was sour and did not apologise."
city.mk.complaints.2: Below, the director's reply: "The apple apologises. Sourness is its character."
city.mk.complaints.3: "I complain about the cold in the fish row. The fish are happy and I'm not." Added: "The fish are happy. No claim stands."
city.mk.complaints.4: "Please put a bench in the shade." "Done." "Thank you, but now there's always somebody sitting in the shade."
city.mk.complaints.5: An unsigned entry: "No complaints. Just wanted to write." The director stamped it: "Accepted."
city.mk.complaints.6: "The pigeons ate my pie." Added: "And the director's pie. A commission is looking into it. The pigeons sit on the commission."
city.mk.complaints.7: The last page is blank except for one blot. The pen on its string swings like a pendulum, waiting for a new complaint.
city.mk.complaints.prompt: E — leaf through the complaints book
city.mk.control_scales.prompt: E — check a purchase on the control scales
city.mk.cscales.1: The control scales. You put your purchase on the left pan, weights on the right. It all matches to the gram. At the far end of the market someone sighs with relief.
city.mk.cscales.2: In the morning the scales are especially strict: the needle doesn't tremble, the pans don't sway. The director watches from the office over his glasses.
city.mk.cscales.3: By evening there's a queue at the scales: people checking sausage, honey and suspicions.
city.mk.cscales.4: On the box of weights: "100 g is a hundred grams. Not 'about', not 'by eye', not 'well, you understand'."
city.mk.cscales.5: One weight is brass, worn smooth. They say it's older than the market. It weighs what it should.
city.mk.day.jam.1: A new slip below: "Jam tasting: Friday, Saturday, Sunday, 11 to 4. The jury's table is by the entrance."
city.mk.day.mon.1: MONDAY. The meat row rests: a knife has a right to a day off too. Fish and vegetables are in.
city.mk.day.sat.1: MARKET BOARD. "SATURDAY: THE BIG MARKET! Every row open, tea till the last customer, the jam jury at full strength. Come with one bag, leave with two."
city.mk.day.sat.2: In chalk below: "On Saturdays even those who are 'on holiday' the rest of the week trade. Rule 14."
city.mk.day.sun.1: SUNDAY. The fish are off, the butcher is on, the rows are shorter, the pigeons are on duty. Tea till closing.
city.mk.day.week.1: WEEKDAYS. Rows from seven to six. Fish from six to two, meat from seven to three. Tea as long as the samovar's lit.
city.mk.day_board.prompt: E — read the market's day board
city.mk.fish_a.1: The fishwife lays a flounder on her palm and names the weight to the gram. The scales confirm it, a little late.
city.mk.fish_a.2: "This morning's catch, still cold from the sea. Don't sniff, listen: hear the ice rustle?"
city.mk.fish_a.3: "The ice is melting, the fish are hurrying home. Take some before they leave."
city.mk.fish_a.4: "Saturday, everyone in the queue is a neighbour. Ask about fish soup: every grandmother has her own recipe and every one is right."
city.mk.fish_a.5: "If you catch some yourself, bring it. I'll weigh it fairly and pay the market price. Just don't say where you got it: a fish mustn't know it was caught."
city.mk.fish_b.1: The smoker rearranges the fish on its rail. It smells of smoke, alder and a little of eternity.
city.mk.fish_b.2: "Smoked it overnight, it's drying off now. Come after lunch and it'll be just right."
city.mk.fish_b.3: "Hot-smoked for a snack, cold-smoked for a feast. What have you got today?"
city.mk.fish_b.4: "On Saturday the herring barrel is gone by noon. Want to, queue up early, I won't tell anyone."
city.mk.fish_b.5: "Catch a bream and I'll smoke it for free. But half is mine: that's for the smoke."
city.mk.grinder.1: A pedal grindstone. I press the pedal, the wheel wakes up and hums, water sprays out in a fan. Only real things make a sound like that.
city.mk.grinder.2: Today is sharpening day: names on the tags, neat edges on the knives. The oldest knife has been sharpened so often it's thinner than a memory.
city.mk.grinder.3: The grindstone is resting today. On the tag: "Knives and scissors sharpened Tuesdays and Fridays, 8 to 12. Leave the knife, come back in an hour."
city.mk.grinder.4: The pedal's rod gleams like the spokes of a bicycle that's ridden all the time.
city.mk.herbs.1: Mint, lemon balm, dill, basil. I rub a leaf between my fingers and the smell rises and settles on my shoulders.
city.mk.herbs.2: In the morning there's dew on the leaves. It smells of cold green.
city.mk.herbs.3: By midday the herbs have warmed and smell generous, like tea in a big pot.
city.mk.herbs.4: Toward evening the buckets of flowers are pushed against the wall. The smell stays, half across the market.
city.mk.herbs.5: On Saturdays asters and a bunch of cornflowers are added to the herbs. Someone is already bargaining: for the bunch and for a smile.
city.mk.jam_jars.1: The jury's table. Jars with ribbons and paper numbers: no. 7 sea buckthorn, red ribbon; no. 12 gooseberry and mint, blue; no. 19 "pine cones", green. Jar no. 23 has no tag and a hair ribbon tied round its neck.
city.mk.jam_jars.2: A jury note has appeared by the jars: "Spoons put away. Tasting at weekends, starting Friday, one spoon per person."
city.mk.jam_jars.3: The flies formed their own jury and sat on jar no. 12 until they were chased away. The flies' verdict was not announced.
city.mk.jam_jars.4: Jar no. 12 has gone half empty. Everyone says it's the mint. The mint isn't commenting.
city.mk.jam_jars.5: A notice in chalk on a bit of cardboard: "Jam tasting: Friday, Saturday and Sunday, 11 to 4. Spoons are here. Bring your own courage."
city.mk.jam_jars.6: The list of those who want jar no. 23 opened: the market director, against; the scales attendant, for; the honey seller abstained; the children, unanimously for. Decision: open it at the tasting.
city.mk.jam_jars.prompt: E — look over the jury's table
city.mk.jar.1: The unlabelled jar: 412 grams. The needle stands dead level, the attendant nods.
city.mk.jar.2: Today 412 grams. Same as yesterday. The attendant wrote it in her notebook and put a full stop without much joy.
city.mk.jar.3: 412. The market director taps the scales. The scales are honest. So is the jar.
city.mk.jar.4: 412. Only the needle trembles a little longer than usual, as if listening.
city.mk.jar.5: Something stirred under the lid. The attendant says: "That's not jam, that's evening." And writes in the notebook: "Evening, 412 g."
city.mk.jar.6: A note under the jar: "This is not jam. It's the summer nobody got round to eating. Come in August." No signature. The handwriting is round and familiar, but everyone in the market denies it.
city.mk.pigeons.1: The crumbs are in a paper bag by the bench: everyone feeds from it and the bag has no owner. The pigeons think the market was built for them and that people are good seasonal workers.
city.mk.pigeons.2: A handful of crumbs and the air gets noisy: pigeons swoop in from the roofs as if they'd waited all morning for the bell.
city.mk.pigeons.3: At midday the pigeons are lazy. They walk, like people in the market: importantly and past.
city.mk.pigeons.4: By evening only the most persistent are left. One pigeon has taken the bench and looks at me as if I owe it something.
city.mk.pigeons.5: On Saturday there are three times as many pigeons: they come from every district for the big market.
city.mk.pigeons.prompt: E — toss the pigeons some crumbs
city.mk.slate.bait.1: "Morning worms, fat ones. Maggots for the not-squeamish."
city.mk.slate.bait.2: "Hooks, floats, line. Free advice: fish bite on patience."
city.mk.slate.bait.3: Toward evening: "Leftover worms marked down. The evening bite is the best, believe me."
city.mk.slate.bait.4: Saturday: "Tomorrow's Sunday, everyone goes to the water. Worms handed out by the list."
city.mk.slate.birds.1: "Bird feed: suet for the tits, rowan for the bullfinches, whatever you give for the sparrows."
city.mk.slate.birds.2: "Hand-made birdhouses. No starlings have moved in yet; they're reading the terms."
city.mk.slate.birds.3: Toward evening: "The birds get tired and so does the seller. Take a handful of seed and sit on a bench."
city.mk.slate.birds.4: Saturday: "Mealworms are in. For the birds, not for you."
city.mk.slate.bread.1: "The bread is still warm. Hold on to it, it runs away."
city.mk.slate.bread.2: "Pies: cabbage, apple, and the one the baker won't name. Take the apple."
city.mk.slate.bread.3: In the evening: "Yesterday's bread is cheaper, and better with tea."
city.mk.slate.bread.4: Saturday: "A big round loaf to order. Two carry it, five eat it."
city.mk.slate.butcher.1: "Fresh meat, sharpened knives. Mince until ten, then 'come back tomorrow'."
city.mk.slate.butcher.2: "Home-made sausage. If it smells of garlic, it's the real thing."
city.mk.slate.butcher.3: The meat row closed at three. On the slate: "Tomorrow: mince for cutlets."
city.mk.slate.butcher.4: Saturday: "Sausage is ordered ahead: we know who'll come and aren't surprised."
city.mk.slate.dairy.1: "Morning kefir, straight from the ice. No sour cream yet: it's still thinking."
city.mk.slate.dairy.2: "Round cheese, braided cheese. One crumb to taste. We are counting."
city.mk.slate.dairy.3: In the evening: "Leftover milk marked down. Kefir, as everyone knows, will be better tomorrow."
city.mk.slate.dairy.4: Saturday: "Cheeses in from the farm beyond the forest. We all taste together, in a circle."
city.mk.slate.fish.1: "Flounder since morning. The sprats are yesterday's, but honestly labelled."
city.mk.slate.fish.2: "The ice is melting, the fish are hurrying home. Take yours now."
city.mk.slate.fish.3: The fish row closed at two. On the slate: "Tails for the cats, the rest till tomorrow."
city.mk.slate.fish.4: Saturday: "Not enough fresh catch for everyone. Join the queue the evening before."
city.mk.slate.fruit.1: Chalked: "Morning apples, crisp. Take them while they crunch; by lunch they're just apples."
city.mk.slate.fruit.2: "Apples, 5 roubles. Boiled corn. Ask how it was boiled and the seller will tell you. In detail."
city.mk.slate.fruit.3: After five a line is added: "Everything on the counter is marked down. Apples with a bruised cheek, half price."
city.mk.slate.fruit.4: Saturday: "Named-variety apples, with a sticker and a pedigree. Without the pedigree, cheaper."
city.mk.slate.sweets.1: "Boiled sweets in jars. In the morning: sweets for the brave."
city.mk.slate.sweets.2: "Chocolate 23, sweets 7, seeds 9. The seller insists seeds count as sweets."
city.mk.slate.sweets.3: In the evening: "Whatever's left in the jars: a rouble a handful. No more than a handful!"
city.mk.slate.sweets.4: Saturday: "The gingerbread tower. Whoever finishes it gets the next floor up."
city.mk.slate.veg.1: "Vegetables straight from the bed, still with soil. The soil is free."
city.mk.slate.veg.2: "Pumpkin cut to order. Weighed by eye, and we err in your favour."
city.mk.slate.veg.3: Toward evening: "Cabbage, with a discount for tiredness. The carrots aren't tired but they came down too."
city.mk.slate.veg.4: Saturday: "Cucumbers: shipped-in and ours. Ours are crookeder but more honest."
city.mk.tasting.1: Zoya's sea buckthorn. Sharp and bright, like a sun that was asked to be quieter and wasn't. First place well earned.
city.mk.tasting.2: Gooseberry and mint. First green, then cold. You want to stand there and breathe through your nose.
city.mk.tasting.3: "Pine cones", the separate category. Smells of forest and tastes of forest too. Bold, you can't deny.
city.mk.tasting.4: The honey seller's plum. Dark and thick. I don't want to give the spoon back, but it's taken from me.
city.mk.tasting.5: Jar no. 23. The jury opens it with ceremony and steps back. The taste: wind off the sea, the wet planks of a pier, somebody's distant voice. I smile and can't say why. The market director beside me does too.
city.mk.unlabeled_jar.prompt: E — look at the jar without a label
city.night.binoculars.1: At night the binoculars show little: black water, white crests and the buoys glowing green.
city.night.binoculars.2: Something dark drifts along the moon's path. A log, probably. Or a very calm seal.
city.night.binoculars.3: Far out a ship's lights are burning: red, green, white. As if it were looking out for someone too.
city.night.binoculars.4: On the empty beach someone sits right by the water, not moving. I lowered the binoculars: let them be.
city.night.telescope.1: The coin clinked and the eyepiece filled with stars. So many, as if someone had spilled salt on a black tablecloth.
city.night.telescope.2: I found the Moon. You can see the craters and one long bright streak, like a scratch on a record.
city.night.telescope.3: I aimed it at the sea. Dark, only a barge's light rocking, and the lighthouse sweeping its beam right across the glass.
city.night.telescope.4: To the north, over the mountains, something glows faintly red. Maybe the volcano isn't asleep. Maybe I imagined it.
city.night.telescope.5: A satellite! A steady dot crawling between the stars, not blinking. I followed it until my time ran out.
city.night.view.1: At night, from up here, the town is a handful of lights by dark water. A red lamp blinks on the boiler-house chimney.
city.night.view.2: The cable-car cabins hang dark; only the last one has a lit window. Someone in no hurry to get home.
city.night.view.3: The lighthouse turns its beam, and each time the beach steps out of the dark for a second, like a photograph.
city.night.view.4: So many stars over the sea that there's no horizon: where the water ends, the sky begins.
city.night.view.5: In the west, beyond the sands, something glows quietly in the dark. Not a town, not the moon. I looked that way for a long time.

city.ps.booth.am: Early on the booth is quiet. The assistant puts on the first record that comes to hand: someone sings about the sea as softly as one sings in an empty hall. It ends and I keep standing there.
city.ps.booth.any.1: The sleeves stand slanted in the crate like teeth in a smile. I chose by the cover: it had a lighthouse. It played one about a lighthouse. A coincidence, of course.
city.ps.booth.any.2: The booth is lined in blue and the voice from the speaker comes closer, as if the singer stood at my shoulder. I didn't turn round: what if he does.
city.ps.booth.eve: By evening the booth is warmer: the music has warmed the walls. Something lazy and jazzy plays. Beyond the glass people head home, and I somehow don't.
city.ps.booth.noon: After lunch the booth is crowded with other people's thoughts: someone's fingerprints on the sleeve. The needle settles into the groove, a waltz plays. I don't know it, yet somehow I remember it.
city.ps.chalk.fri.1: "FRIDAY IS FISH AND CHEESE DELIVERY. Buy at once or they'll say it's gone. The fish is at the grocery counter, the smell is everywhere."
city.ps.chalk.fri.2: Under it someone has chalked: "Cheese first, fish as you feel." The assistant leaves it up: she says it's good advice.
city.ps.chalk.mid: "WEDNESDAY AND THURSDAY are the quietest days. Choose in your own time; the shop assistants don't bite, and if they do, they do it politely."
city.ps.chalk.mon: In chalk on the board: "MONDAY IS STOCKTAKING. If you can't find it, it isn't missing, it's accounted for."
city.ps.chalk.sat: "SATURDAY — no delivery. We take what there is. What there is, see the shelves." Beside it, a smiling bottle of kefir is drawn.
city.ps.chalk.sun: "SUNDAY — no shop assistants, the till is open. Looking is allowed, bread is tomorrow." The lettering is clearly by the cashier: very even.
city.ps.chalk.tue.1: "TUESDAY IS THE DAIRY DELIVERY. The van arrives at ten. Queue starts here, along the red runner. Two per person."
city.ps.chalk.tue.2: Lower down, in another hand and smaller: "There is enough kefir for everyone who is standing. Don't fret. Kefir doesn't like the fretful."
city.ps.clothes.1: I flick through the hangers. Tags are sewn inside the collars: "46-3", "48-4", "50-2". Size and height, like a cipher only the assistant knows.
city.ps.clothes.2: No item has a price. The assistant explains: this is a showing, not a sale. "Touch, try, beauty has to be touched. But we won't take it away."
city.ps.clothes.3: A heavy woollen coat smells of wardrobes and mothballs. Next to it a pale rustling raincoat crackles: thin as wrapping paper, yet it keeps the rain out as well as the coat.
city.ps.clothes.4: A small child's raincoat hangs on the lowest bar, with a hood and a mushroom-shaped button. On the tag: "For those who grow faster than we sew."
city.ps.delivery.am.1: Crates of milk are stacked against the wall, the bottles clinking in their slots. A porter in an oilcloth apron counts aloud while the assistant checks it against a slip.
city.ps.delivery.am.2: The queue already stretches along the red runner, though nothing is out on the shelves yet. People look at the crates with respect, like at guests.
city.ps.delivery.pallet: Wooden pallets are stacked by the wall; they smell of damp planks and a little of milk.
city.ps.delivery.pm.1: The crates are empty; what's left are the slats and the smell of kefir. The porter has gone, leaving his apron folded neatly on a slat: back again tomorrow.
city.ps.delivery.quiet.1: The hand-truck by the wall stands idle. The crates on it are empty, but their sides still hold a coolness, as after winter.
city.ps.delivery.quiet.2: On the pallet in chalk: "Don't touch, it's not our day." The pallet obeys and touches nobody.
city.ps.fitting.1: I drew the curtain and was left alone with somebody else's coat. The sleeves are longer than my arms: it was clearly cut with room for future growth.
city.ps.fitting.2: From beyond the curtain: "Well, how is it?" "Fine!" I lied: I was wearing a scarf from a different outfit. The assistant tactfully didn't check.
city.ps.fitting.3: Hat askew, scarf wound three times. In the mirror somebody older looked at me. I smiled at him; he didn't smile back: an adult, after all.
city.ps.fitting.am: In the morning the fitting room smells of pressed cloth and dust. Nobody hurries you, and you want to keep the coat on a while longer.
city.ps.fitting.eve: In the evening, by the next curtain, two people argue whether blue suits. Somebody sighs and says: "It suits."
city.ps.fmirror.1: A narrow-framed mirror, a little cloudy in one corner. I stand in it down to the waist, and imagination paints the rest. Mine is generous.
city.ps.fmirror.2: Behind me in the mirror I can see the aisle, and in it an assistant with a tape measure on her shoulder. She nods at my reflection. I nodded too, not wanting to be rude.
city.ps.fmirror.3: On the frame in chalk: "The mirror doesn't flatter, but doesn't lie. Please don't confuse it with us." Seems the joke gets passed from hand to hand.
city.ps.hooks.am: The hooks are almost empty: it's early. One holds somebody's scarf left over from last night; the attendant pretends it isn't there.
city.ps.hooks.any: Over every hook there's a number. A coat and its token live in pairs, like the two halves of one ticket.
city.ps.hooks.day: Half the hooks are taken: coats, a rustling raincoat, a hat with a fur crown, and a child's jacket on the lowest hook so its owner can reach.
city.ps.hooks.eve: By evening the hooks are so full that coats hang two to a hook. The attendant flits along the row, tokens jingling on her wrist like sleigh bells.
city.ps.hooks.night: The empty hooks sway a little in the draught. The tokens are piled on the counter: every coat has gone home for the night.
city.ps.lost.b1: Behind the desk sits a woman with glasses on a chain; in front of her a form headed "Record of Found Property" and an ink pad. "What have you lost?" "Nothing." "Then do come in, only don't take anything. It's all somebody else's."
city.ps.lost.b2: "The bureau takes everything," she says. "Umbrellas, mittens, keys. Once we took an accordion. The accordion turned out to be a wedding one."
city.ps.lost.b3: "We keep things for a month. If nobody comes, we send them to the fair, for the lottery. Better they make somebody happy."
city.ps.lost.d1: "The yellow umbrella with the duck-head handle? Yes, we have it today. The night watchman found it in the records department last night, perched on the counter as if on a roost."
city.ps.lost.d10: "We've decided: the announcement will be made not by the announcer but by somebody younger. The microphone is over there on the desk. Press the button and tell her the umbrella has been found. But like a human being, not like we do it."
city.ps.lost.d4: "The owner came and took it. An hour later they brought it to me from the fabrics department. I'm not surprised any more, I just write a new record. We have plenty of forms."
city.ps.lost.d7: "She admitted she loses it on purpose. I said: 'Lidiya Sergeyevna, you can't do that.' She said: 'I know,' and asked that next time it be announced louder."
city.ps.lostshelf.1: A right-hand mitten, red with stripes. No left one. The tag: "Waiting for its pair until the fifteenth."
city.ps.lostshelf.2: Keys on a ring with a plastic fish. If the fish could talk, it would have said long ago what they open.
city.ps.lostshelf.3: An empty violin case. The tag: "No violin was found. The case was. Perhaps it has gone off to play by itself."
city.ps.lostshelf.4: Horn-rimmed glasses folded with the arms inside. The tag: "Probably it isn't them that is wanted but whoever will see them." I decided not to try them on.
city.ps.lostshelf.5: A photograph: two people laughing in front of a lighthouse. The tag: "Found under a display case. We will return it to whoever knows who they are."
city.ps.lostshelf.6: A seventh-grade algebra textbook with a bookmark at the problem about two trains. The tag: "If you're still travelling, come back, we know the answer."
city.ps.lostshelf.7: A single child's shoe, left, toe worn. Beside it a note: "The right one went ahead and hasn't come back yet."
city.ps.lostshelf.8: A knitted hat with a pompom. The tag: "The pompom was not lost. It has always been like that." So the pompom is the great arguer here.
city.ps.lostumb.base: In the stand by the lost and found: ten umbrellas, one torn, two for children, the rest somebody's. Each has a dated tag and no two dates are the same.
city.ps.lostumb.d1: The yellow umbrella with the duck isn't among them. They say it moves between departments by itself: here today, in fabrics tomorrow.
city.ps.lostumb.d5: One umbrella is furled especially neatly and tied with a ribbon: yellow, with a duck's head. On the tag four entries: "Issued. Returned. Issued. Returned." There's no room left on the tag.
city.ps.lostumb.d9: The tag on the yellow umbrella is new and clean. The old one, written over from edge to edge, lies beside it under a paper clip, for keeps.
city.ps.menu.am: On the board: "Breakfast: semolina porridge, tea, a cheese sandwich." The porridge comes with jam if you ask, and asking is allowed.
city.ps.menu.eve: "Tea and supper: pies, tea, ice cream." Ice cream is written last and underlined twice: somebody's hope.
city.ps.menu.night: The menu has been wiped half away: the cleaner left a single word, "tea". Nothing more is needed.
city.ps.menu.noon: "Lunch: soup of the day, cutlet with mash, compote." The soup of the day is the same as yesterday: "of the day" here is a concept, not a date.
city.ps.mic.1: I pressed the button and the lamp turned red. The loudspeaker overhead repeated my words a moment late, an echo: "...attention, customers... customers... customers..."
city.ps.mic.2: "A customer in a blue jacket found someone's mitten on the stairs. The mitten awaits its pair at the lost and found. Thank you." The assistant nodded approvingly: short and to the point.
city.ps.mic.d10: "Lidiya Sergeyevna! Your umbrella has been found! It is waiting for you at the lost and found. I repeat: your umbrella has been found. Come, it misses you." For a second everybody in the hall froze. Then somebody clapped.
city.ps.shoemirror.1: The low mirror is tilted to show only feet. New shoes look even newer in it, and my own seem to walk apart from me.
city.ps.shoemirror.2: I tried on one shoe. It fit like a glove. The assistant watches me walk up and down in just the one and nods: "Go on, walk. The shoe has to get used to you."
city.ps.shoemirror.3: In the mirror my socks don't match. I knew that, but the mirror couldn't have been politer: it showed them and kept quiet.
city.ps.shoemirror.4: Beside it on the mat stands a shoehorn as long as an oar. Somebody in the family must have had very narrow heels.
city.ps.staff.fri: "Friday. Fish and cheese delivery. Fish to take home only by an entry in the log. Cheese isn't logged: it's in plain sight anyway."
city.ps.staff.mon: A sheet held by drawing pins: "Monday. Meeting at 8:40 by the till. Whoever is late takes the minutes. The minutes are one line, no more."
city.ps.staff.sat: "Saturday is a short day. Cash handed in at 19:30, counters wiped, kefir put in the cold. Smile at customers until the last minute."
city.ps.staff.sun: "Sunday. Only the cashiers are on. To the shop assistants: nobody has cancelled watering the flowers on the windowsill."
city.ps.staff.thu: "Thursday. Wages at the till until 13:00. Sign legibly: signatures 'in the shape of a fir tree' will not be accepted."
city.ps.staff.tue: "Tuesday. Dairy delivery: porters at 9:30. Have the scales, two buckets and patience ready for the intake. Patience is issued by the manager, one per person."
city.ps.staff.umb: A fresh notice pinned over the old ones: "Umbrellas found in departments are to be taken to the lost and found. Do not let them go walking. Management."
city.ps.staff.wed: "Wednesday: sanitary day in the fabrics department. Do not be alarmed by the smell of mothballs. The mothballs are on duty and will not leave."
city.ps.tannoy.closing.1: "The store closes in an hour. We ask customers not to rush, but not to linger either."
city.ps.tannoy.lost.1: "Lost and found, upstairs: a mitten has been found, right hand, red with stripes. The left one, apparently, is still with you."
city.ps.tannoy.lunch.1: "Dear customers! The shoe department is closed for a fifteen-minute break. The shoes won't go anywhere, we'll keep an eye on them."
city.ps.tannoy.morning.1: "Attention! Flowered cotton has arrived in the fabrics department. Lengths are measured from the shoulder to the fingertips. The ruler is with the assistant, but each of us has our own conscience."
city.ps.tannoy.morning.2: "Hot pies are available in the café upstairs. The pies are waiting, but not for very long."
city.ps.tannoy.night.1: The loudspeaker is silent. Now and then it crackles, as if the store were listening to itself at night.
city.ps.tannoy.open.1: The loudspeaker clicks and a pleasant woman's voice greets the whole store: "Good morning, dear customers! The store is open. Happy shopping and a good day."
city.ps.tannoy.sat: "It's Saturday and the café upstairs has ice cream. Please don't leave ice cream in your pocket."
city.ps.tannoy.tue: "The dairy counter is receiving its delivery. Please don't worry: there is enough kefir for everyone in the queue, and even for those who are thinking of joining it."
city.ps.tannoy.umb1: "A request to the owner of the yellow umbrella with the duck-head handle: your umbrella was found in the records department and is waiting for you at the lost and found. It is waiting patiently."
city.ps.tannoy.umb2: The announcer reads slowly, as customers asked: "Lidiya Sergeyevna. Lidiya Sergeyevna. Your umbrella has been found. I repeat: Lidiya Sergeyevna, your umbrella has been found."
city.ps.tannoy.umb3: "The announcement is cancelled. The yellow umbrella with the duck-head handle has been returned to Lidiya Sergeyevna. The store thanks everyone who helped to search, and the umbrella too."
city.ps.toy_train.prompt: E — wind up the little train
city.ps.train.1: I turned the key on the little locomotive's side until the spring crackled. It ran round the loop, its wagons clinking, and never left the rails, though I hoped it would.
city.ps.train.2: The little train rolled on solemnly and stopped in front of a cardboard box marked "Station". The passengers must have been boarding. I nudged it with a finger: time to go.
city.ps.train.3: A boy stands frozen next to me, mouth open. He watches the train as if it were carrying him. I wound it once more and stepped away so as not to be in the way.
city.ps.train.4: A date is stamped under the little locomotive: before I was born. The spring still remembers how to run.
city.ps.type.1: I put in a sheet and typed: "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog." Every letter is there. I left the sheet in the carriage for the next customer.
city.ps.type.2: The carriage rang at the end of the line and I jumped: I'm used to keys being silent. The test sheet is full of names: "Vasya", "Masha", "We were here".
city.ps.type.3: One letter, the Russian "zh", sticks. The assistant says it isn't a fault but a character. A typewriter with character costs five roubles more.
city.ps.umbstand.base.1: In the stand by the cloakroom: three black umbrellas, one checked, and a walking stick with a rubber tip. Each has a token tied to the handle. All very orderly.
city.ps.umbstand.base.2: The cloakroom attendant says you can tell the weather from the umbrellas: if they stand dry, by evening you'll be borrowing one.
city.ps.umbstand.y1: Among the umbrellas there's a yellow one with a duck-head handle. A tag on the handle reads: "Found. Awaiting owner." The duck looks at me with dignity.
city.ps.umbstand.y2: The yellow umbrella isn't in the stand. On the hook beside it hangs an empty tag, and on it in pencil: "Gone on business."
city.ps.umbstand.y3: A note is pinned to the stand: "The yellow umbrella is at the lost and found, not here. It is busy: waiting for Lidiya Sergeyevna." Signed: the cloakroom attendant.
city.ps.umbstand.y4: The umbrella is back in the stand, wiped clean. Beside it a note: "For Lidiya Sergeyevna. Returned at noon over the radio. Please don't lose it until next Tuesday."
city.ps.window.am.1: Behind the glass a woman stands on a stepladder with pins in her mouth. She is dressing a dummy in a coat and keeps turning it until the folds fall right.
city.ps.window.am.2: A second dummy stands next to her, headless for now, waiting its turn. The window is half empty. The winter things have arrived, the autumn ones haven't been taken away yet.
city.ps.window.am.3: On the window floor, chalk footprints mark where each dummy's foot belongs. The woman checks them the way a dancer checks steps.
city.ps.window.day.1: The window is finished. The dummies, all in the same pose, look out over the passers-by at the square. A small card says modestly: "Display piece. Not for sale."
city.ps.window.day.2: On the inside of the glass chalk marks are left, showing where each foot goes. The dummies' shoes cover them now.
city.ps.window.day.3: One coat is pinned at the back: perfect from the front, a gamble from behind. The window is honest from one side only.
city.ps.window.night.1: The window glows alone. The dummies gaze at the empty square as if they too had something to think over at night.
city.ps.window.night.2: The lamp in the window flickers a little. In that light the dummy's coat looks blue, then grey. In the morning it will be dressed all over again.
city.ps.window.umb: The dummy in the blue coat holds a yellow umbrella with what looks like a duck-head handle. Up close I read the tag: "Duplicate. In case the original goes off to the toy department again."
city.pu.pu_bakery_chat.1: "Still warm. You have to take bread while it breathes: in an hour it's just bread."
city.pu.pu_bakery_chat.2: "The rye is Lyuba's doing, not mine. The starter is seventeen years old, older than the two of us and cleverer."
city.pu.pu_bakery_chat.3: "By evening it's buns that are left. Take some: in the morning they're better than they looked in the evening."
city.pu.pu_bakery_chat.4: "On Sundays the baker's off, so it's yesterday's bread. But yesterday's bread is still bread. And the toast is better."
city.pu.pu_bakery_chat.5: "A jam bun is the most honest food in the world: what you see is what you get, plus a bit sticky."
city.pu.pu_bakery_dough.1: The dough is springy and a little alive. You press and it answers. Flour sticks to hands, sleeves, and the nose I scratched for no reason.
city.pu.pu_bakery_dough.2: The baker looked in, shrugged and showed me how to fold. I folded, and the dough visibly became kinder.
city.pu.pu_bakery_dough.3: I made one crooked loaf. They didn't give it to me ("for order's sake") but set it in the common row. I don't know why that pleases me so.
city.pu.pu_bakery_oven.1: The brick oven breathes heat from a distance. From its door comes a smell that makes the stomach cheerful.
city.pu.pu_bakery_oven.2: The oven is cooling, but the bricks remember the morning. Hold a palm near it and you feel a warm breeze.
city.pu.pu_bakery_today.1: On the sandwich board by the door: "The starter woke at 4:10. First tray at 5:00, rye at 7:00. Poppy buns by nine, if the poppy seeds don't fly off."
city.pu.pu_bakery_today.2: In chalk: "Yesterday the starter was fussy. The baker talked to it for half an hour. It helped. The bread is cheerful today."
city.pu.pu_bakery_today.3: In chalk: "Order: a name-day pie, Thursday. Volunteers needed to roll the dough. Paid in buns."
city.pu.pu_bakery_today.4: In chalk: "The pie is baked! Thanks to those who rolled. The leftover dough goes to the children. Volunteers: come in, the table's free."
city.pu.pu_barber_bottles.1: On the shelf under the mirror stand flasks: Shipr, Troinoi, Neptune. I opened the Shipr and at once remembered a grandfather's razor, though I have none.
city.pu.pu_barber_bottles.2: Beside it a glass of combs, each in its own pocket. The most worn is labelled: "For the management."
city.pu.pu_barber_newspapers.1: Newspapers on the table, with rings of cups on them. The local news page: "The cable car stopped for five minutes; everybody looked at the sea." The barber adds: "Best five minutes of the year."
city.pu.pu_barber_newspapers.2: News: "The bakery has a new sign. The bread is painted a little too rosy. The baker is pleased." The barber: "The bread is said to be offended."
city.pu.pu_barber_newspapers.3: News: "The photo studio has put up a new portrait of the newcomer boy." The barber, without turning: "And his haircut could go straight to an exhibition, if you take my meaning."
city.pu.pu_barber_radio.1: The radio on the shelf softly airs the morning exercise show. The barber hums along with the brisk announcer without lowering his scissors.
city.pu.pu_barber_radio.2: A request concert is on. The announcer reads: "For the girl on the promenade, who knows this is for her." The barber nods as if he knows her.
city.pu.pu_barber_radio.3: A football commentary riding on a wave of hiss. The barber argues with the announcer in a whisper so as not to spoil a customer's haircut.
city.pu.pu_barber_sink.1: The tap hisses and gives a thin warm stream as if reluctantly. The basin is white-flecked with soap, and a forgotten comb lies on the edge.
city.pu.pu_barber_strop.1: A leather razor strop, worn shiny in the middle. It smells of leather and a little of soap.
city.pu.pu_barber_strop.2: The barber shows how to strop: away from you, smoothly, blade trailing. "Don't hurry. A razor likes not to be rushed." I drew an empty finger along it, felt nothing, but it felt good.
city.pu.pu_beer_chat.1: "We open at two, and at two sharp somebody's already waiting. The ones who just need to sit."
city.pu.pu_beer_chat.2: "Evening is league hour. Darts on Tuesdays, dominoes on Thursdays, everybody lies about fish on Fridays. I take notes."
city.pu.pu_beer_chat.3: "After ten it's quieter. I set mugs down softly, the radio lower. Boys after nine get only soda; not my rule, but reasonable."
city.pu.pu_beer_chat.4: "Friday: everybody who held out all day is here now. Look for a free barrel; they're not always where they stood."
city.pu.pu_beer_chat.5: "I've got a rule here: a mug must have time to sweat before it's finished. So take your time, lad."
city.pu.pu_beer_league.1: In chalk on the blackboard: "Darts league. Tuesday: Beer Bar v. Fish Shop. Score 3:2 to us. The fishermen demand a recheck: the bartender threw."
city.pu.pu_beer_league.2: In chalk: "Wednesday: the recheck. Everybody threw except the bartender. Score 3:3. The bartender pretends that's what he wanted."
city.pu.pu_beer_league.3: In chalk: "Thursday, the final. Saturday: the return match at the fish shop; the target there is cardboard, but honest."
city.pu.pu_beer_league.4: In big chalk letters: "The final is played. Friendship won, and one fisherman's bullseye. Lads may fetch the ball: there's table football in the corner, go on!"
city.pu.pu_beer_radio.1: The radio airs the five o'clock news: "Weather at the sea unchanged. Wind south-westerly." The bartender nods as if it were his doing.
city.pu.pu_beer_radio.2: A football commentary! Everyone has turned to the radio like flowers to the sun. "Goal!" and five mugs clink at once.
city.pu.pu_beer_radio.3: Quiet music with a gentle hiss: someone hums along without knowing the words.
city.pu.pu_beer_taps.1: Chalk labels over the taps: Zhigulevskoye, Rizhskoye, Martovskoye, Kvass. Kvass is underlined twice: "For those at the helm of a boat."
city.pu.pu_beer_taps.2: On the Friday label an addition: "Fresh barrel! Poured with exactly two fingers of foam." The foam is measured by the bartender's finger, not the customer's.
city.pu.pu_beer_taps.3: Label "Weekend range": beer, beer and a little beer. Kvass, just in case somebody wants variety.
city.pu.pu_books_board.1: A notice: "Looking for The Mysterious Island. Blue, no cover, with a pencilled 'it will all work out' on the endpaper. A tea and gratitude for whoever returns it."
city.pu.pu_books_board.2: Under it, a new one: "Saw a blue book at the baker's: it props open the pantry door. I report as a citizen."
city.pu.pu_books_board.3: A third notice: "The book has been returned. The baker apologised and left a bookmark: a cable-car ticket. Thanks, all. Tea is on the table."
city.pu.pu_books_board.4: New: "The second-hand dealer arrives Saturday. If you need a book about the sea, birds or stars, write down the title. We'll look in the box."
city.pu.pu_books_chair.1: The armchair is cosy as a boat without oars. The lamp's green light lies on the page and the words become calmer.
city.pu.pu_books_chair.2: Towards evening someone has left a plaid on the chair. I didn't ask whose. I wrapped myself up and listened to others turning pages.
city.pu.pu_books_chat.1: "It's quiet here in the morning. Readers wake later than books. Read what you see; we'll sort out what you've bought afterwards."
city.pu.pu_books_chat.2: "After lunch people come for detectives and leave with poetry. Or the other way round; I don't know which is worse."
city.pu.pu_books_chat.3: "By evening the light is green from the lamp and someone's already asleep over a page in the chair. Don't wake him; it's the best review."
city.pu.pu_books_chat.4: "Saturdays a second-hand dealer comes from the city with a box. I look first, you look second. But you can come earlier."
city.pu.pu_books_chat.5: "If you find something good, leave a bookmark: a ribbon, a ticket, a letter. The next reader will know the book was loved."
city.pu.pu_books_globe.1: A globe on a tall stand. Pencilled on it: "N. lived here" and a cross by the sea. N. isn't named. I don't ask.
city.pu.pu_books_globe.2: I turned the globe: where the map is blank, a small fish is drawn. Someone decided there's no such thing as empty.
city.pu.pu_books_mags.1: Magazines on the shelf: Science and Life, Around the World, Young Naturalist. One is open at an article "How a Gull Is Built"; the page is thumbed to softness.
city.pu.pu_books_mags.2: A stamp with a distant island is tucked in Around the World as a bookmark. I study the island longer than the article.
city.pu.pu_cafe_chat.1: "Good morning. I'm making coffee in a pot for now, the old way: the Leningrad machine is at the repair shop. The foam is the real thing, though."
city.pu.pu_cafe_chat.2: "Lunch? Pies and tea. Tea, by the way, never breaks down."
city.pu.pu_cafe_chat.3: "By evening the sea turns pink; you can watch it from right here. We don't charge for the window."
city.pu.pu_cafe_chat.4: "Weekends are packed, and there are still only four chairs by the window. Sit down before they're gone."
city.pu.pu_cafe_chat.5: "Monday. The gulls are resting, and so am I. Nearly."
city.pu.pu_cafe_chat.6: "Foam is just patience. Don't rush the coffee and it will tell you everything."
city.pu.pu_cafe_papers.1: A binder of the Lyudmilovsk Evening News: in the "Fish Tuesday" column the flounder won again.
city.pu.pu_cafe_papers.2: The Sunday paper: a crossword. Eight down, "Sea bird, five letters." Pencilled in: "gull." Correct.
city.pu.pu_cafe_papers.3: A binder of local papers. Weather on the back, ads in the middle, the horoscope at the bottom: "Today you will be offered a cup of something hot."
city.pu.pu_cafe_papers.4: Someone underlined an ad: "I take in knitting, I give back warmth." Beside it, scribbled: "Call!"
city.pu.pu_cafe_specials.1: In chalk on the board: "Today, coffee from the pot. The Leningrad machine is ill; the repair shop has promised to look into it."
city.pu.pu_cafe_specials.2: In chalk: "Pot coffee again today. Please don't rush us or knock on the counter; we're sad enough."
city.pu.pu_cafe_specials.3: In chalk: "They are hunting the whole coast for a valve for the Leningrad. If you've seen a valve, tell the barista."
city.pu.pu_cafe_specials.4: In chalk: "The valve is found! At the fish shop, from an old paraffin stove. The machine comes back tomorrow."
city.pu.pu_cafe_specials.5: In big chalk letters: "LAUNCH! The first cup from the Leningrad goes to whoever comes and asks."
city.pu.pu_cafe_stool.1: From the stool you can see the barista whip the foam and quietly taste it. I won't tell.
city.pu.pu_cafe_stool.2: Towards evening the ones who don't feel like going home yet gather at the bar. The talk is quiet, and so are the cups.
city.pu.pu_cafe_stool.3: The clock ticks quietly. It smells of coffee and the damp wood of the sill.
city.pu.pu_cafe_window.1: Waves roll right up to the wall. One gull bobs on them and acts as if it were all planned.
city.pu.pu_cafe_window.2: By day you can see bathers and boats from the window. Someone waves, probably not at me.
city.pu.pu_cafe_window.3: The sunset has tinted the glass pink. The cups on the sill have gone pink too.
city.pu.pu_cafe_window.4: Beyond the window, the dark sea and the lighthouse's spark. The darker outside, the cosier in here.
city.pu.pu_deckchair.1: The canvas deckchair gives and takes my shape. Beyond the wall you can hear the waves sorting pebbles.
city.pu.pu_deckchair.2: The sun has moved and the deckchair's shadow has slid right. I shift the chair after it. All clever people do.
city.pu.pu_deckchair.3: The chair creaks in the same spot. If you lie quite still, the creak becomes part of the song.
city.pu.pu_deckchair_2.1: This striped deckchair stands closer to the window. From here you see sandalled feet walking by, and not one face.
city.pu.pu_deckchair_2.2: A boy outside presses his nose to the glass, looks at me and sticks out his tongue. I do the same. We're even.
city.pu.pu_dumpling_chat.1: "We shape them in the morning. While you sleep we're up to our elbows in flour. Come after eleven; everything will be hot."
city.pu.pu_dumpling_chat.2: "Lunch hour: plates in hand and don't be shy. Everyone here is one of us, even first-timers."
city.pu.pu_dumpling_chat.3: "Evenings are quieter: people from work finish off the dumplings. I like this hour; steam from the pots clouds the window."
city.pu.pu_dumpling_chat.4: "On Sundays I put in a thirteenth. Don't tell the pasty bar; they'd take it the wrong way."
city.pu.pu_dumpling_chat.5: "Twelve to a portion. I count every one. Not because I'm stingy, but because there must be order."
city.pu.pu_dumpling_pot.1: Dumplings float in the big pot. They rise one by one like small pillows. When the last one has risen, it's time.
city.pu.pu_dumpling_pot.2: Warm steam over the pot, smelling of bay leaf and pepper. I stand there like a fool, smiling. That seems to be the point.
city.pu.pu_dumpling_rules.1: Self-service rules on cardboard: "1. Take your own tray. 2. Bread is free, but not the whole loaf. 3. Return the trays. 4. Don't take the plates home; there's one set for everyone."
city.pu.pu_dumpling_rules.2: Beneath, in a different hand: "5. Thank you is also a payment. 6. Smiling isn't compulsory, but advisable."
city.pu.pu_dumpling_today.1: In chalk on the board: "Dumplings, 12 pieces. With sour cream, 12 pieces and sour cream. The argument with the pasty bar over "three chebureks" continues."
city.pu.pu_dumpling_today.2: In chalk: "Yesterday the pasty bar said our portion is smaller. We counted. Not smaller. Counted again. Still not smaller."
city.pu.pu_dumpling_today.3: In chalk: "Peace proposal: two dumplings for one pasty, exchange through the window. Negotiations under way."
city.pu.pu_dumpling_today.4: In chalk: "The exchange has taken place. The pasty turned out tasty. The dumpling, they say, too. Both sides satisfied. Tea on the house."
city.pu.pu_fish_chat.1: "Morning fish is the most honest: it hasn't had time to lie yet. Take it while it still smells of the sea."
city.pu.pu_fish_chat.2: "A bit dry? Happens. By noon what's left is what the fishermen couldn't hide from their wives."
city.pu.pu_fish_chat.3: "Saturday is fish-soup day. Want soup? Take some ruffe and don't ask whose they are."
city.pu.pu_fish_chat.4: "Bait? Worm for flounder, shrimp for everything else. Cheap, and worth a hundred times the price."
city.pu.pu_fish_chat.5: "Off to the pier with a rod? Remember: fish bite on silence, not bait. The bait is just for manners."
city.pu.pu_fish_knots.1: Scraps of rope are pinned to the board, each with a knot and a label: fisherman's, bowline, clove hitch, sheet bend. I touched them. The knots are real.
city.pu.pu_fish_knots.2: Under the longest piece, a note: "A knot that holds needn't be pretty. A knot that's pretty must hold."
city.pu.pu_fish_knots.3: One knot hangs with no label, pulled impossibly tight. Somebody must have argued with a fish and lost.
city.pu.pu_fish_rods.1: Rods in the rack: bamboo, fibreglass, and one sea rod as thick as my wrist. The tag on the sea rod: "Not for beginners. Nor for the modest."
city.pu.pu_fish_rods.2: The reel is wound with line the colour of water. While you look it seems not to be there at all; that must be the idea.
city.pu.pu_fish_scale.1: The hanging steelyard swings and settles. The needle says "a little less than you'd have liked"; that's what it says to all customers.
city.pu.pu_fish_scale.2: I put my palm on the pan. The needle didn't stir: a hand apparently weighs nothing.
city.pu.pu_fish_tides.1: A framed tide table. Below it, in chalk: "No herring. Waiting." Three earlier "waiting"s are crossed out and written again.
city.pu.pu_fish_tides.2: In chalk under the table: "A shoal seen off the Far Buoy. Eino says it's fry. Eino is rarely wrong."
city.pu.pu_fish_tides.3: In chalk: "Gulls flying low over the water. Herring at Grey Rock, at the pier by evening. Get your buckets ready."
city.pu.pu_fish_tides.4: In chalk, in a shaky hand: "HERRING! Three crates. Fresh until lunch!"
city.pu.pu_fish_tides.5: In chalk: "Eino has left a little bait at the bottom of a crate for those who know how to wait. Ask at the counter."
city.pu.pu_pasty_chat.1: "From ten. The first chebureks are the crispiest because they don't yet know they're being eaten. Take them before they find out."
city.pu.pu_pasty_chat.2: "Lunch hour: our queue is special, everybody pretends not to be hungry and then takes two."
city.pu.pu_pasty_chat.3: "By evening the oil is in character. Evening chebureks aren't worse, just calmer."
city.pu.pu_pasty_chat.4: "On Sundays I serve with vinegar and red pepper. Those who are afraid, take tea with it. Those who aren't, take tea as well."
city.pu.pu_pasty_chat.5: "A cheburek is a little pie that once decided to grow big. Don't stop it: let it crunch."
city.pu.pu_pasty_fryer.1: Oil boils in the cauldron. A cheburek creeps slowly to the edge, flips and turns golden with bubbles. It's beautiful, like a little eruption.
city.pu.pu_pasty_fryer.2: The cook lifts out a cheburek with a skimmer, shakes it and lays it on a napkin. The napkin turns see-through at once. "Don't touch, you'll burn," he says. I touched only with my eyes.
city.pu.pu_pasty_table.1: On the tall table stand a salt cellar, a bottle of vinegar and a stack of paper napkins. One napkin corner is pencilled: "I was here, it was delicious."
city.pu.pu_pasty_table.2: The vinegar on the table is the real kind, dark, in a lemonade bottle. Somebody has carefully labelled it: "Careful: vinegar."
city.pu.pu_pasty_today.1: The board by the door: "Crimean-style chebureks, 16 kopecks. Pepper on request. We make no comment on the dumpling bar's "twelve"."
city.pu.pu_pasty_today.2: In chalk: "We were told: 'three chebureks is a portion.' We agree: a portion of chebureks is three. Of dumplings, however they count."
city.pu.pu_pasty_today.3: In chalk: "Exchange proposal received. Considering. Dumplings for tasting, cheburek for tasting. Talks over tea."
city.pu.pu_pasty_today.4: In chalk: "The exchange has taken place. The dumplings turned out good. Quietly admitted. Chebureks go out the window while hot. Thanks, neighbours."
city.pu.pu_photo_camera.1: Under the black cloth, on the ground glass, the whole studio upside down. The lamp stands on the floor and the ceiling is underfoot. You get used to it.
city.pu.pu_photo_camera.2: Aim it at the door and the glass shows the sea and people walking upside down and still hurrying somewhere.
city.pu.pu_photo_camera.prompt: E — look into the ground glass
city.pu.pu_photo_negatives.1: A drawer of negatives. The envelopes are labelled: "Fishermen", "Roofs", "Children at the fountain", "Unidentified". "Unidentified" is the thickest.
city.pu.pu_photo_negatives.2: I held a negative to the light: white is black, black is white, and the person in it laughs just the same. Laughter doesn't invert.
city.pu.pu_photo_negatives.3: In the "Unidentified" envelope the last frame: an empty promenade at dawn. Caption: "Taken to remember that nobody was here and it was good."
city.pu.pu_photo_props.1: On the stand, costumes for shoots: a captain's cap, a veiled hat, a sailor's striped vest. A tag on the cap: "Take care; it has already been to sea once."
city.pu.pu_photo_props.2: In the raincoat pocket a note: "Don't want to, don't put it on. Do want to, still don't put it on, but hold it." I held it. The coat is heavy and honest.
city.pu.pu_photo_samples.1: The wall of samples. A new picture in the corner: "Fishermen on the pier, 1957." Everyone looks at the camera and nobody smiles except the dog.
city.pu.pu_photo_samples.2: A new picture: "The first cable car, a test run." Two people stand rigid in the cabin as if for a portrait; they're afraid.
city.pu.pu_photo_samples.3: A new picture: "A wedding on the promenade. The wind took the veil; in the second take the groom holds it." The photographer has captioned: "Take two, the most honest."
city.pu.pu_photo_samples.4: A new picture pinned over the others, still damp at the edges: a boy in a jacket looks at the camera closely, as if he wants to ask something. Caption: "Newcomer. Stayed."
city.pu.pu_rental_bikes.1: The bicycles stand in a row: red frames, blue, green, and a yellow one. A paper on the yellow one's carrier says: "For those who hurry slowly."
city.pu.pu_rental_bikes.2: A tag with a number and a price is tied to each handlebar. On the red one, added: "The bell is louder than it looks."
city.pu.pu_rental_bikes.3: There's sand on the tyres: someone has already ridden along the beach. The owner doesn't scold; he says it's the best advertising.
city.pu.pu_rental_boats.1: A school blackboard with the boat schedule: No. 1 Seagull, running. No. 2 Neptune, running. No. 3 drying on the shore. No. 4 Swallow, at the repair shop being painted.
city.pu.pu_rental_boats.2: A note in chalk: "Swallow is being painted blue with a white stripe. Don't touch with a finger: it's drying. There have been cases."
city.pu.pu_rental_boats.3: Swallow is back on the water! A trial circuit done; she leaks through only one crack, but romantically.
city.pu.pu_rental_boats.4: Notice: "Saturday at 4 p.m., the Race to the Buoy (rowing, in pairs). Prize: the warmest tea on the whole coast. Sign up at the counter."
city.pu.pu_rental_boats.5: The sign-up list: the baker and the souvenir seller, two fishermen, one stranger in a raincoat. The last line is empty. "There's room for you," someone has added.
city.pu.pu_rental_chat.1: "Morning is for bicycles. Brakes checked, bell rings, the chain only grumbles a little. A rouble an hour, and thirty kopecks extra for the wind in your face."
city.pu.pu_rental_chat.2: "Afternoons are for boats. Oars go out by number and come back in order. Number seven is missing; don't ask."
city.pu.pu_rental_chat.3: "Deckchairs till six. After six I fold them, and you watch the sunset standing, like people from the past."
city.pu.pu_rental_chat.4: "Saturday is the Race to the Buoy. I sign people up in pairs. No singles: they row in circles."
city.pu.pu_rental_chat.5: "Today is the Race to the Buoy. Those with a partner, onto the water. Those without, onto a deckchair to cheer."
city.pu.pu_rental_chat.6: "The deposit's a passport. No passport? Then your word of honour. No word either? Then at least a smile."
city.pu.pu_rental_keys.1: A plywood board of hooks and numbers. Lock keys hang on the hooks, and on one, a little plush fish too. That's the key to Swallow; she likes to be treated gently.
city.pu.pu_rental_keys.2: A receipt is pinned nearby: "Left in storage: one umbrella, one left shoe, one notebook. Come and collect."
city.pu.pu_rental_tariff.1: On the board: "Bicycle, 1 rouble an hour. Boat, 2 roubles an hour, for two. Deckchair, 30 kopecks an hour; umbrella free if the wind doesn't take it."
city.pu.pu_rental_tariff.2: Below, in chalk: "Children under 10 with parents. Parents under 40 with children. Everybody else as it turns out."
city.pu.pu_souvenir_amber.1: In the case are pieces of amber. One holds a gnat with splayed legs, another a tiny air bubble. The tag: "Summer, about forty million years ago."
city.pu.pu_souvenir_amber.2: Held to the light, amber turns to honey. I didn't pick it up: it turns out it looks fine without me.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_boxes.1: Boxes on the shelf: caskets with shells on the lids, painted spoons, wooden fish on strings, gull-shaped whistles. The whistle sounds like a kettle regardless.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_boxes.2: A paper stuck to one casket lid says: "If you open it, you buy it." I didn't open it.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_chat.1: "Amber is frozen time. The resin flowed for millions of years so we could hang it on a string. Take the one you like; each has its own age."
city.pu.pu_souvenir_chat.2: "Towards evening come the ones who forgot about presents. I know them by their eyes. Postcards are for them."
city.pu.pu_souvenir_chat.3: "Weekends bring the passengers from the suburban train. They ask: 'What's the most local thing?' I say: 'The wind.' But I sell what I have."
city.pu.pu_souvenir_chat.4: "Take your time. Everything lies in its place here, and if it doesn't, someone bought it and put it back."
city.pu.pu_souvenir_globe.1: A globe on a tall stand. Lyudmilovsk isn't marked with a pin, but looking from the right it's somewhere around here. The sea is labelled small: "Baltic".
city.pu.pu_souvenir_globe.2: I gave the globe a spin. It rolled for a long time and stopped on the Pacific. Far away. I nodded: I'm fine here.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_guestbook.1: A guestbook open at page five. An entry: "Yerevan, July. The sea turned out bigger than on the postcard. Thank you." A little boat is drawn beside it.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_guestbook.2: A new entry: "Riga, but Mum was born here. Found the house where Grandma lived. The house is there. The windows are different." Signed with just a first name.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_guestbook.3: An entry in a child's hand: "Tashkent. Saw a gull up close. It looked at my bun. Didn't give it up. Proud."
city.pu.pu_souvenir_guestbook.4: An entry written in several languages at once: "It was good here." Beneath it three signatures and one blot.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_guestbook.5: The next page is blank. A pencil on a string lies on top. It seems to be waiting for my entry, even if only in my head.
city.pu.pu_workshop_bins.1: Little drawers with labels: "M3 screws", "M4 screws", "assorted washers", "nothing special", "will sort later". The last is the heaviest.
city.pu.pu_workshop_bins.2: One drawer holds only buttons. Beside it a tag: "For those who came to mend trousers and stayed to mend life."
city.pu.pu_workshop_chat.1: "In the morning I solder. Don't distract me; at that hour even silence costs extra."
city.pu.pu_workshop_chat.2: "Afternoons I take things in. They bring everything: radios, irons, clocks; once they brought a nightingale. A mechanical one, but offended."
city.pu.pu_workshop_chat.3: "Saturday's a short day. What I haven't fixed by three gets fixed on Monday, and comes out better."
city.pu.pu_workshop_chat.4: "The Leningrad from the café? The valve is the problem. They say the fishermen have one. If so, it'll be singing by midweek."
city.pu.pu_workshop_chat.5: "Bring it and I'll fix it. If I can't, I'll say so, and then at least you'll know your sorrow wasn't for nothing."
city.pu.pu_workshop_radios.1: The radios on the shelf wait their turn, each with a tag. One purrs the Blue Light show, another is silent, and a third broadcasts the weather for a town next door.
city.pu.pu_workshop_radios.2: One set is open: inside are valves like small glass cities. The master calls them by name.
city.pu.pu_workshop_tags.1: Tags on nails. No. 41: a Riga-6 radio, won't sing. No. 42: an iron that heats unevenly. No. 43: the Leningrad coffee machine (Seagull café), needs a valve.
city.pu.pu_workshop_tags.2: No. 43: "No valve in Lyudmilovsk or in Riga. Searching old things." The master has been searching old things for two days.
city.pu.pu_workshop_tags.3: No. 43: "Found it! At the fish shop, from a written-off paraffin stove. Fits with a hair's gap. Filed it to size."
city.pu.pu_workshop_tags.4: No. 43: DONE. To go back to the café the same day; I'll carry it myself. No. 44: "alarm clock, rings at the wrong time"; bring it in and we'll cure it.
city.pu.pu_workshop_tags.5: A new tag, no number yet: "The boy's torch. A bulb, a battery and a promise." It seems they already know me here.
city.pu.pu_workshop_tv.1: The screen shows the test card: circles, stripes, squares. A perfectly steady picture is rare; the shop is proud of it.
city.pu.pu_workshop_tv.2: A television with a screwdriver left inside. The most peaceful sight on the coast: the blue bar doesn't move.
city.px.bell.1: I pulled the rope. The bell struck thickly, bong, and the sound went out over the water, far, far away. The gulls on the rail flinched but came back within a minute.
city.px.bell.2: I rang slowly, as you do in fog: once a minute. Nobody answered from the sea. But a lantern lit on the next pier: someone heard and is awake.
city.px.bell.3: On a day off the order is to ring politely: people are resting on the promenade. I rang as softly as one can ring a bell the size of a person.
city.px.bottle.1: A model brigantine on a stand, sails of cigarette paper. Arkady took three winters to make it. Beside it a green bottle with a cork: "Open only together."
city.px.bottle.2: The bottle is sealed with tar, a rolled note inside. Chalked on the glass: "Do not open until Maria returns." The chalk is fresh: they renew it every day.
city.px.bottle.3: The bottle has been opened and closed again. The note inside: "We saw your light eleven miles off. Thank you. Captain Laptev." The cork is freshly tarred, this time for keeps.
city.px.bottle.prompt: E — look at the little ship
city.px.cat.1: The keepers' cat sleeps curled in the basket, one ear still on duty. I scratched his cheek: he kept sleeping, only noticeably louder.
city.px.cat.2: The cat opened one eye, appraised me and closed it again. I think I've been taken on probation. Until the first herring, probably.
city.px.cat.3: The cat isn't asleep: he sits upright in the basket, watching the light turn above. I looked at the ceiling too. A pale patch walks across the walls and he follows it with his eyes.
city.px.cat.4: At weekends the cat sleeps even harder. The keepers swear he's the only one in town who reads the timetable, and his day off is on it.
city.px.clockwork.1: The lens's turning gear: a weight in the shaft, wheels in brass cheeks. Daylight needs no beam and the lens is under a linen cover, but they wind it ahead so there's no waiting at dusk. I gave it ten turns.
city.px.clockwork.2: Sunset: the covers are off and the clockwork wound. The handle goes stiffly. The weight crawls up the shaft, then the wheels take it and start counting time.
city.px.clockwork.3: At night you can hear the gear all through the house: tick, tick, tick, and every twenty seconds a beam lays down upstairs. I wound it: the weight must never be left at the bottom.
city.px.cup.1: I set a hot cup beside the log. The steam climbs and the lamp behind it goes hazy. Whoever comes will find it, smile first and drink after.
city.px.cup.2: I left the cup by the night log so that whoever comes on watch finds it warm. Slid it right up to his pen. Now this place belongs to someone.
city.px.flags.1: The yellow flag of the signal code means: "My vessel is healthy, I request permission to enter." The keepers keep it at the top of the pigeonholes: visitors are always welcome here.
city.px.flags.2: Red and yellow on the diagonal: "Man overboard." The flag is worn at the folds. Never once had to be raised, and checked every spring. First they check it, then they say nothing.
city.px.flags.3: The white and blue flag: "Divers below, keep clear." It goes up when the piles at the pier are cleaned. In the next pigeonhole lies a small whistle for the divers.
city.px.flags.4: In one pigeonhole there's a checked kerchief instead of a flag, with a slip: "For Maria. If they ask what it means: 'We're waiting for you.'" The kerchief is freshly washed.
city.px.gweather.1: The instrument screen: white louvres, two thermometers inside. The vane points west: that's where weather comes from, the keepers say. The anemometer spins evenly, like three small suns.
city.px.gweather.2: At night the anemometer rings thin and fine. The screen is dark, chalked on its door: "Readings at 02:00. Arkady." Added smaller in chalk: "Don't sleep."
city.px.keeper_bottle.prompt: E — look at the little ship
city.px.keeper_clockwork.prompt: E — wind up the lantern's clockwork
city.px.keeper_cup.prompt: E — set a cup of tea on the desk
city.px.keeper_watch.prompt: E — open the clockwork's watch book
city.px.oilskins.1: Two yellow oilskins and one small, a child's. The linings are stitched "A. O." and "A. K.", the small one "For guests". It goes to whoever is taken up top in the rain.
city.px.oilskins.2: The oilskins are still damp: someone has just been out on the gallery to check the bell. A thin drip crawls from a hood into an old boiled-sweet tin set on the floor.
city.px.oilskins.3: The sou'wester hangs on its hook with its brim toward the door. A habit, so you don't forget it going out. Aram says no storm ever starts without it.
city.px.ships.1: The table of ships' lights: white masthead, red to port, green to starboard. By day a seiner on the sea: a dark silhouette and a flock of gulls over it.
city.px.ships.2: Far off a passenger steamer crawls: white as sugar and as small. By the table, at night it will show three white lights and a red and a green.
