city.px.ships.3: A barge along the shore, a thread of smoke, riding low. The table: "Tug with tow: two masthead lights in line." Checked: true, down to the last detail.
city.px.ships.4: An empty sea, only glints. The keepers joke that on days like this you look for ships and find thoughts. I found one, but it was a small one.
city.px.ships.5: At night two lights side by side on the water, red and green: a ship heading straight at me. By the table it's bound for the pier, but not yet, another forty minutes.
city.px.ships.6: A white light low over the horizon, another a little higher: a seiner, fishing. The lantern beams rock on the water with her side.
city.px.ships.7: A single green light at the very edge. By the table: starboard side, the vessel is going left. I wished it were Maria, and was surprised how easily the wish came.
city.px.ships.8: Darkness, only the beam touching the water once every twenty seconds. Between beams the dark is so thick it seems alive and very attentive.
city.px.signal.1: By day the lamp is hardly seen. I clacked the shutter three times anyway: "I'm here." Someone in the port waved a red rag: the tug's mechanic, probably.
city.px.signal.2: At night the lamp strikes like a fist: three flashes toward the sea. A blink came back from the horizon. My heart went thump with it and kept the rhythm a long while.
city.px.storm.1: A painting: a stormy sea and a lone seiner on a crest. Pencilled on the frame: "Not ours, but very like Maria." The painter clearly saw a storm up close.
city.px.storm.2: By lamplight the waves in the painting seem alive. Look long enough and the seiner is about to vanish behind a crest. I looked away first.
city.px.stove.1: I lit the little stove with birch logs. The kettle starts to hum before I've found a mug. I poured myself some and slipped a second helping into my pocket.
city.px.stove.2: The kettle puffs and the shadow of its lid jumps on the wall. It smells of smoke and dried mint from a tin. Good strong tea, with sea salt in the air.
city.px.stove.3: The night watch begins with the kettle. The fire crackles softly in the stove while above the ceiling the light slowly turns. The tea came out nearly as good as the keepers'.
city.px.tides.1: Monday. High water at the pier 06:40 and 19:05, low water 00:30 and 12:50. In chalk: "Order chalk."
city.px.tides.2: Tuesday. High water 07:25 and 19:50, low 01:15 and 13:35. By evening the mussels on the piles will show: enough for supper.
city.px.tides.3: Wednesday. High water 08:10 and 20:35, low 02:00 and 14:20. A note below: "Boatmen: toward eight there's a pull under the pier."
city.px.tides.4: Thursday. High water 08:55 and 21:20, low 02:45 and 15:05. The figures are written clearly, as for an exam.
city.px.tides.5: Friday. High water 09:40 and 22:05, low 03:30 and 15:50. In the corner a little fish is drawn, winking at the reader.
city.px.tides.6: Saturday. High water 10:25 and 22:50, low 04:15 and 16:35. Saturday's tide is the longest: Aram says even the sea is in no hurry.
city.px.tides.7: Sunday. High water 11:10 and 23:35, low 05:00 and 17:20. Underlined in red: "Many people on the promenade by evening. Ring the bell softly."
city.px.watch.1: The clockwork's watch book. "06:10. Wind south-west, force four, visibility good. Seiner Maria sailed for herring, promised to be back tomorrow by evening. Arkady."
city.px.watch.2: "21:00. We wait for Maria till midnight. The light was lit twenty minutes early: let them see it from far off. Aram."
city.px.watch.3: "23:50. No Maria. The radio is silent. The barometer is falling. I wound the clockwork every four hours, not only by the book. Arkady."
city.px.watch.4: "04:00. Storm. We ring the bell every two minutes, a second night running. Hands shaking, but it rings. Told the port by radio: Maria not seen. Aram."
city.px.watch.5: "A night without sleep, the beam runs true, the gale never knocked it off once. The kettle is empty, the bread gone. If anyone comes in, please make us tea. Arkady."
city.px.watch.6: "05:20. It's eased. A faint voice on the radio: 'Lighthouse, this is Maria. Engine failed, we drifted a day. We saw your light. Coming to you.' Aram wept, Arkady pretended not to notice."
city.px.watch.7: "18:40. Maria is at the pier. Captain Laptev left a bottle by the door, a note inside. Put it on the shelf by the little ship. The bell rang this time for nothing: for joy."
city.px.watch.8: "Quiet. A day off by order of both of us. Wrote verses: Aram offered the rhyme 'came back, grinned back', Arkady rejected it, but wrote it down just in case."
city.px.weather.1: Barometer: 1018, the needle planted. Thermometer: nine. Humidity middling. Everything promises a fine day and a dull watch. Pencilled beside it: "Maria sailed."
city.px.weather.2: Barometer: 1014. The needle has crept a hair to the left, or I imagined it. I tapped the glass: it holds. On the card: "Check again this evening."
city.px.weather.3: Barometer: 1006, and the needle is crawling as I watch. Aram's note: "Take sandwiches to the watch. It will be noisy tonight." Under it, Arkady's: "Noisy and long."
city.px.weather.4: Barometer: 998. The needle presses against the word "Storm" and trembles. The glass is hairlined from old tapping. Someone has stuck a slip beside it: "Don't tap. It knows."
city.px.weather.5: Barometer: 994, lower than anything in this notebook. The needle lies on "Storm" and doesn't stir. On the back of the card Arkady wrote the number and ringed it twice.
city.px.weather.6: Barometer: 1003, the needle's on its way up. Chalked on the frame: "Easing." The thermometer cautiously says eight. Even it doesn't seem to believe it.
city.px.weather.7: Barometer: 1015. The needle is back at "Change" and looks, I think, embarrassed. Beyond the wall the wind sighs without any malice now.
city.px.weather.8: Barometer: 1021. Someone has drawn a small sun above it and signed: "This is Arkady. Doesn't believe it, draws it anyway." The sun came out crooked and very warm.
city.rassvet.closed.board: Something is chalked on the board in the dark but I cannot read it. I'll have to come by day.
city.rassvet.closed.floor: The floor is polished to a shine, the piano is under its cloth, the record is in its sleeve. Until tomorrow.
city.rassvet.closed.hall: It is dark in the hall and the notice board is barely visible. Somebody has chalked at the bottom: "Lights on at three."
city.rassvet.closed.menu: The menu on the board cannot be made out in the dusk. Only the big word at the top shows: "TEA". The rest is probably as usual.
city.rassvet.closed.poster: The poster behind dark glass. In the dusk I can make out only the word "Today"; the rest tomorrow, when the lights are on.
city.rassvet.dance.free1: The floor is empty and polished to a shine. A record lies on the player waiting for the teacher. I did three waltz steps to my own count and the echo answered.
city.rassvet.dance.free2: The mirror shows all of me, which is usually enough for a minute. I pretended to be only straightening my shirt, and straightened it three times.
city.rassvet.dance.fri: Friday is polka. We hop so hard the mirror trembles and nobody wants to stop first. When the record ended we kept hopping for another second.
city.rassvet.dance.sat: Saturday is a request night. Whoever asks for a waltz gets a waltz, whoever asks for a foxtrot gets a foxtrot. One couple ordered something that is not in the programme, and the teacher played it herself.
city.rassvet.dance.thu: Thursday is slow dances. The light is dimmed, the record rustles, couples sway on the spot as if the floor were drifting a little. The teacher walks among them whispering, "Breathe."
city.rassvet.dance.tue: Tuesday is waltz. The teacher claps: "One-two-three, young man, not one-two-stop!" I tried not to tread on myself and trod on my neighbour.
city.rassvet.dance.wed: Wednesday is foxtrot. The steps are quick and everybody's face is solemn, as at an exam. My partner said, "Don't look at your feet." I looked and lost the beat.
city.rassvet.door.1: Behind the door they are warming up: "do-re-mi-fa", then "do-re-mi-fa" again, but crosser. The choirmaster asks for basses. The tenors come in first: they always do.
city.rassvet.door.2: Behind the door the drama circle is rehearsing. Somebody says loudly and with feeling, "Dinner is served!" and somebody just as loudly answers, "No!" Then both laugh and it begins again.
city.rassvet.door.3: Late. Behind the door one voice and one violin, both quiet. They play the same passage for the fourth time: it does not come right, but it gets lovelier each time.
city.rassvet.door.4: Silence. The red lamp over the door is out. I put my ear to it: the radiator hums and nothing else. I decided not to disturb anyone.
city.rassvet.film.fri_d: A boy from the yard wants to win the table-tennis championship and trains against the wall of the house, on the garage roof, in the bread queue. His coach is a caretaker who plays left-handed and without a net. The final is won not by him but by a small girl with pigtails, but the cup goes round all the same and everyone is happy. For a long while afterwards the ball keeps tapping in the yard.
city.rassvet.film.fri_e: A musical. Every evening on the pier gather those who can dance and those who cannot but are shy. One couple cannot find the step: she leads, he treads on her foot. They waltz on the wet planks until the last lamp goes out. The lamp does not go out before the music ends: that is how it is done in films. The hall files out into the street, and somebody hums.
city.rassvet.film.mon_d: A comedy. A holiday-maker arrives for a week and his hat blows away on the first day. The hat tours the whole town: it sits on a monument, sails in a boat, rides in a cable-car cabin. He chases it all through his holiday and at the end realises he has rested better than anyone. The hall laughs so hard the screen shakes.
city.rassvet.film.mon_e: An old fisherman has waited forty years for a new lighthouse to be lit on the point. Every morning he goes down to the shore and straightens his scarf as if before an important meeting. At last the lighthouse is lit, and for the first time in his life he does not know what to do with his morning. He just stands and looks at the light. The hall weeps and nobody hides it.
city.rassvet.film.sat_d: A detective story for children. The most important gull has vanished from the fish quay, and a boy with a magnifying glass and a sandwich becomes the detective. He questions the witnesses: a herring, a cat and one very evasive swan. The gull is found on the cinema roof: she was being shown the films too. At this point the hall turns round to look at the ceiling every time.
city.rassvet.film.sat_e: A film about the projectionist of a small town. He loves every film he runs, but he only ever watches a sliver through the little window of the booth. One day he comes down into the hall and sits in the front row to see a whole film at last. It turns out the most interesting thing in the hall is happening not on the screen but on the faces. The hall can't help glancing back at the booth.
city.rassvet.film.sun_d: A cartoon. A hedgehog gets into a cable-car cabin to take an apple to a friend at the other end of town. First a giraffe rides along, then an orchestra, then one very serious snail. By the time they reach the station the apple has gone off, but everybody else arrives, and it turns out it is the friend's birthday. The children in the hall shout "Catch!" in chorus, although nobody has thrown anything.
city.rassvet.film.sun_e: An old silent film: a pianist plays to the screen, and the hall is so quiet you can hear the seats creak. A man walks down an empty street and every time turns the wrong way. He meets a closed shop, a wet umbrella on a bench and a window where somebody is playing a piano. At the end he finds the house, but we are not shown whose. You come out and for a few minutes you walk slowly.
city.rassvet.film.thu_d: A summer comedy. Three friends carry one watermelon across the whole town to a house where it is expected. On the way the watermelon manages to be a pillow, a ball and an important witness. When they arrive it turns out they were expected yesterday. They eat it on the porch anyway, four of them: the fourth is the neighbour's dog.
city.rassvet.film.thu_e: A radio amateur catches a call sign at night that is in no directory. For three nights he writes down dots and dashes and tells no one, and on the fourth he finds the courage to answer. One word comes out of the speaker: "Hearing you." After that there is not a word in the film: only the valves glowing orange and the needle trembling. Afterwards you want to keep quiet for a while.
city.rassvet.film.tue_d: A black-and-white newsreel. Cranes, concrete, and a girl with a tape measure giving orders to a gang of grown men. The cable car cuts across the sky and the cabins slide over the roofs like beads on a string. At the end the announcer says, "The town is ready", while on screen people carry a piano up the stairs of a new house.
city.rassvet.film.tue_e: The night shift on the cable car. The operator brings down the last cabin and always finds something forgotten in it: a glove, a book, somebody's word on the misted glass. The last passenger carries a letter in his pocket and is afraid to hand it over. The cabin reaches the station, the door will not open, and for two minutes they look at the sea in silence. Then the door opens.
city.rassvet.film.wed_d: A popular-science film. The announcer explains that the sun is a star and that we live next to it, which is perfectly normal. Drawn rays run to the Earth for eight minutes while the whole hall counts along with him. At the end we see a sunflower turning after the light, and then a sleepy cat doing exactly the same.
city.rassvet.film.wed_e: A girl finds a bottle with a letter by the breakwater. The letter is in Swedish, so she walks through town showing it to everyone: the fisherman, the chemist, the postman. Each translates it his own way and every time the letter comes out new. She decides to answer herself, in Russian, and throws the bottle back into the water. The hall is silent, and then it claps.
city.rassvet.hall.1: A request: during the show please do not talk, rustle or crack sunflower seeds. Rustling is an insult to the projectionist and to the people in the film.
city.rassvet.hall.2: Found in the hall: two left gloves, an old programme, a striped scarf. Ask at the cloakroom; name the colour and the character.
city.rassvet.hall.3: At weekends there are ten minutes of newsreel before the evening show, then the film. Latecomers: on tiptoe and no hard feelings.
city.rassvet.hall.4: New Year's week: a tree in the foyer, tangerines at the buffet one to a customer, and before the evening show the whole hall says "Happy New Year" in chorus.
city.rassvet.hall.5: 8 March: ladies get tea at the buffet without queueing. Gentlemen queue as usual, and also get tea.
city.rassvet.hall.6: 1 September: schoolchildren get the front row if they bring a school diary and a smile. The diary need not be opened.
city.rassvet.ladder.1: The club's ladder, in chalk on the board. From the top: Lev Markovich, Zoya, Vadim, Uncle Grisha, Kirill (ten years old). Under him an empty line labelled "a place for the brave".
city.rassvet.ladder.2: Kirill has climbed a rung. Uncle Grisha rubbed out his name and at once wrote it in again, a little lower: just in case.
city.rassvet.ladder.3: Zoya has challenged Lev Markovich. The game is set for Saturday, the stake is tea. Chairs are already set round the board.
city.rassvet.ladder.4: Saturday: Zoya won. Lev Markovich wrote himself onto the second line and left whistling. He likes losing more than winning: there is more to go over afterwards.
city.rassvet.ladder.5: On the bottom, empty line someone's hand has written: "Guest: draw with Vadim." A question mark beside it: everybody is waiting to see if the guest will come again.
city.rassvet.ladder.6: In the cupboard under the board lies a pad of sheets for recording games. The top one is blank, headed: "A start has been made."
city.rassvet.lost.1: A bucket of umbrellas by the hat stand. Tags on the handles: "blue", "black", "somebody's". Above them on the stand hangs a hat from the spring before last, and the cloakroom lady will not touch it: what if they come back.
city.rassvet.lost.2: A note is pinned to the tag on the black umbrella: "I'll call for it as soon as it rains." There is no rain yet, so the owner must be busy.
city.rassvet.lost.3: The cloakroom lady says the thing most often forgotten in the hall is a glove, and always just one. One glove is not a loss, it is a hint.
city.rassvet.menu.1: The menu: tea 15, coffee 30, pie 18, biscuits 20, Buratino 18. At the bottom in chalk: "Ice cream after the show, not during."
city.rassvet.menu.2: On Saturdays there are curd tarts with the tea, two to a customer so there is enough for all. The prices are the same. The buffet lady said the tarts are her way of telling who has come to the cinema for the first time.
city.rassvet.menu.3: The Sunday menu: tea and whatever is left from Saturday. The buffet lady says, "If there's little left, it was good."
city.rassvet.mirror.1: In the mirror: the couples, and the clock on the wall behind me. Half the hall looks at itself, the other half at the clock.
city.rassvet.mirror.2: In the mirror: an empty hall, a piano and me. The piano looks more confident.
city.rassvet.mirror.3: Slips of paper are tucked into the frame: the timetable, the teacher's phone number and somebody's drawing of a dancing dog. The dog keeps better time than many.
city.rassvet.piano.1: By day the pianist sits at the piano learning something without the music. I asked permission, he nodded and moved over. Together it came out twice as bad but twice as loud.
city.rassvet.piano.2: In the evening the piano works for the dance class: all the music is underlined in red. I tried to slip in a tune of my own and the teacher, without turning round, said, "In time."
city.rassvet.piano.3: At night the hall is empty and the piano is under a cloth. I lifted the cloth and pressed one key. The sound went all through the foyer and came back. I covered the piano again.
city.rassvet.piano.4: On the stand: music with no cover, the waltz "The Pier", copied out by hand. I played the first bars and somebody in the foyer said quietly, "That's the one."
city.rassvet.poster.fest: Poster, festive. Today the shows run without a break from three o'clock until closing. A ticket is thirty roubles as always, and the buffet gives free tea to anyone who came in a hat. Hats are lent at the cloakroom, but only real ones.
city.rassvet.poster.fri: Poster. Today: in the afternoon “The Yard Champion”, in the evening “Waltz on the Pier”. Tomorrow: afternoon “The Case of the Missing Gull”, evening “The Projectionist”. Friday. After the evening show the buffet stays open another half hour.
city.rassvet.poster.mon: Poster. Today: in the afternoon “Holiday at My Own Expense”, in the evening “The Man Who Waited for the Lighthouse”. Tomorrow: afternoon “How Lyudmilovsk Was Built”, evening “The Last Cabin”. On Mondays the box office takes only smiles and thirty roubles.
city.rassvet.poster.sat: Poster. Today: in the afternoon “The Case of the Missing Gull”, in the evening “The Projectionist”. Tomorrow: afternoon “The Hedgehog's Cable-Car Adventures”, evening “The Empty Street”. Saturday: no break between shows; the break is in the buffet.
city.rassvet.poster.sun: Poster. Today: in the afternoon “The Hedgehog's Cable-Car Adventures”, in the evening “The Empty Street”. Tomorrow: afternoon “Holiday at My Own Expense”, evening “The Man Who Waited for the Lighthouse”. Sunday. The front row is for those who came with a hedgehog or without.
city.rassvet.poster.thu: Poster. Today: in the afternoon “Three Friends and a Watermelon”, in the evening “Silence on the Air”. Tomorrow: afternoon “The Yard Champion”, evening “Waltz on the Pier”. Thursday: the radio corner is open; the photo circle meets at six.
city.rassvet.poster.tue: Poster. Today: in the afternoon “How Lyudmilovsk Was Built”, in the evening “The Last Cabin”. Tomorrow: afternoon “The Sun Is Our Home”, evening “A Letter in a Bottle”. Tuesday: dance class in the foyer in the evening; noise is allowed, but in time.
city.rassvet.poster.wed: Poster. Today: in the afternoon “The Sun Is Our Home”, in the evening “A Letter in a Bottle”. Tomorrow: afternoon “Three Friends and a Watermelon”, evening “Silence on the Air”. Wednesday. Please arrive before the bell, not together with it.
city.rassvet.radio_a.1: Radio Lyudmilovsk: morning exercises to a piano. The announcer counts "and one, and two" so briskly that I want to get off my chair, but I stay.
city.rassvet.radio_a.2: A request concert: the fishermen ask for a song about the shore and are given a song about the shore. Requests are always played here, even the unfortunate ones.
city.rassvet.radio_a.3: The evening bulletin: wind from the sea, the cable-car timetable and an announcement about a lost umbrella. The umbrella, they say, has been found, but its owner has not.
city.rassvet.radio_a.4: At night Radio Lyudmilovsk is silent, the set only hisses, and now and then somebody's violin slips through the hiss. Turn the knob: the violin comes closer, then recedes.
city.rassvet.radio_b.1: By day the amateurs chatter on short wave: somebody in Riga asks for the weather again, somebody in Tallinn tells about his cat. The call signs sound like the names of neighbours.
city.rassvet.radio_b.2: Towards evening the distant ones come on. An amateur in Arkhangelsk spells out a QSL card letter by letter, then reads the address: "Lyudmilovsk, House of Culture, radio corner." That's us.
city.rassvet.radio_b.3: At night the air is as wide as the sea. A announcer in a foreign language reads out numbers, someone answers in Morse, and between them something quite different chirps. I wrote down the dots and dashes and understood none of them.
city.rassvet.radio_b.4: Our club's call sign is known in three countries. An amateur in Finland sent greetings to "the circle with the mug"; I did not understand, but passed it on.
city.rassvet.radio_b.5: Towards morning the stations go out one by one. What is left is an even noise, and in it suddenly something short: "...hearing you, Lyudmilovsk." I checked: at this hour there is nobody in the club but me.
city.rassvet.reel.prompt: E — watch from the front row
city.rassvet.reelfilm_1: The film hisses and the first frames have faded like a postcard. People walk along the pier with buckets and flags, and all of them look into the camera as if they cannot believe they are being filmed. A girl in a big beret climbs the lighthouse and lights the lamp, but the lamp does not burn. The third reel ends, the fourth tears, the fifth is gone: the screen turns white where the morning should have risen. The pianist played the waltz from the poster's sheet, and nobody in the hall moved.
city.rassvet.reelfilm_2: We came again, almost the same people. In the dark somebody said the director's name out loud and several voices answered at once. The white light at the end is now called "the fifth reel", and nobody complains.
city.rassvet.stubs.1: Ticket stubs in a tray: red for the afternoon shows, yellow for the evening ones. The clerk counts them every evening and gets a new number every time, but always the same smile.
city.rassvet.stubs.2: At the weekend there are twice as many stubs. The pile is weighed down with a cup so it will not fly about, and the cup is already empty.
city.rassvet.stubs.3: On the top stub in pencil: "Four people asked for Rassvet." The clerk does not know which Rassvet is meant, the house or the film, and writes everything down just in case.
city.rassvet.stubs.4: A stub with a red star: "front row, Rassvet". There are already forty-two of them. The clerk has stopped counting and started smiling.
city.rcb.abacus.1: In the morning the abacus clicks sharply: yesterday's takings only add up on the second go.
city.rcb.abacus.2: The beads are pushed to the right: someone was counting empty bottles. I slid them back and still got "forty-three".
city.rcb.abacus.3: By evening the beads wander along the wires every which way. Nina Pavlovna counts faster than any till and can't stand being prompted.
city.rcb.abacus.4: The abacus waits for morning. Red beads are roubles, yellow ones tens.
city.rcb.bread.1: The bread is still warm: it came on trays this morning, and the crust crackles if you just look at it.
city.rcb.bread.2: Some white loaves and a couple of rye ones left. Nina Pavlovna pushes the rounder ones to the front.
city.rcb.bread.3: By evening the bread looks like yesterday's and tastes like today's. The price tag says so.
city.rcb.bread.4: The rack is empty, only crumbs and a note: "Tomorrow morning."
city.rcb.bread.prompt: E — look at the bread rack
city.rcb.cork.1: The cork board. A notice in pencil on a school exercise page: "Lost: a red woollen sock, the left one. Knitted by my grandmother, there is no other like it. Flat 3-07, ask for Vitya."
city.rcb.cork.2: Under it a second sheet: "Vitya, a red sock is hanging on the line, on the right. But it's a right one. Nina Pavlovna from the shop."
city.rcb.cork.3: Next to it a note in a crooked hand: "The right one is not mine. Mine is the left, with a darn on the heel. Vitya."
city.rcb.cork.4: The wash schedule was renewed: "Monday, first floor; Tuesday, second..." At the bottom in red pen: "Whoever took the second machine on Sunday, have a conscience!"
city.rcb.cork.5: A fresh notice: "The sock with the darned heel has turned up! It is in the Lost Property box. The right one of the pair is kept by Nina Pavlovna, but she will hand it only to Vitya himself."
city.rcb.cork.6: Vitya thanks everyone who helped look. And for those still missing something, the Lost Property box stands under the shelf: maybe yours is in it.
city.rcb.deposit.1: Bottle deposit. The bottles clink in their crates and it smells of last year's lemonade. No chipped necks, no foreign labels.
city.rcb.deposit.2: I've nothing to return yet. But three rows of empty kefir bottles stand on the table, straight as soldiers.
city.rcb.deposit.3: A sheet is pinned over the table: "An empty bottle, three roubles. Three bottles, tea and a dry ring-roll." Nobody promises the tea, but the sheet hangs there.
city.rcb.feed.1: I tossed a handful of seeds on the rusty tin. The pigeons arrived before I counted to three and shared the spoils with quarrels and cooing.
city.rcb.feed.2: A white tumbler pigeon perched on my hand and briskly pecked the seeds from my palm. The others waited like a queue in a shop.
city.rcb.feed.3: By evening the pigeons settle in a row along the loft's edge. One seed each for the night, and the chatter dies down.
city.rcb.feeder.1: Tits come first: grab a seed and fly to the pipe to crack it. They come one at a time and quarrel over every grain.
city.rcb.feeder.2: In the daytime sparrows: a whole noisy gang at once, looking as if the feeder was built just for them.
city.rcb.feeder.3: Towards evening a gull lands and strolls over the roof. The feeder is too small for her, but she'll look anyway.
city.rcb.feeder.4: The feeder is empty. A dusting of dust and one forgotten grain.
city.rcb.fold.1: A sheet is folded by two. Today a stranger held the second corner, and we parted without a word, very pleased with ourselves.
city.rcb.fold.2: A forgotten towel with an embroidered gull lies on the table. I folded it into a neat square and left it on top for its owner.
city.rcb.fold.3: Warm linen smells of powder and iron. I stacked the shirts and matched the socks. One was left without a partner, as usual.
city.rcb.goods_day.1: Monday: bread from the bakery, rye and white loaves. Kefir comes at lunchtime.
city.rcb.goods_day.2: Tuesday: apples from the orchards outside town, six roubles. Soft ones on the side don't count.
city.rcb.goods_day.3: Wednesday: little round cheeses, only two delivered. First come, first served.
city.rcb.goods_day.4: Thursday: loose cookies, take them in a paper cone. Please bring the cone back, though nobody does.
city.rcb.goods_day.5: Friday: sunflower seeds roasted this morning. Husks in your pocket, not on the floor!
city.rcb.goods_day.6: Saturday: stock up on water and kefir, we're closed tomorrow. Bread only until noon.
city.rcb.goods_day.7: Sunday: shop closed. All questions to Nina Pavlovna, flat 1-02, ring twice.
city.rcb.lie.1: The morning sun doesn't burn yet, it only warms a cheek. The canvas is cool, gulls cry below, and nothing needs doing.
city.rcb.lie.2: Noon. I squint and red clouds float under my eyelids. A pigeon warms itself on the pipe beside me, eyeing me with one eye.
city.rcb.lie.3: Sunset. The clouds over the sea turn pink at the edges like paper held to a lamp. Below, the windows of the house light up one by one.
city.rcb.lie.4: At night you see the stars from the roof. The Great Bear stands over the ventilation stack, and three short beams run from the lighthouse across the sky.
city.rcb.lie.prompt: E — lie down on the lounger
city.rcb.lost_box.1: In the box: buttons in a matchbox, one glove, somebody's key on a string. A tag on top: "Kept a month, then to a good home."
city.rcb.lost_box.2: Among the things: a child's bobble hat and glasses missing one arm. The hat smells of dry linen, the glasses of tears. I put everything back in the same order.
city.rcb.lost_box.3: At the very bottom, under the lone glove, a red sock with a darn on the heel. The left one! I hung it on the line beside the right. The pair was together, and the line at once looked happier.
city.rcb.lost_box.prompt: E — look in the Lost Property box
city.rcb.mags.1: A women's magazine with patterns: a sundress in one evening. The pattern is crossed out in someone's pencil: "Too tight at the shoulders."
city.rcb.mags.2: A picture weekly with a crossword. Three words are filled in by another hand, all three wrong. I fixed them and felt as good as after exercise.
city.rcb.mags.3: A science monthly: an article on clouds. Each kind has a name, and the coast is where you see them best. I finished it before the drum stopped.
city.rcb.mags.4: A bound volume of a travel magazine: an island where it's always summer. The machine behind me hums like distant surf.
city.rcb.mags.5: A crumpled satirical magazine with a torn corner. On the back someone wrote a number: "call after six."
city.rcb.mangle.1: The mangle is stiff as an unoiled door. A wet pillowcase passed between the rollers and came out flat as a pancake.
city.rcb.mangle.2: Stamped on the frame: "Schmidt's workshop, 1927." This mangle is older than anyone in the house. It survives because nobody knows how to repair it.
city.rcb.mangle.3: The handle squeaks in time: one-two, one-two. A minute in I caught the rhythm and began to hum.
city.rcb.radio.1: Morning exercises on the radio: "Arms out... and one!" Nina Pavlovna squats between the shelves and never drops a jar.
city.rcb.radio.2: A programme for housewives: a beetroot salad recipe, numbers in grams. The shopkeeper nods and jots something on the back of a receipt.
city.rcb.radio.3: Music by request. The shopkeeper hums along under her breath, off key but wholehearted.
city.rcb.radio.4: Evening news: the harvest, milk, wind on the coast. Good to count on an abacus to.
city.rcb.radio.5: The radio crackles softly: the air is empty until morning.
city.rcb.roofnote.1: "The roof is for everyone. Solarium rules: stubs in the tin, don't chase pigeons, take the washing in before sunset. House council."
city.rcb.roofnote.2: "The pigeon loft on the roof is Vitya's, flat 3-07. The pigeons are polite. Seeds at Nina Pavlovna's shop: ten roubles a bag."
city.rcb.roofnote.3: "Vitya is sad: the sock his grandmother knitted is gone. Please look carefully: red, left, with a darn."
city.rcb.roofnote.4: "Stuck up again, the wind tore it off. Don't leave slippers by the telescope! Jupiter is visible only from the chalk-marked spot."
city.rcb.roofnote.5: "The sock is found! This evening there is samovar tea on the roof for everyone who looked. Bring your mugs. Vitya."
city.rcb.scale.1: Floor scales with little weights on the beam. The needle shivered and settled: exactly two kilos of potatoes, not a gram more. Nina Pavlovna always lays on one extra weight for luck, and everybody pretends not to notice.
city.rcb.scale.2: A tin tag on the platform: "Inspected in March." Under it someone scratched with a nail: "Short weight, not here."
city.rcb.scale.3: I stepped on myself. The needle swung and showed forty-eight. So a sack of potatoes weighs more than I thought, or I weigh less.
city.rcb.shower.1: The water in the tank warmed in the sun all day: warm on top, the bottom still remembers the well. I gasped, laughed and dried off with the towel from the nail.
city.rcb.shower.2: The rose first sprayed sideways, then settled. Over the canvas screen you see only sky and a gull. A rooftop shower: the tenants' best invention.
city.rcb.socks.1: On the line over the table hangs what was forgotten: a striped sock, a mitten, half a pair of baby rompers. Every peg has a dated slip pinned to it.
city.rcb.socks.2: A red woollen sock for a right foot. A pencil note beside it: "Not yours? Ask in the shop."
city.rcb.socks.3: The red sock still hangs. A second one has appeared, a blue one without a mate: somebody decided the red one was lonely.
city.rcb.socks.4: Someone took the blue sock. The red one stays and waits. The peg has been moved so it won't flap in the draught by the door.
city.rcb.socks.prompt: E — look at the line of forgotten things
city.rcb.tea.1: The samovar puffs like a little locomotive. The tea is strong and amber, with mint from the tub. The cup comes with a lump of sugar and a view of the sea.
city.rcb.tea.2: Evening tea on the roof. Vitya, in two different socks, red and blue, pours into mugs and explains that the red one now has its pair. Everyone keeps a straight face.
city.rcb.tea.3: At night the samovar cools, ticking softly. At the bottom of the mug there's one more mint star. I drank up and looked at the real ones.
city.rcb.tea.prompt: E — pour tea from the samovar
city.rcb.telescope.1: The tripod telescope looks out to sea. A fishing boat, a shirt drying on its mast, glints running over the lens. A note on the tube: "Don't swing it."
city.rcb.telescope.2: At night the telescope shows the Moon so close you see the mountains on the edge of the shadow. A slip beside it: "Jupiter left of the tube, four dots. The tripod stands on chalk marks, don't move it! V. P."
city.rcb.telescope.3: The Perseids are scattered above the roof. While I counted, three streaked the sky. I didn't manage a wish, but the telescope watched in silence as if it understood.
city.rcb.telescope.4: In winter the stars are prickly as frost. In the telescope, Orion: the belt and a nebula like a breath on glass.
city.rcb.tub1.1: A sign: "Tomatoes 'Ox Heart'. Do not pick! Z. I." The stems are tied to sticks with rags, like arms in bandages.
city.rcb.tub1.2: One tomato is already turning pink on one side. The owner is clearly counting the days: notches on the stick beside it.
city.rcb.tub2.1: A sign: "Dahlias. Last year's tubers, do not dig up!" The buds are tight as fists.
city.rcb.tub2.2: An orange tongue is already poking out of one bud. In a couple of days this will be the smartest roof on the block.
city.rcb.tub3.1: A sign: "Mint for tea. Pinch one leaf at a time!" Someone drew a steaming cup next to it.
city.rcb.tub3.2: I rubbed a leaf between my fingers: it smells so good I want to put the samovar on at once.
city.rcb.tub4.1: A sign: "Dill. Cucumbers promised, but changed their minds." The dill has outgrown the sign.
city.rcb.tub4.2: In the dill's shade hides one single cucumber the size of a finger. It evidently hasn't heard it changed its mind.
city.rcb.wash.1: I put shirts and a towel in the drum and added powder. The machine groaned, took in water and began to turn. Forty minutes: just enough for the magazines by the bench.
city.rcb.wash.2: Daytime wash: the machine hums evenly, the drum turns socks and thoughts together. The minutes drip along with the water.
city.rcb.wash.3: In the evening the machines have a queue of baskets. I got the end one, which rattles on the spin. You get used to it.
city.rcb.wash.4: The machine stands quiet with its door ajar so it won't smell damp.
city.rcb.washline.1: Start of the week: the first floor's blue sheets on the lines. White shirts hang in a row like pupils at assembly.
city.rcb.washline.2: Wednesday and Thursday: colourful children's clothes, polka dot socks and a tiny striped vest. Its owner can't be more than a metre tall.
city.rcb.washline.3: Friday: heavy blankets. They hang motionless like sails in a calm and smell of the sea, though washed in powder.
city.rcb.washline.4: Weekend: the lines are nearly empty. Just one forgotten pillowcase flaps like a flag and nobody comes for it.
city.read.art.1: An album by a marine painter. He painted the same pier a hundred times and never got it the same twice.
city.read.art.2: "How to Paint Light." First tip: you can't paint light, you can only leave room for it on the paper.
city.read.art.3: A mosaic exhibition catalogue. In one, a woman holds the sun the way you'd hold a hot frying pan: carefully, a little afraid.
city.read.art.4: A book about this very library: the capsules, it turns out, were meant as "rooms to be alone in without being lonely".
city.read.art.5: Children's drawings published as a book. Under one: "This is my dad at work. Work is where he glows."
city.read.birds.1: "Birds of the Coast: a Field Guide." The laughing gull isn't laughing at you, says a footnote. That's just her voice.
city.read.birds.2: Starlings, the author writes, can imitate a creaking gate, a ringing telephone and a woman calling her cat in.
city.read.birds.3: Chapter: "How to attract a rare bird." A feeder, patience, and not one sudden movement. "Patience" is underlined twice.
city.read.birds.4: On a plate, a jay at life size. The wing feather is so blue I want to touch it to see if it's wet.
city.read.birds.5: The last page: "Birds remember the way to the sun better than we do. If you get lost, watch where they fly in autumn."
city.read.chess.1: A book of studies. White to play and win, if they think of sacrificing the queen. I didn't.
city.read.chess.2: Club championship games, written out by hand. One move is marked "?!" and beside it: "but beautiful".
city.read.chess.3: "Chess for Beginners": the knight moves in an L because, the author explains, it's more fun that way.
city.read.chess.4: An article on the Sicilian defence. I read it twice and understood only that you can defend with gusto too.
city.read.chess.5: A problem on the last page: "Mate in two. Solution in the next issue." The next issue isn't on the shelf.
city.read.cooking.1: A cookbook worn soft with use. On the pie page, a grease stain shaped like Africa.
city.read.cooking.2: A recipe for Lyudmilovsk fish soup: fish, potatoes, onion and "a pinch of fireside talk". Without the last one, it says, it won't work.
city.read.cooking.3: Recipe cards in many handwritings. One says "Granny Zoya's honey cake. Show no one." It's been shown to everyone.
city.read.cooking.4: Japanese cooking for beginners: wash the rice "until the water is as clear as morning". Mornings must be special there.
city.read.cooking.5: A chapter called "Sunshine Jam": apricots, sugar and a south-facing windowsill. Not a word on how to eat it after.
city.read.engineering.1: "Cable Cars: Design and Operation." The tensioning diagram looks like a spider's drawing after a drafting course.
city.read.engineering.2: Plans for a house on stilts. In the margin the architect wrote: "Let the wind walk under the house, and children run there."
city.read.engineering.3: A young engineers' magazine: how to build a radio in a matchbox. I stared at the diagram so long I heard the sea.
city.read.engineering.4: A handbook of lighthouses: a Fresnel lens gathers light the way cupped hands gather water from a stream.
city.read.engineering.5: A textbook on computing machines with a punch card for a bookmark. The holes look like a constellation.
city.read.garden.1: "A Garden in the Sea Wind": what to plant so it won't blow away. The author's answer: "Patience. And sea buckthorn."
city.read.garden.2: A gardener's calendar. For April: "Sow dill, talk to the apple tree." The second is underlined.
city.read.garden.3: A schoolboy's herbarium in a folder. Under a pressed daisy: "Found by the sea. Smelt of sunshine."
city.read.garden.4: How to grow tomatoes on a ninth-floor balcony. The main thing, the author writes, is not to look down and to praise the seedlings often.
city.read.garden.5: A sunflower, the note says, turns its head after the sun only while it's young. Later it faces east and waits.
city.read.kids.1: A pop-up book about a hedgehog who wanted to see the sea. On the last page the sea unfolds right into your hands. I jumped.
city.read.kids.2: "Tales of the Lighthouse." In one the lighthouse falls in love with a star, in another with a steamer. The star never knew.
city.read.kids.3: A picture alphabet: "A for anchor, B for buoy, C for cable car…" Under "Me" there's a boy who looks a lot like me.
city.read.kids.4: A colouring book where someone coloured the sun with felt tip right through the paper: three layers, yellow, orange, yellow again.
city.read.kids.5: A "Why?" encyclopaedia. Why is the sky blue, why is the sea salty, why do we sleep. The last one has no answer, just "sleep".
city.read.local.1: "Lyudmilovsk: a Short Guide." The town, it says, was founded "in time immemorial, roughly on a Thursday".
city.read.local.2: A photo album: the promenade without palms, the square without a fountain, the cable car without cabins. The people in the photos are the ones walking about today.
city.read.local.3: A local history collection: Sun Square once had a great sundial. They say it ran fast whenever the town had a holiday.
city.read.local.4: A list of streets and their old names. One street used to be called "The Street We Walked Home Along". It's written just like that.
city.read.local.5: A pamphlet about Topi, the marshes west of town: "Visits are not advised. Reasons are not given, but you will feel them."
city.read.medicine.1: "The Home Doctor." For a cold, tea with raspberry; for melancholy, a walk by the sea. The second has a tick beside it.
city.read.medicine.2: A poster-pamphlet: "The sun is a friend, but even friends have bad days. Wear a sun hat."
city.read.medicine.3: An anatomy atlas. The heart is drawn in such detail it feels rude to look, like peeping.
city.read.medicine.4: A book on sanatorium cures: "Sea air, mineral water and no hurry." The last, it says, is the one least often prescribed.
city.read.medicine.5: A nurse's handbook. In round handwriting in the margin: "The patient in 12 asked again what the sun was like today. I said: good."
city.read.misc.1: I leafed through at random. In the margin someone had neatly underlined one word: "always".
city.read.misc.2: The book fell open by itself at page forty: people must often open it there.
city.read.misc.3: Between the pages: a pressed maple leaf and a tram ticket with no date.
city.read.misc.4: I read half a chapter and realised I'd read it before. I just don't remember where.
city.read.music.1: A teach-yourself guitar book, three chords. On page four someone gave up and drew a cat in the margin.
city.read.music.2: Sheet music for the waltz "Mist Over the Sea". I can't read music, but you can tell by the look of it: slow and a little guilty.
city.read.music.3: A biography of a conductor who once stopped the orchestra so everyone could hear a thrush singing outside.
city.read.music.4: A record catalogue from the Surf label. Next to the song "Sunbeam Bunny" someone has put five exclamation marks.
city.read.music.5: A solfège textbook. "Do" is home, "sol" is the sun, and "ti" is anyone's guess. The author doesn't know either.
city.read.poetry.1: A thin book by a local poet. "The sea writes on the sand / and wipes it all away, / as if it can't quite trust / the draft of its own grey."
city.read.poetry.2: Poems about the cable car: the cabins are "glass nuts on a string". Lovely, though it's unclear who'd crack them.
city.read.poetry.3: An inscription in ink on the flyleaf: "For Lida, so she won't miss the south. Though how much further south can you get." An illegible signature.
city.read.poetry.4: A haiku in translation: "The old pier. / The gull says nothing, / the wave finishes." The translator must have stood on a pier a long time.
city.read.poetry.5: "I saw the sun from within: / it's like a house where someone waits." Then the page is stained with tea, and I never found out who.
city.read.poetry_sale.1: On sale: "Poems of the Sea, Volume Two". There's no volume one. The bookseller swears volume two makes sense without it.
city.read.poetry_sale.2: A slim typewritten collection by a local poet. The dedication: "To the cable car, which never notices me."
city.read.poetry_sale.3: A three-rouble book full of pencil notes. Next to the line "the sun sets into the water and does not go out" someone wrote: "Checked. True."
city.read.poetry_sale.4: Children's verse about a gull who wanted a job at the post office. The last page is torn out, so I never found out if they took her on.
city.read.poetry_sale.5: A sign on the table: "Poetry sold by weight. Sad ones weigh less, happy ones more." Luckily nobody actually weighed them.
city.read.science.1: "Physics for the Curious." If the Earth stopped, the author writes, we'd all fly east. Politely, without panic.
city.read.science.2: A kitchen experiment: a glass of water, a postcard, turn it over. The water stays in. Pencilled beside it: "It doesn't. Tested. Mum."
city.read.science.3: An old science magazine: an article on how machines will learn to think. The last paragraph has been neatly cut out with scissors.
city.read.science.4: A chapter on light: a ray from the Sun takes eight minutes. So I always see the sun as it was eight minutes ago. A bit sad.
city.read.science.5: The periodic table across two pages. Someone pencilled in a hundred-and-nineteenth box and labelled it "lyudmilium".
city.read.sea.1: "Sailing Directions for Lyudmilovsk Bay." Depths in fathoms, shoals marked with crosses, and one with a question mark.
city.read.sea.2: The handbook says the tide here comes not by the timetable but "when it sees fit". Tables attached, just in case.
city.read.sea.3: A book of sea knots. I learnt the figure-eight and tied my shoelace with it at once. Took five minutes to undo.
city.read.sea.4: An old lighthouse keeper's memoir: in forty years he never saw the sea repeat itself. Not one wave the same.
city.read.sea.5: On the current chart the bay looks like a palm and the currents like the lines on it. The long one runs right through the pier.
city.read.sun.1: "The Sun is an ordinary star," the textbook begins. Then it spends twenty pages proving it's nothing of the sort.
city.read.sun.2: A star atlas. A pencil note by the constellation Cygnus: "You can see us from here. Probably."
city.read.sun.3: A pamphlet, "Solar Energy Serving the Town". On the cover, a vast sphere of mirrors round the Sun. Caption: "A project. Someday."
city.read.sun.4: A chapter on sunspots. People have been counting them for centuries, as if someone were counting the sun like loose change.
city.read.sun.5: An old calendar of sunrises and sunsets. Next to the longest day someone drew a little bonfire and wrote: "Don't sleep".
city.read.travel.1: "Shores" magazine: photos of every lighthouse on the coast. Ours is the double spread, and the caption, oddly, says "You are here".
city.read.travel.2: A guide to the north: volcanoes, fumaroles, snowfields and meadows where "the grass is knee-high and the sky lower than usual".
city.read.travel.3: A timetable of ferries that no longer sail. Someone ringed one crossing, "Lyudmilovsk to Far Shore, 06:40", and wrote: "Waiting".
city.read.travel.4: A traveller's diary: "Day three. Went nowhere. Sat on the promenade. Best day of the trip."
city.read.travel.5: An atlas with a sheet glued in: a map of places on no other map. The furthest is labelled simply "later".
city.reg.clinic.1: A handwritten notice: "The aquarium in the hall is not medicinal but soothing. Do not tap the glass. The fish is called the Head Doctor, the children named it so. Galina Petrovna feeds it at half past eight. Reception."
city.reg.clinic.2: A note from the nurse: "The watering can is by the aquarium. Water must settle for a day, so we draw it the evening before. Whoever is on duty, don't forget, or the fish will take offence, and it has a temper."
city.reg.clinic.3: "Yesterday the Head Doctor wouldn't eat. Galina Petrovna sat with him half the evening. Today he is eating. Thank you to everyone who asked."
city.reg.clinic.4: "Who has been feeding the fish biscuits? The water is clouding. Do not feed fish biscuits. They are spiteful enough as it is."
city.reg.clinic.5: "Sad news: the Head Doctor has lost his companion. There was a second fish; it did not survive the move. We are collecting for a new friend. The jar is on the reception desk. We'll get as many as we can pay for."
city.reg.clinic.6: "The jar today holds forty kopecks and one button. We keep the button: a present for the fish."
city.reg.clinic.7: "The market has promised two guppies on Friday. The Head Doctor doesn't know yet. Don't tell him."
city.reg.cog.1: A fresh sheet: "The club chess clock is missing, the one with the crack on the left dial. Whoever borrowed it, please bring it back. No scolding, only joy."
city.reg.cog.2: "Until the clock turns up, games are timed with the hourglass from the first-aid room. The sand is slow. If you're in a hurry, move faster."
city.reg.cog.3: "Thursday's blitz is cancelled: the hourglass was smashed in time trouble. The culprit repents and is sweeping up."
city.reg.cog.4: "To the model-makers: something is ticking under the workbench in the workshop. Please report what of yours is ticking, and why."
city.reg.cog.5: The model-makers' reply, pinned underneath: "It's a ship ticking. It's clockwork. Nothing to do with your clock. But we'll look too."
city.reg.cog.6: "The clock is found! It was on stage among the props for the play Time, Forward! The director swears he thought it was a dummy."
city.reg.cog.7: "Saturday: the Return of the Clock tournament. The left dial is still cracked and still two minutes fast. White plays at its own risk."
city.reg.fair.1: A chalk poster: "Saturday at six: open contest at the strongman. Beresnev against all comers. Gallery and lottery until sunset."
city.reg.fair.2: A note in red: "The travelling photographer arrives by the end of the week. Please don't frighten him with the wooden horses."
city.reg.fair.3: The notice about the sandal is already crumpled, read all morning. Nobody has signed under it. "Whoever has seen the left one, tell the lottery stand."
city.reg.fair.4: "The photographer has arrived. Record-holders free, everyone else ten roubles. The left sandal, they say, had its picture taken yesterday, alone, without its pair."
city.reg.fair.5: A fresh note: "The left sandal is found! The pair is reunited in the Lost and Found basket by the scales. Thank you to everyone who looked under the benches."
city.reg.library.1: A new notice: "Amnesty for overdue borrowers! Books returned free of fines until the end of the month. Even very old ones. Especially very old ones."
city.reg.library.2: "On the night of the 3rd, the book A Guide to Sundials was dropped in the returns box, issued 14 May 1968. Would the reader please call in. Just to talk."
city.reg.library.3: "Found in the Guide: a bookmark, a cable-car ticket to Lighthouse station, and in pencil: 'I read slowly. Forgive me.'"
city.reg.library.4: "The reader has not called in. The book is on display on the 'Returned' shelf by the window. Please don't touch: it's tired."
city.reg.library.5: "Three more books arrived on the 'Returned' shelf this week, all without slips, all about the sun. We now check the returns box twice a day."
city.reg.library.6: "To our unknown reader. If you are reading this: on Tuesdays we put the kettle on for two. There are no fines and there won't be."
city.reg.library.7: Added to the last notice: "We put the kettle on three Tuesdays running. On the third, there was a pressed daisy in the second cup. We consider that he called."
city.reg.market.1: "Jam contest! Jars accepted at the scales until Friday. Judges: the scales attendant, the honey seller and whichever child is around."
city.reg.market.2: "23 jars received. One has no label and tastes like the wind off the sea. Would the owner please come to the scales."
city.reg.market.3: "The judges remind you: pine-cone jam is not cheating, it's courage. But it goes in a separate category."
city.reg.market.4: "Three people have tasted the unlabelled jar. All three are smiling and can't say why. No more tasting, or the whole market will stop."
city.reg.market.5: "Results: 1st, sea buckthorn (Zoya, vegetable row); 2nd, gooseberry and mint; 3rd, pine cones. Audience prize: the unlabelled jar."
city.reg.market.6: "The owner of the unlabelled jar has not come forward. The jar stands by the scales. It's weighed every morning. It doesn't get any lighter."
city.reg.market.7: "Next year there will be a new category: 'Jam Nobody Made'. No entries accepted: such jars turn up on their own."
city.reg.rassvet.1: Notice: behind the radiator in the storeroom the projectionist has found a tin with no label. Film inside. Anyone who knows about film, please come by after the show.
city.reg.rassvet.10: Thank you to everyone who came. The tin is back in the storeroom, but now it has a label on the lid in big letters: "RASSVET. Do not lose." The film is no longer thought a made-up story but ours.
city.reg.rassvet.2: A pencilled note: the lid has one word on it, "Rassvet". Yes, like on our front. The projectionist says the house was named after this film, and everybody took the film for a made-up story.
city.reg.rassvet.3: The box office asks that nobody run the film on our projector: it is brittle, and the machine is meant for new stock. The argument in the buffet is still going.
city.reg.rassvet.4: The radio amateurs propose asking on the air whether anyone knows such a film. The club's call sign is on the card by the radio table, next to the mug.
city.reg.rassvet.5: An answer came at night on short wave from the next port: the film was shot here, on the pier, by the whole town, in 1931. The director left for the north before he could finish it.
city.reg.rassvet.6: The chess players found a poster from those years in the club archive: "Rassvet. Five reels. Live music." Live means the piano in the hall. The waltz from the poster has survived and the sheet is by the piano.
city.reg.rassvet.7: The projectionist rewound the film frame by frame, alone, in white gloves. Three reels of five are whole, the fourth is in shreds, the fifth is missing. He said even that is a lot.
city.reg.rassvet.8: The dance class has decided to learn the waltz from the poster. The teacher says the step is an old one and it needs two more couples. Come, if you can count to three.
city.reg.rassvet.9: It is decided: Rassvet is shown at one screening, from the front row, to anyone who comes and sits down. The ticket is thirty roubles, as always. The piano plays live, if there is somebody to play it.
city.reg.store.1: "At the lost and found: a yellow umbrella with a duck-head handle. Found in the records department. Owner please come to the first floor."
city.reg.store.2: "Yellow duck umbrella returned to its owner. Found again, in the fabrics department. Owner please come to the same place, first floor."
city.reg.store.3: "Dear owner of the yellow umbrella! The lost and found is open until 20:00. You may drop in just like that, without the umbrella."
city.reg.store.4: "Umbrella found in the toy department. The toy seller claims the duck on the handle winked at him. The seller has been given a day off."
city.reg.store.5: "The umbrella's owner has confessed she loses it on purpose: 'It's so nice to hear my name announced over the whole store.'"
city.reg.store.6: "At customers' request, lost-and-found announcements are now read over the radio twice. Slowly. With the name."
city.reg.store.7: "Nothing lost today. The lost and found will announce this over the radio at 12:00, just in case someone was waiting."
city.reg.tarelka.1: Pinned under the menu: "Lost: Kesha the parrot, green. Answers to 'Kesha' and to 'Mind the doors, please'. Finder gets a pastry on the house."
city.reg.tarelka.2: Below, in another hand: "Kesha was seen at Amber Shore station. Announcing the stops. Passengers pleased, the dispatcher less so."
city.reg.tarelka.3: "To cable-car passengers: if the cabin says 'Next stop, Lighthouse' and you're going to Zenith, it isn't the dispatcher. It's Kesha. Stay seated."
city.reg.tarelka.4: "Kesha spotted on the sanatorium roof. Shouting 'Sun! Sun!' The guests applauded; treatments ran half an hour late."
city.reg.tarelka.5: "Please don't try to catch Kesha with nets: he takes offence and stops announcing. Offer him sunflower seeds and say 'Terminus'."
city.reg.tarelka.6: "Kesha came back on his own. He sits on the coffee machine saying 'Terminus. Please vacate the cars.' He ate the pastry himself, too."
city.reg.tarelka.7: The last sheet, quite fresh: "Kesha asks you not to prompt him with station names. He already knows more than he should. Horizon, for example."
city.san.book.1: The guest book. "Arrival. Lunz V. S., 3-14. A voucher 'for the nerves'. I have no nerves, I have fingers that haven't played for a long time." A line below in other handwriting: "Aliyev G. R., 2-09, watchmaker. Being treated for retirement."
city.san.book.10: On the last page there is an empty field and a pencil note: "The notebook is on the piano. If you can, play it. If you cannot, just open it and see how it is written down. The clock in the pump room is running."
city.san.book.2: "There is a piano in the winter garden. A quarter tone out of tune, but kind. Played for half an hour, the receptionist did not mind. — V. L." Added: "Heard it in the pump room through the wall. Not a quarter tone, a half; don't be modest. — G. A."
city.san.book.3: "The clock over the pump-room door has stood at 4:10. I asked since when. They said: 'Since we started working here.' I request permission to look at it. — G. Aliyev." Below, a stamp: "Permitted. Just don't take it all the way apart."
city.san.book.4: "Guseyn Rashidovich plays chess by the dining-room window as if time ticked on his side. The score is 3:0 in his favour. I ask that it be counted a draw: he thinks aloud. — V. L."
city.san.book.5: "The pump-room clock is running. The spring was fine; it only lacked oil and respect. Vera Sergeyevna says it is now frightening to drink the water: at 4:10 it will stop being medicinal. — G. A."
city.san.book.6: "At Saturday's dance Guseyn Rashidovich trod on my foot during the waltz and said the metronome was to blame. There was no metronome in the hall. The waltz was lovely. — V. L."
city.san.book.7: "Vera Sergeyevna leaves on Saturday. I ask you to leave a music notebook on the winter-garden piano for her: I copied the Barcarolle from memory like a drawing, every bar labelled. Watchmakers write music like drawings. — G. A."
city.san.book.8: "Found the notebook on the piano. Every bar labelled like a gear. Played until supper without a single slip. In return I leave him a chess notebook: all our games written down, and in every one I mate him. Please do not show it until he leaves. — V. L."
city.san.book.9: The receptionist's entry: "Lunz and Aliyev checked out the same day, though they arrived on different days from different towns. Both hold tickets to the Lighthouse station. They asked us to leave the music notebook in the garden: 'Let whoever is not afraid play it.'"
city.san.book.prompt: E — leaf through the guest book
city.san.chess.1: A morning game, the pieces still cold. Someone left a game unfinished, black short of time. I make a move and do not know whose side I am playing.
city.san.chess.2: A game by the window. Opposite sits a guest in a panama hat with a magnifying glass: not because he sees badly, but because he is used to examining small things. I lose beautifully.
city.san.chess.3: Chess in the evening under the lamp. The pieces throw long shadows on the board and the rook looks like a lighthouse. I win, and by the third move I understand I was allowed to. Politely.
city.san.clock.1: The clock above the pump-room door has stopped. The hands are frozen at 4:10. Beneath it a plate: "Do not touch. Time is resting."
city.san.clock.2: A stepladder stands under the clock, and on a step lie a tiny screwdriver and a note: "Please do not move. G. A."
city.san.clock.3: The clock is down. On the sill, on a clean napkin, the cogs lie in order like pieces of a puzzle. An elderly guest whispers something to them and moves the smallest with tweezers.
city.san.clock.4: The clock is running! It ticks quietly and surely. A plate: "Running. Accurate. Checked by radio." Below someone added: "Now you can be late neither for the water nor for lunch."
city.san.court.1: The window looks onto the ring courtyard: a fountain with a white bowl, a round lawn and the windows opposite. In one a person waters geraniums, in another a towel with an embroidered sun is drying.
city.san.court.2: At night the courtyard is dark and round. The fountain whispers, three windows burn on different floors. Maybe someone there cannot sleep either and is looking at me.
city.san.evening.day: The lobby by day. The parquet by the door is polished to a shine, and on a little table by the wall a gramophone sits under its lid. A sign: "Dances and lectures in the evening. Programme at the reception."
city.san.evening.early: Evening is near. Guests drift into the lobby: some with a book, some with chess, some just to look at people.
city.san.evening.fri: Friday, tea with music. The gramophone plays old ballads, then a jazz band. Guests drink tea and discuss the weather, which is wonderful today, and of course that is their doing.
city.san.evening.late: The lobby at night: the parquet is dark, the gramophone sleeps under its lid. The night attendant leafs through a ledger and nods: "Quietly, please, people are resting."
city.san.evening.prompt: E — look in on the lobby evening
city.san.evening.sat1: Saturday dancing! The receptionist winds the gramophone and guests in indoor shoes circle on the parquet. A waltz, then a foxtrot, then another waltz, because they ask for it.
city.san.evening.sat2: I dance too: awkwardly at first, then however it goes. An elderly watchmaker leads his partner like an engineer building a bridge. She smiles: the bridge will hold.
city.san.evening.wed: Wednesday, the doctor's lecture "How to Sleep So That You Wake Rested". The listeners sit along the walls. The doctor says the main secret is not to think about sleep. Half the hall has already thought about sleep and fallen asleep.
city.san.garden_read.1: I settle into the armchair among the palms. The morning sun lays the window squares on the pages. I notice I am reading the same line for the third time: it is that pleasant.
city.san.garden_read.2: In the afternoon the garden is quiet and warm and smells of earth and tea. Somewhere in the pipes water murmurs. I read a chapter and dozed a little over the next one.
city.san.garden_read.3: In the evening one small lamp burns in the garden and the leaves on the panes look like ink blots. Reading is hard, but listening to the quiet is easy.
city.san.labels.1: A plate by the palm: "Fan palm. Called Galina Petrovna. Brought by train in 1974, travelled in the compartment with the conductor and complained of draughts. Please do not stroke the leaves."
city.san.labels.2: A plate: "Monstera. Name: Boris. Grown from a cutting a guest gave on leaving. The card said: 'Let it grow, since I cannot.'"
city.san.labels.3: A plate by the arch: "Ficus Semyon. The garden's oldest resident. His leaves are wiped with a damp cloth on Fridays, and he has never once complained."
city.san.labels.4: A plate: "Cacti Petya and Pasha. They flower once in three years, usually at night. Last time both bloomed at once, and the night attendant stood watch beside them till morning."
city.san.labels.5: A plate: "Fern. No name. Naming it has been proposed many times, but every guest proposes their own. On the list: Klava, Motya, Elvira and 'The one on the left'."
city.san.labels.6: A plate by the door: "It is always +22 in the winter garden. The plants are used to it, and so are the guests. If you feel cold, it is not the garden."
city.san.menu.fri: Menu, Friday. Pickle soup, meatballs in tomato, pasta, kefir for supper. The guests' opinion: the meatballs were better last week. The cook's opinion: it is the same every week.
city.san.menu.mon: Menu, Monday. Vegetable soup, steamed cutlet with mash, dried-fruit compote, a cabbage pie.
city.san.menu.sat: Menu, Saturday: festive lunch. Cold kefir soup, chicken Kiev, a 'potato' chocolate cake. There is dancing after lunch, so be careful with the cake.
city.san.menu.sun: Menu, Sunday. Pancakes with sour cream and jam in the morning, chicken broth, a bake, tea with lemon. Second helpings come without questions.
city.san.menu.thu: Menu, Thursday. Cabbage soup, chicken pilaf, beetroot salad, compote. The pilaf is made by a cook who sailed as a ship's cook on a freighter before the sanatorium.
city.san.menu.tue: Menu, Tuesday. Borscht (sour cream only on a doctor's prescription), fish in marinade, buckwheat, tea.
city.san.menu.wed: Menu, Wednesday: fish day. Fish soup, pike-perch with potatoes, cranberry kissel. Whoever dislikes fish gets an apple and sympathy.
city.san.oxygen.1: The white cylinder hissed and the glass filled with pink foam to the brim. It tastes like a cloud with raspberry. My head went light and a little giddy.
city.san.oxygen.2: The cocktail came in a tall glass: foam on top, raspberry syrup underneath. A sign: "No more than two a day: after the third you start talking to the flowers."
city.san.quartz.1: The doctor gave me dark goggles and told me not to look at the lamp. I want to look anyway: it is blue and hums softly like a hive. After five minutes I was warm, as after the sea.
city.san.quartz.2: The lamp came on with a click. "No more than ten minutes," said the doctor, "and don't fall asleep." I didn't. Almost.
city.san.quartz.3: Under the lamp my skin glows and my head goes quiet. The doctor explains it is good for the joints, the mood and 'generally'. 'Generally' is the key word of medicine.
city.san.quartz.4: The goggles sit funnily, like an aviator's. In the wall mirror I see a patient in blue light who looks far healthier than I do.
city.san.quartz.prompt: E — sit under the quartz lamp
city.san.radio.1: The radio at the head of the couch plays dance music quietly. The announcer reads the forecast: south-west wind, sea state two, mood excellent.
city.san.radio.2: At night the radio plays under its breath: first a waltz, then a lullaby, then the time signals. A good accompaniment for counting sheep and waiting for morning.
city.san.reg.1: A new notice: "Please do not close the lid of the winter-garden piano. The instrument has to breathe, and in the evenings it is opened for playing."
city.san.reg.2: "The pump-room clock has stopped. The repairman has been called three times: he comes, looks and leaves with a sad face. The healing water runs on schedule regardless."
city.san.reg.3: "Dancing in the lobby on Saturdays at 19:00. Bring indoor shoes, records and a good mood. Trodden feet are a matter for your partner, not the receptionist."
city.san.reg.4: "Wednesdays at 18:00, the doctor's lecture 'How to Sleep So That You Wake Rested'. Free entry. Please do not leave until the lecturer wakes up." The last sentence is crossed out but still readable.
city.san.reg.5: "Found: a chess rook, either ivory or very good plastic. It waits for its owner in the receptionist's drawer. The owner is asked first to say what colour it is."
city.san.reg.6: "The pump-room clock is running! Please do not touch the hands, and do not be late: it shows now." Next to it another: "Thanks to G. R. Aliyev from the staff and from the water."
city.san.reg.7: "V. S. Lunz and G. R. Aliyev have checked out. A notebook of music is left on the winter-garden piano. Request: do not take it away, play it. The management."
city.san.regime.1: "Daily regime. Morning: 7:30 exercises, 8:00 thermometer and weighing, 8:30 breakfast." Underneath, by hand: "Whoever slept through exercises slept through them with pleasure."
city.san.regime.2: "Daily regime. Before lunch: 9:00 pump room, first glass (small sips), 10:00 treatments as prescribed, 11:00 oxygen cocktail, 12:00 a walk along the promenade. Heal without hurry."
city.san.regime.3: "Daily regime. 13:00 lunch. 14:00 quiet hour." The word "quiet" is underlined twice, and beside it someone has drawn a kettle and written: "Shhh."
city.san.regime.4: "Daily regime. 15:30 second glass at the pump room, 16:00 afternoon snack, 17:00 chess, books, letters home, 18:00 free time: the sea, a bench or the clouds, your choice."
city.san.regime.5: "Daily regime. 19:00 supper. 20:00 evening in the lobby: a doctor's lecture on Wednesdays, tea with music on Fridays, dancing on Saturdays. The other evenings are quiet, as they should be."
city.san.regime.6: "Daily regime. 22:00 lights out. Silence in the corridors, silence in the pump room, silence on the piano." In small letters below: "The night attendant stays awake and will tell nobody who went for water."
city.san.trolley.1: On the trolley are books left by guests: a coverless Martin Eden, three crosswords filled in with pencil to the last square, a cookbook with a jam stain on the pancake page.
city.san.trolley.2: Someone's bookmark in Martin Eden: a cable-car ticket. Yesterday's date. So the reader is still here, with about fifteen pages left.
city.san.trolley.3: A book about sea salt: "Salt is the only stone that people eat." In the margin in pencil: "Checked. True."
city.san.trolley.4: A 1979 issue of the magazine Health, the article "How Not to Fear the Doctor". Someone circled the title and wrote: "Didn't help, but it was fun."
city.san.trolley.5: A thin booklet, "Reading Music in One Evening". The pages are worn through, with fingers and numbers drawn in the margins. On the cover, a signature: "V. L."
city.san.trolley.6: A book of chess problems. A slip is tucked into page 41: "Mate in three. Guseyn Rashidovich, it can be solved. Don't be cross." Below, a crossed-out answer: "No peeking."
city.sch.bag.1: Behind the mats in the corner hides a blue bag. The strap is worn, "L.K." in ink on the side, a sneaker's sole sticking out of the pocket. Found it, it seems.
city.sch.bag.2: The bag smells of rubber and a banana that has probably lived here since Friday. The sneakers inside: one laced, one not. The owner was in a hurry.
city.sch.bag.3: I put the bag on the bench by the gym door where it can be seen. Someone will collect it.
city.sch.bbio.1: On the board, a heart with four chambers in chalk. Two are labelled; the other two say "we'll sort it out."
city.sch.bbio.2: On the board, the structure of a leaf: stalk, veins, green arrows everywhere. At the bottom: "Whoever picked a leaf off the ficus knows."
city.sch.bbio.3: No biology today. On the board, yesterday's skeleton in a funny pose, and someone has drawn it a hat.
city.sch.bbio.4: In the empty room the board says only: "Water the plants! Duty pupils." The plants, by the way, are alive.
city.sch.bell.1: I rang it so loudly that three heads looked out from behind a classroom door at once. First lesson: don't be late.
city.sch.bell.2: I rang in the middle of a lesson. A teacher looked out of the nearest door, regarded me, and quietly shut it. She said nothing, but she will remember.
city.sch.bell.3: The bell ran as an echo through the emptying corridors. Somebody laughed far away: "You again!"
city.sch.bell.4: In an empty school the bell sounds different, longer than by day. I put it back and went on tiptoe.
city.sch.coats.1: The racks are stuffed: checked jackets, a red coat with an embroidered hare, three hats on one hook. Under the bench, a brood of indoor shoes.
city.sch.coats.2: The hooks are nearly empty. On one hangs a forgotten scarf, long and striped, smelling of autumn. It waits for its owner.
city.sch.coats.3: The empty cloakroom smells of wet wool and cooling radiators. Only the scarf on its hook has not lost hope.
city.sch.concert.1: Poster: "On Saturday at 15:00 in the gym, the school concert. Everyone who failed to hide will sing. Performing: a girl from 8A (piano), the spoon orchestra of 5B."
city.sch.concert.2: A handwritten addition: "The Song about the Sea needs a second pianist. Rehearsals every day after sixth period. Metronome provided."
city.sch.duty.1: The school duty log. Entries in a column: "8:10 opened the doors. 8:25 Petrov late, but with flowers. 9:40 the pointer broke in 5A; the pointer was mended."
city.sch.duty.2: "Remarks: a blue bag with gym shoes has gone missing from the cloakroom. Please check the lost-and-found box." Beside it: "Checked already. No."
city.sch.duty.3: "Duty rules: greet at the door, keep shoes off the wet floor, answer the bell on time, answer questions politely." Someone has added: "and patiently."
city.sch.duty.4: On the last page, in a child's hand: "If you're on duty, don't panic. The bell doesn't bite." Next to it, a drawing of a bell with teeth.
city.sch.globe.1: The globe creaks on its axis. My finger stopped on the Pacific, where, as usual, there is not a single town.
city.sch.globe.2: I looked for our bay on the globe. Or rather for the place where it ought to be: no Lyudmilovsk, not even a dot. The scale let us down.
city.sch.globe.3: I spun it too hard: Africa merged with Antarctica and Australia turned into a rainbow for a second. I braked with my palm.
city.sch.globe.4: Under the stand a slip of paper: "Do not spin during tests." The paper has yellowed, so the rule is old and our parents broke it too.
city.sch.herb.1: Herbarium of 7A: daisy, clover, plantain, a maple leaf with veins drawn on. Calligraphic labels; the plantain's has two spelling mistakes.
city.sch.herb.2: A frame with eelgrass thrown up on the beach by a storm. The card: "Zostera. Collected by Katya L. after the storm of 14 October. Still smells."
city.sch.herb.3: A pine twig with a cone and a tiny dried mushroom. Beneath: "For the lesson on the forest. Do not eat the mushroom."
city.sch.herb.4: An empty frame with a card: "What you find will go here. Do not pick anything protected."
city.sch.lesson.1: Monday, geography. The teacher ran her pointer along our own coast and asked for three towns starting with L. I named two and nearly named the one we were sitting in.
city.sch.lesson.2: Tuesday, literature. We read aloud from Turgenev's night in the meadow. The girl in front read so quietly that even the radiators fell silent.
city.sch.lesson.3: Wednesday, physics. The teacher hung a weight on a thread and said: "Watch how everything comes back." It swung, and we counted the swings and kept losing count.
city.sch.lesson.4: Thursday, history. We heard about the old port. Where our seafront is now, nets used to dry, and every house had its own little jetty.
city.sch.lesson.5: Friday, drawing. We had to draw what we could see from the window. I drew a seagull. My deskmate said it came out as a potato, but a contented one.
city.sch.lesson.6: The first lesson. The room smells of chalk and wet jackets; everyone is still a little asleep with their eyes open.
city.sch.lesson.7: The last lesson. The clock hands crawl a centimetre at a time while the sun is already out strolling. The teacher pretends not to notice our glances.
city.sch.lesson.8: A lesson like any lesson: a squared notebook, a faded blotter and somebody's note: "don't copy from Misha, he doesn't know either."
city.sch.lost.1: The lost-and-found: a mitten (left), a mitten (right, another colour), a seventh-grade geography book bookmarked at the Pacific. The things wait for owners with the patience of old toys.
city.sch.lost.2: Also an unpaired slipper, a spectacle case, a bobble hat and a note: "If the hat is yours, tell us the shape of the bobble."
city.sch.lost.3: No blue gym bag here. But a note is pinned to the box: "Lyosha K., 6B, look in the gym, not here: that's where you last jumped."
city.sch.lost.4: At the bottom: a pencil, a comb and a photograph of an unknown cat. Photographs are what is left in the box most often. Nobody comes for them.
city.sch.mboard.1: A staff in chalk: a clef, four bars and the title "Song about the Sea." Over the third bar a fat question mark.
city.sch.mboard.2: At the bottom: "We take breath from the belly, not from the ears." Next to it, a smiling belly.
city.sch.mboard.3: A notice: "Choir: Tuesday and Thursday after sixth period. Spoon orchestra: as the mood takes it."
city.sch.menu.1: Monday's menu: pea soup, a cutlet with mash, dried-fruit compote. In the corner in chalk: "Bread: unlimited."
city.sch.menu.2: Tuesday: borscht, navy-style pasta, kissel. Today's kissel is so thick the spoon stands up by itself.
city.sch.menu.3: Wednesday is fish day: pickle soup, fish and potatoes, tea. The seagulls have already gathered in the yard with serious faces.
city.sch.menu.4: Thursday: cabbage soup, goulash with buckwheat, compote. Someone added: "Lyudmilovsk-style goulash." Nobody knows what that means.
city.sch.menu.5: Friday: vermicelli soup, cheese pancakes with sour cream, cocoa. Two pancakes per person. Buffet: pies, buns, kefir, apples.
city.sch.menu.6: No menu is written for the weekend: the canteen is closed and the board is wiped squeaky clean. Only a little drawn plate is left in the corner.
city.sch.metro.1: Tick. Tick. Tick. The weight swings to and fro like the pendulum of very calm clocks. It makes you want to breathe in time.
city.sch.metro.2: I slid the weight up: the metronome bustled as if it were late. I slid it down: it sighed and waddled along.
city.sch.metro.3: On the lid are scratched "adagio" and "don't touch if you can't." I can only listen. I listened.
city.sch.p.board: E — see what is on the board
city.sch.p.lost: E — rummage in the lost-and-found box
city.sch.p.tea: E — take a glass of tea
city.sch.recital.1: I stepped to the edge of the stage. The hall is empty but the chairs are set out, which is somehow scarier than a full house. I said "hello." The echo said: "...llo."
city.sch.recital.2: I read two quatrains about the sea aloud. At the second, somebody clapped softly from behind the curtain. I turned: no one, only the curtain swaying.
city.sch.recital.3: I took an imaginary microphone and announced: "The Song about the Sea. Performed by the entire coast." I bowed. So did the echo.
city.sch.reg.1: Wall newspaper "Young Lyudmilovsker." Urgent: on Friday after PE a blue bag with gym shoes went missing. Owner: Lyosha K., 6B. A finder gets thanks in the paper and a glass of tea.
city.sch.reg.10: A new notice: a red ball has gone missing from the gym. We assert nothing, but we advise looking under the mats.
city.sch.reg.11: The editors' conclusion of the week: everything in a school turns up, you just have to stop hurrying.
city.sch.reg.2: Column "You asked, we answer": "Why is there no ice cream in the buffet?" Answer: "Because winter starts before summer ends." The editors ask you not to cry.
