city.sch.reg.3: The editors have investigated. Questioned: the cloakroom attendant, the duty pupil, the geranium on the sill. It turns out the bag is not in the cloakroom. The search goes on.
city.sch.reg.4: The PE teacher declared that the bag "was definitely there the last time I saw it." The pupils' council formed a search party of two people and one draught.
city.sch.reg.5: Music page. We are preparing the "Song about the Sea" for Saturday's concert. A pianist is needed: the spoon orchestra cannot manage the accompaniment. Ask in the music room.
city.sch.reg.6: The bag hunt: checked the lost-and-found (mitten, mitten, textbook), the cloakroom, the corridor. The gym is not fully searched: the mats are heavy and Lyosha is afraid to look.
city.sch.reg.7: Lyosha K. goes to PE in his socks. The teacher allowed it but asks him not to step on the draughts. The editors wish Lyosha warm weather and somebody's dry sneakers.
city.sch.reg.8: Good news: the bag has been found! It was behind the mats in the gym. Somebody who gave no name brought it to the duty pupil. Lyosha promises never to leave his shoes lying about. We ask the unknown helper to come for a glass of tea.
city.sch.reg.9: The concert took place: the "Song about the Sea" was played twice, the second time at the cloakroom attendant's request. The pianist came out without sheet music and made no mistakes. Almost.
city.sch.run.1: A PE lesson: two lines, a whistle, and the class jogs round the hall. I tagged on at the back and nobody noticed an extra.
city.sch.run.2: After lessons the hall belongs to the club: balls thud, sneakers squeak. I jogged along the edge without getting in the way and got a nod from the coach.
city.sch.run.3: A day off: the hall is draughty and smells of floor polish. The floor is waxed so well you only want to run in socks.
city.sch.run.4: The evening hall is huge and dark. You run and hear only your own steps, with the echo failing to keep up.
city.sch.scope.1: Under the glass, a slice of geranium leaf: green cells stand in even bricks, like our school's wall.
city.sch.scope.2: A fly's leg from the collection: so many hairs that the magnification felt almost impolite.
city.sch.scope.3: The little mirror catches the lamp's light. Somebody left a drop from the aquarium on the slide: unhurried beads drift through it.
city.sch.score.1: The board is frozen at "7 : 5." The girls of 7B are beating the boys, and the PE teacher pretends to referee fairly.
city.sch.score.2: After lessons the board says "0 : 0": basketball club has not started, but someone is already bouncing a ball.
city.sch.score.3: A day off. The board shows "0 : 0," as if the match was put off until Monday.
city.sch.score.4: In the evening the board is dark; the digits only glimmer in the windows. The score is whatever it was.
city.sch.tea.1: The big break. Thick tea with lemon peel comes out of the urn; the duty teacher pours it into a faceted glass and nods: "Just don't run."
city.sch.tea.2: The queue has melted away. The tea in the urn is the colour of old copper, but still hot, and the glass is warm as a mitten.
city.sch.tea.3: The urn is cooling and clicking quietly. Nobody is pouring tea right now.
city.sch.tray.1: Put the tray on the trolley. Spoons in the glass, plates in a stack: the paper on the wall says so, and so does common decency.
city.sch.tray.2: On the top shelf: somebody's unfinished crust and a pencilled note: "Duty pupils, it wasn't me." I didn't investigate.
city.sch.tray.3: The trolley rolled a little: one wheel has a mind of its own. Someone nodded from the serving hatch: a good lad.
city.sch.tt.1: Timetable, Monday: 1. Russian, 2. geography, 3. maths, 4. music, 5. PE. At the bottom in red: "Don't forget your gym shoes!"
city.sch.tt.2: Tuesday: 1. literature, 2. algebra, 3. biology, 4. English, 5. drawing.
city.sch.tt.3: Wednesday: 1. physics, 2. algebra, 3. history, 4. PE, 5. form period. Physics, they say, always sways a little.
city.sch.tt.4: Thursday: 1. history, 2. Russian, 3. chemistry, 4. music, 5. crafts. In crafts the boys go to the workshop and the girls to the kitchen, then the other way round.
city.sch.tt.5: Friday: 1. maths, 2. literature, 3. biology, 4. drawing, 5. double PE. The last bell is at 13:40.
city.sch.tt.6: Saturday and Sunday are not in the timetable. Someone has pencilled under the table: "Thank goodness."

city.story.kiosk1.prices.1: "Evening paper 5 rub. Cosmos and Us 40. Shores 40. Postcard 4. Fresh news after lunch, yesterday's at a discount."
city.story.kiosk1.prices.2: Under the glass, a list headed "Asked for but out of stock": "a magazine about cats", "today's weather for tomorrow", "a letter from my son".
city.story.kiosk1.prices.3: In chalk on the side: "The crossword in Friday's issue is hard. 14 down is 'tide'. Don't mention it."
city.story.kiosk2.freezer.1: The freezer glass has misted up from inside. Someone drew a sun on it with a finger, and it's slowly thawing.
city.story.kiosk2.freezer.2: The cups lie in rows like toy soldiers in a box. Winter breathes out of the chest, though outside it's July.
city.story.kiosk2.freezer.3: At the bottom of the chest, a lonely ice lolly from last summer, furred with frost like a coat. Nobody seems to have the heart to sell it.
city.story.kiosk2.freezer.prompt: E — look into the freezer chest
city.story.kiosk2.prices.1: "Plombir in a cup 28 rub. Buratino, Duchesse 18. Water 20. Ice cream doesn't melt if you eat it fast."
city.story.kiosk2.prices.2: At the bottom of the price list, in a child's hand: "Can I have two scoops?" Underneath, in a grown-up's: "Yes. If it's very hot."
city.story.kiosk2.prices.3: "On sale today: sun, free; shade under the awning, also free. Ice cream, for money."
city.story.kiosk3.prices.1: "Skvorets cigarettes 35 rub. Lighters 10. Seeds 10. Under-sixteens: seeds and good advice only."
city.story.kiosk3.prices.2: On the counter, a shell-shaped ashtray and a sign: "No smoking here. Thinking allowed."
city.story.kiosk3.prices.3: Over the hatch, a faded poster: a smoker whose lungs are two grey clouds. Under it someone has added: "Lovely weather, though."
city.story.kiosk4.buckets.1: Buckets of water, and in them carnations, daisies and one big sprig of dog rose, clearly picked on the way to work.
city.story.kiosk4.buckets.2: It smells of wet stems and a little of the sea. The sunflowers stand apart, facing south, like people at a bus stop.
city.story.kiosk4.buckets.3: In the last bucket, a single daisy with its petals plucked. Someone was asking it. From the look of it, the answer was "loves me".
city.story.kiosk4.prices.1: "Carnation 3 rub., daisies 5 a bunch, sunflower 7, dog rose not for sale, it's mine."
city.story.kiosk4.prices.2: Under the prices: "Bouquets for weddings, graduations and making up. Making up at a discount."
city.story.kiosk4.prices.3: In chalk: "Flowers arrive Thursday. Or Friday. Flowers aren't a bus."
city.story.kiosk4.talk.1: "The tulips are sad today, don't take them. Take the daisies, they're silly and cheerful. Though it's look-only: they haven't sent us anything to sell yet."
city.story.kiosk4.talk.2: The flower seller trims stems and tells me the sunflowers turn to the kiosk window every morning. "They think I'm the sun. I don't argue."
city.story.kiosk4.talk.3: "A bouquet for a girl? For your mum? For yourself? For yourself is the best kind. Come back when they're in and I'll make you one."
city.story.kiosk4.talk.4: A note on the counter: "Anahit! Don't put the buckets out till it's dark: the lilac is afraid of the sun." Signed: "Ales, evening shift."
city.story.kiosk5.prices.1: "Cable-car pin: next door at kiosk No. 1. Information 0 rub. More information, also 0. Advice on where to go: depends on my mood."
city.story.kiosk5.prices.2: Under the glass, a photo: a cabin over the sea at dawn, all pink. Caption: "6:04. Empty. Beautiful, though."
city.story.kiosk5.prices.3: "Children, pensioners and first-timers get a window seat. Everyone else too: it's all windows in there."
city.story.kiosk5.talk.1: "A cable-car ticket? You pay in the cabin; we only give information. Ask away: where, when and why. 'Why' is free."
city.story.kiosk5.talk.2: "Twelve minutes to Zenith if the wind doesn't argue. If it does, the cabin sways, a free ride on top."
city.story.kiosk5.talk.3: The information clerk leafs through a thick exercise book: "Passengers' Questions". The last one: "Why do the cabins never meet in the middle?" No answer.
city.story.kiosk5.talk.4: "The last cabin to the Lighthouse leaves at sunset. Not by the timetable, by the sun. The operator decided, and nobody objected."
city.story.kiosk5.timetable.1: "Cable car. Akademgorodok to Aton. Amber Shore to Zenith. Lighthouse. Interval: as long as the cabin is visible from the window."
city.story.kiosk5.timetable.2: The route map is drawn by hand in coloured pencils. Horizon and Polar Star are dotted in and labelled: "Only in dreams, for now."
city.story.kiosk5.timetable.3: "The cable car does not run in a thunderstorm. In a rainbow it runs, but slower, so everyone has time to look."
city.story.kiosk5.timetable.4: Added in pencil: "Whoever left a knitted mitten in cabin No. 7: it's been riding back and forth since Monday. It likes it."
city.story.kiosk6.prices.1: "Key 6 rub. Zip 10. Heel tips 8. Watches: depending on the watch's state of mind."
city.story.kiosk6.prices.2: "Urgent repairs: tomorrow. Very urgent: the day after; it needs thinking about."
city.story.kiosk6.prices.3: Clocks on the wall, each showing a different time. A sign underneath: "The right one is third from the left. Probably."
city.story.kiosk6.talk.1: The repairman doesn't look up from a watch movement. "Put it on the counter. What's broken? It'll mend itself? Then why are you here?" I've nothing to mend, and he seems pleased about that.
city.story.kiosk6.talk.2: "I cut keys, replace zips, treat watches. A heart? No, hearts go to the clinic. Though people do bring them to me sometimes."
city.story.kiosk6.talk.3: The hatch has a "Lunch" sign. The repairman sits right there eating and looking at me. "'Lunch' doesn't mean I'm not here. It means I'm eating."
city.story.kiosk6.talk.4: "A watch that runs fast is better than one that runs slow," says the repairman. "At least it wants to get somewhere."
city.story.kiosk6.tray.1: A tray of things mended but never collected: an alarm clock, an umbrella, one sandal. Each has a dated tag. The alarm clock has been waiting since spring.
city.story.kiosk6.tray.2: A bunch of keys with no tag. The repairman says they're keys "to everything that came before". He'll give them to whoever remembers what they open.
city.story.kiosk6.tray.3: A pocket watch engraved "To L. from L." It ticks loudly, as if in a hurry to be collected.
city.story.photo_desk.1: The photographer wipes a lens and squints at me. "You've got a face for a portrait. Not for a passport, for a portrait. Sit on the stool."
city.story.photo_desk.2: Envelopes of finished prints on the desk, a surname on each. One just says: "The boy who was looking at the sea." Not mine. Not yet.
city.story.photo_desk.3: "A portrait is sixty, ready on Thursday. Stick it in your diary and it'll show you were here," says the photographer, surprised at how that sounded.
city.story.photo_desk.4: Behind the desk, prints dry on pegs: weddings, school leavers, an old man with a dog. Everyone is squinting, as if he'd shot straight into the sun.
city.story.sanatorium_night.1: The receptionist took the money, handed me a towel with a little sun embroidered on it and made up the couch in the treatment room. "Breakfast at eight; we won't wake you."
city.story.sanatorium_night.2: All night mineral water murmured in the pipes behind the wall like a distant stream. I dreamt I was drinking it and turning transparent.
city.story.sanatorium_night.3: I woke at seven exactly, when the sun reached the pillow. Everyone here seems to wake that way.
city.story.sanatorium_night.4: In the night the duty nurse looked in with a torch, tucked my blanket in and tiptoed away. As if I were here for treatment. Maybe I am.
city.story.sanatorium_night.prompt: E — stay the night at the sanatorium
city.t3.stove.prompt: E — throw water on the stones
city.t3.t3_bars.1: The girls lined up at the wall bars: "legs higher, point your toes." I hung to one side, didn't point my toes, but tried.
city.t3.t3_bars.2: The rungs are warm from somebody's hands. I pulled my legs up to my stomach and held until they shook. The coach calls it an "L-sit," my stomach has another word.
city.t3.t3_bars.3: I hung at the very top and counted the windows. There are so many in the hall that I lost count twice. I liked losing count.
city.t3.t3_bike.1: In the morning the sea outside is a grey blanket. I pedalled and chased it to the very horizon. The horizon didn't give in.
city.t3.t3_bike.2: By day gulls pass the window, and a little ship behind them. The ship and I keep the same pace. I won't overtake it: it seems to be going to Sweden.
city.t3.t3_bike.3: In the evening the lighthouse comes on in the window. Every turn of the pedals, one flash. I counted to forty and lost it.
city.t3.t3_bike.4: At night the window shows only my own outline: a boy on a bicycle that goes nowhere. The boy is very determined.
city.t3.t3_changing.1: Behind the screen it's cramped but cosy: a hook, a mirror with a chipped corner and somebody's socks with kittens. The socks aren't mine, but I like them.
city.t3.t3_changing.2: Changed in three moves and spent three more on the laces. The laces won on a draw.
city.t3.t3_changing.3: The screen is a fabric with a pattern like grandma's sofa. You change and feel like a guest.
city.t3.t3_club_board.1: "Sections: basketball, gymnastics, weights, painting, pottery studio. Sign up with the coach, entry free, socks your own."
city.t3.t3_club_board.2: "Young Marine Painters" circle: Saturday, 11:00. Please bring your own eyes and old shirts: shirts will do for aprons.
city.t3.t3_club_board.3: COURTYARD TOURNAMENT "GOLDEN BALL" on Saturday! The "Surf Juniors" need a fifth player. Skill at shooting is optional.
city.t3.t3_club_board.4: "Surf Juniors" line-up: Lyosha, Taya, Ramil, Vanya and... The fifth line is in pencil: "somebody." "Somebody" is underlined twice.
city.t3.t3_club_board.5: Practice before the tournament: every day at five except Sunday. Late: an extra lap. On time: tea in the buffet (tea is not free).
city.t3.t3_club_board.6: Kit for the "Surf Juniors" is handed out at the till. Jersey No. 5 is free. Size: "still growing."
city.t3.t3_club_board.7: The tournament is on the hall's court, Saturday at 15:00. Fans: seats on the benches. Don't catch the balls. Catch the mood.
city.t3.t3_club_board.8: "SURF JUNIORS: SECOND PLACE!" The team thanks the coach, the buffet lady for the tea, and "number five" for turning up. The certificate is waiting at the till.
city.t3.t3_coach.1: "New here? The hall opens at seven, the sections are on the timetable by the door. Found a free ball? Shoot. Just not at the windows: they cost me more than the balls."
city.t3.t3_coach.10: "Second place is when you're glad and cross at once, and both halves are right. Taya is telling the whole courtyard about your shot. One more time?"
city.t3.t3_coach.2: "You've been around a few days now. I noticed: you come in like it's a job. Good. Sport loves the ones who show up on a boring Tuesday."
city.t3.t3_coach.3: "I hear you were shooting from the far line. Missed, but with a face like you'd scored. In basketball that's half the job. The other half is scoring."
city.t3.t3_coach.4: "Not now, the boys are warming up. Come over when I blow the last whistle."
city.t3.t3_coach.5: "Quiet, the girls are counting their jumps. If anyone loses count they start over, and I'm the one who has to listen."
city.t3.t3_coach.6: "Listen, "Surf Juniors" have a courtyard tournament and there are only four of us. Vova moved away with his parents, his ball stayed behind. Want to be the fifth? Running is optional. Standing there and not getting in the way is a must."
city.t3.t3_coach.7: "Come to practice at five. The hoop on the back wall is for people who mean to play, not pose for photos."
city.t3.t3_coach.8: "Good that you keep coming. The number-five jersey is at the till, locker five is free. Just don't wipe your face on it: there's one jersey and a lot of faces."
city.t3.t3_coach.9: "Game day. Stick close to Taya: she reads the court better than I read the paper. The rest will sort itself out."
city.t3.t3_court.1: The tournament! Lyosha passed me the ball and the hall suddenly went quiet, as if everyone were waiting for me to do something. I did: I shot. The ball knocked twice on the rim and dropped in. Taya shrieked so that the glasses in the buffet shook.
city.t3.t3_court.2: The Seagulls pressed from all sides. Ramil cut right, Taya took the rebound, and I stood under the hoop and waited. And got what I waited for: the ball came into my hands by itself. We lost the final by one point, but they clapped for us too.
city.t3.t3_court.3: The court after the tournament: sweet wrappers, chalk, somebody's hairpin. The fans' ribbon is still hanging on the hoop.
city.t3.t3_court.4: Two on two: me and Taya against Ramil and Lyosha. We lost 6 to 10. Taya said it was a warm-up and I believed her, with relief.
city.t3.t3_court.5: A scrimmage to ten. I scored two, Lyosha scored eight and apologised a lot. All of this is for the tournament.
city.t3.t3_court.6: On Sunday the five don't meet: everyone has families, grannies, lunches. I dribbled alone on the empty court. The ball obeyed well.
city.t3.t3_easel_lighthouse.1: The lighthouse in the morning is pale as a candle in a sunny room. I painted almost without colour, only white, and it began to glow from inside.
city.t3.t3_easel_lighthouse.2: By day the lighthouse is just a red-and-white tower. I painted a tower and got a chimney. I wrote "Lighthouse" under it. The caption helped.
city.t3.t3_easel_lighthouse.3: At sunset the lighthouse turns pink and its shadow lies all the way to the pier. I spent longer on the shadow than on the tower.
city.t3.t3_easel_lighthouse.4: At night the lighthouse is all about the beam. I painted it in yellow on dark, and the canvas seemed to warm up a little.
city.t3.t3_easel_sea.1: The morning sea is grey as pearl: grey, pink and a little green. I painted with a wet brush and the sea came out wet.
city.t3.t3_easel_sea.2: By day the sea is blue and there's never enough blue. I painted until it looked like a postcard and was upset. The studio leader said: "Somebody paints the postcards too."
city.t3.t3_easel_sea.3: In the evening the sea is gold, then copper, then dark. I couldn't mix paints fast enough: the sea changed faster than the brush.
city.t3.t3_easel_sea.4: At night I painted the sea from memory, by lamplight: black, with a moon path. The leader said: "The night sea isn't painted with the eyes." What with, he didn't say.
city.t3.t3_easel_teacher.1: The teacher's easel: a big canvas with a charcoal sketch: a pier, gulls, a boy in a hood. The boy has no face yet.
city.t3.t3_easel_teacher.2: The teacher has put paint on the pier: a peach sky, a steel sea. The boy still has no face but stands more firmly.
city.t3.t3_easel_teacher.3: The boy has got a face. I look at him and try not to think that it's a little familiar.
city.t3.t3_easel_teacher.4: The canvas is signed and stands by the door with a note: "Hang in the foyer." The boy looks at the sea. Now at the sea, not at me.
city.t3.t3_glaze.1: On the bench, jars of glaze: "green," "blue," "do not touch." "Do not touch" is the prettiest. Nothing to touch until Thursday: the bowls haven't been fired yet.
city.t3.t3_glaze.2: I glazed bowl No. 7: green, with a little blue on the bottom. The potter warned me: in the jar the glaze is one colour, out of the kiln it will be another. Like people.
city.t3.t3_glaze.3: The bench is tidied, the jars are shut. On the newspaper, the print of a bowl's foot: someone checked whether it stands level.
city.t3.t3_glaze.4: The bench is empty, only the "do not touch" jar stands at the edge. I didn't touch it. Apparently I'm growing up.
city.t3.t3_hoop_free.1: The west hoop is warmed up by morning: the sun comes through the window right onto the backboard. I aimed at the patch of sunlight. I hit it more often than the hoop.
city.t3.t3_hoop_free.2: It's quiet at the west wall: people come here who aren't ready for spectators yet. I became one of them. Two in a row, and at once I wished someone were watching.
city.t3.t3_hoop_free.3: By evening the floor creaks louder and the ball bounces more cheerfully. I shot until the shadow of the hoop crept to the middle of the hall.
city.t3.t3_hoop_main.1: A practice is under way at the back wall: five boys, three balls, one whistle. They put me on rebounds. I rebounded honestly and even returned a ball to whoever threw it.
city.t3.t3_hoop_main.2: At the back wall the girls practise shots from under the hoop and count aloud. I stood beside them and shot in time: scored on "seventeen."
city.t3.t3_hoop_main.3: In the morning the hoop is mine. The cleaner was wiping the lines, and the ball left dusty marks on them: exactly as many as my misses.
city.t3.t3_hoop_main.4: In the evening the light over the hoop is warm, like in a film about champions. Ten shots, no spectators, I clapped for myself.
city.t3.t3_hoop_main.5: On Saturdays it's courtyard against courtyard here. They took me "for five minutes." It turned out to be twenty.
city.t3.t3_hoop_main.6: On Sunday there's a grandfather and grandson at the hoop. Grandpa teaches shooting "from the chest," the boy says "from the heart." The boy, by the way, scored.
city.t3.t3_kiln.1: The kiln is cold. On the shelf beside it, raw bowls, grey as mice. You can't pick them up: they'd crumble from a glance.
city.t3.t3_kiln.2: The kiln hums and smells evenly of warm brick. Through the peephole, orange light. A note: "Firing. Do not open. Do not knock. Peek no more than three times."
city.t3.t3_kiln.3: The kiln has cooled. The door is ajar, inside white cups with a pink tinge. One has cracked. The potter says: "That's not a flaw, that's character."
city.t3.t3_kiln.4: The second firing, with glaze. A red peephole, a quiet hum. On the kiln, in chalk, a number: 1060.
city.t3.t3_kiln.5: The kiln is open and the finished ware is inside! It shines like wet stones. Bowl No. 7 is green as the sea on a grey day, with two blue specks.
city.t3.t3_kiln.6: The kiln is resting, like everyone. Warm to the touch. On the floor, crumbs of glaze, green and light blue.
city.t3.t3_lockers.1: Lockers by number. On No. 7 someone scratched: "Do not open until victory." The door opens, so there must have been one.
city.t3.t3_lockers.2: On door No. 3 there's a fish sticker and a note: "Slippers live here. Do not feed."
city.t3.t3_lockers.3: A new paper on locker No. 5: "Free. For the fifth." In the coach's handwriting, pressed hard.
city.t3.t3_lockers.4: Locker No. 5 stands open. Inside, a jersey with a five and a note on the hook: "Size: still growing. Don't lose it."
city.t3.t3_lockers.5: On locker No. 5 my name has been added in chalk. Chalk, so it's easy to wipe off. It doesn't come off: I tried with my sleeve.
city.t3.t3_mats.1: On the mats the girls do the "bridge" and the "birch." Mine came out more of a "stump." Lidia Pavlovna said: "A stump is a tree too."
city.t3.t3_mats.2: The mats are warm after the gymnasts. I lay down and looked at the ceiling: a cobweb shaped like a constellation. I named it the Vaulting Horse.
city.t3.t3_pool.1: "POOL (tower, upper bridge, turn left) CLOSED. Tiles being replaced. The tiles have arrived, the tiler has arrived. The glue has not."
city.t3.t3_pool.2: "The glue has arrived. The tiler has gone to fetch tiles of another colour. The pool will be "sea" rather than "white." Thank you for your patience."
city.t3.t3_pool.3: "Tiling in progress. Six 25-metre lanes will be painted on the bottom. Lanes are promised straight, though straightness remains at the tiler's discretion."
city.t3.t3_pool.4: "Filling has begun. The pool fills like a cup in the kefir queue: slowly and with dignity." The lifeguards have hung the ring in its proper place. The ring now looks at the water.
city.t3.t3_pool.5: "The pool opens on Monday. A trial swim for those who bring a doctor's note and a cap." A cap can be found in the "Lost caps" box at the till.
city.t3.t3_reception.1: "The pool needs a doctor's note, the gym a season ticket, table tennis a good mood. Which of those have you got?"
city.t3.t3_reception.2: Cups above the desk, and under them a box marked "Lost swimming caps." There are more caps than cups.
city.t3.t3_reception.3: The cashier hands out a locker key on an elastic band: "Number seven, a lucky one. Don't mix it up with eight, that's the coach's."
city.t3.t3_reception.4: Timetable of sections: gymnastics, swimming, "Health after sixty" and "Health before sixteen." The second one is for me.
city.t3.t3_reception.5: "I'm keeping the number-five jersey, but I hand it only to those who promise not to wipe their face on it. The coach said: "A jersey has a number, not a towel.""
city.t3.t3_reception.6: "The coach has gone to paint the balls yellow. So that from the stands you can tell which is the ball and which is us. We're visible anyway."
city.t3.t3_results.1: Courtyard league table. 1. Seagulls: 12 points. 2. Lighthouse: 10. 3. Surf Juniors: 8. In pencil: "there will be more."
city.t3.t3_results.2: Hall records. Vault: Lyosha, "with room to spare." Pull-ups: Taya, 14, "not counting sighs." Next to it, an empty line: "a record not yet beaten."
city.t3.t3_results.3: Swimming, 25 m record: 19.4 seconds. The plaque is under repair together with the pool. The record-holder is waiting for water.
city.t3.t3_results.4: Courtyard tournament, results. 1. Seagulls: 3 wins. 2. Surf Juniors: 2. 3. Lighthouse. Best newcomer: No. 5 with 4 points, 3 rebounds, 1 ball into his own hoop. The own-hoop ball has been crossed out "for educational reasons."
city.t3.t3_results.5: Under the table, in chalk: "Thanks, number five." In the match record, a name is written against number five. The one I know already.
city.t3.t3_sauna_sit.1: In the morning the sauna is empty and smells of birch. I sat and listened to the stones cooling: tick, tick, tick.
city.t3.t3_sauna_sit.2: After practice the basketball players pile in, red as crayfish. The whole conversation: "Oof." And the answer: "Yep."
city.t3.t3_sauna_sit.3: Saturday steam! On the top bench a man in a felt hat reads a wet newspaper. The news is as fresh as it gets: straight out of the steam.
city.t3.t3_sauna_sit.4: On Sunday there are two people in the sauna, both asleep sitting up. I sat quieter than water so as not to disturb the Sunday.
city.t3.t3_sauna_water.1: I splashed a ladle onto the stones. They hissed and the steam settled on my shoulders like a warm blanket.
city.t3.t3_sauna_water.2: A ladle, a bucket, the stones: very simple. Only the steam doesn't listen and goes where it likes, usually into my face.
city.t3.t3_sauna_water.3: A sign on the stove: "Pour water in moderation." I poured in moderation. Moderation, it turns out, smells of a birch whisk.
city.t3.t3_sections.1: "Timetable. Mon, Wed, Fri: basketball (boys). Tue, Thu: gymnastics (girls). Sat: weights in the morning, games after lunch. Sunday: the hall is yours, there is no coach."
city.t3.t3_sections.2: Today: basketball, "Surf Juniors", 15:00–19:00. Please don't step on the court in street shoes. We ask politely. The coach asks impolitely.
city.t3.t3_sections.3: Today: gymnastics, Lidia Pavlovna's group. The vaulting horse is warming up, the wall bars are taken until six. Spectators: the bench.
city.t3.t3_sections.4: From 7 to 15 the hall is free; at 11:00 there's a PE lesson for class 6B. Please don't mistake the balls for heads.
city.t3.t3_sections.5: Saturday: weights until lunch, games after. Spectators free, players: bring water, leave the nerves.
city.t3.t3_sections.6: Sunday: short day, no coach. The ball is the responsibility of whoever picked it up.
city.t3.t3_sections.7: The hall closes at 21:00. The night watchman asks to be reminded of this very politely and very early.
city.t3.t3_shower.1: The hot water came in fits, like thoughts after practice. Then it steadied, and I stood there until I remembered the queue.
city.t3.t3_shower.2: The soap fell, I went after it, it went away from me. Caught it on the third try. Sport, basically.
city.t3.t3_shower.3: The water washed off the dust, the tiredness and half of my misses. The rest will dry by themselves.
city.t3.t3_shower.4: Steam, the noise of water, an echo. I sing without an ear but loudly. The shower is the one place where I'm surely the champion.
city.t3.t3_tactics.1: A chalk diagram on the board: circles are ours, crosses are not. One arrow leads to the basket. Another leads to the buffet, and it looks thicker.
city.t3.t3_tactics.2: A play called "Five": four circles stand firm, the fifth is empty with a question mark. Underneath: "newcomer: don't get in the way, but do teach."
city.t3.t3_tactics.3: The fifth circle has moved to the left wing and is ringed twice. Beside it: "don't let him fall, pass on time, make noise only when it counts."
city.t3.t3_tactics.4: The plan for Saturday: the Seagulls play rough, so play fast. Over it, big: "Run!" and small: "and think."
city.t3.t3_tactics.5: The board has been wiped clean. In the corner, a circled five and one word: "Thanks."
city.t3.t3_vault.1: Lidia Pavlovna's group: two vaults each over the horse. I got one counted: the second was more of a fall.
city.t3.t3_vault.2: Ran up, pushed off the springboard, cleared it, this time with room to spare. The horse nodded, or I imagined it.
city.t3.t3_ware.1: The shelf is empty apart from somebody's old cups and a bag of plaster.
city.t3.t3_ware.2: On the shelf, raw bowls by number, still grey and damp. No. 7 stands between two others and looks confident.
city.t3.t3_ware.3: The bowls have dried and paled like bread. They stand in line for the kiln. No touching: a finger can leave you in them forever.
city.t3.t3_ware.4: After the first firing the bowls are pink and ring when flicked. No. 7 is whole. Beside it, a cracked No. 3: the potter kept it "for beauty."
city.t3.t3_ware.5: The glazed bowls look wet but matt: the colour will come out in the kiln. Hard to believe, but it will.
city.t3.t3_ware.6: Finished! Green, blue, speckled. Beside them a note: "Take them yourselves. If you can't take them, give them away." No. 7 is mine.
city.t3.t3_ware.7: The shelf is resting. On it, one bowl, somebody's, with a note: "This one's mine. Not for giving." Beside it an empty spot for mine.
city.t3.t3_weights.1: The weightlifting section clatters in the corner: two huge men lift plates and whisper curses at them. I joined the queue for the bar: it moved slowly but respectfully.
city.t3.t3_weights.2: The basketball boys are working their legs. "Squat until you're lower than the hoop," the coach orders. "Then stand up and you'll be taller." I squatted five times. Stood up taller.
city.t3.t3_weights.3: Quiet and iron. I loaded the plates the way the coach taught me: the strength is in the legs, not the face. The face went red anyway.
city.t3.t3_weights.4: Held the bar without lifting. The bar didn't care: it's iron. I did. I think I've made friends with iron.
city.t3.t3_wheel.1: The potter said: "Centre it. Clay is like character: press and it runs away, don't press and it won't stand." On the third try the walls held. Bowl No. 7 came out with one side higher than the other. It was put aside to dry.
city.t3.t3_wheel.2: The wheel is quiet today: the kiln is firing and the potter looks into it every ten minutes, like into an oven with a pie. I just centred clay, for the feel of it.
city.t3.t3_wheel.3: Nobody sits at the wheel today: everyone is waiting. The bowls came out of the kiln after the first firing, No. 7 turned pink and rings like a bell. Next comes glaze, and that's not the wheel, that's the bench.
city.t3.t3_wheel.4: At the weekend the wheel goes to the little ones: they make "wrong" hares. They left me a lump too. I made a hare with one ear. The potter said: "That's not a hare, that's a running hare."
city.take.any.1: Nothing left here. Someone got here first.
city.take.any.2: Empty. Only a dusty rectangle where something used to lie.
city.take.daily_paper.1: I took a paper. On the front page, a fisherman with a flounder the size of a saucepan lid.
city.take.daily_paper.2: Today's issue. Forecast: clear, wind off the sea, music in the park possible in the evening.
city.take.daily_paper.3: The paper's still warm, as if it had just been printed behind the wall.
city.take.postcard.1: I took a postcard of the promenade. The sky on it is bluer than it ever really is.
city.take.postcard.2: A "Greetings from Lyudmilovsk!" card. Nobody to send it to, but I'll keep it.
city.take.postcard.3: On the back someone had pencilled "Dear…" and never finished.
city.talk.butcher.1: The butcher hones his knife and nods to me like an old friend. There's nothing for me to buy from him.
city.talk.butcher.2: "Out of mince, come early tomorrow. Scraps for the cats are free."
city.talk.butcher.3: Above the counter, a chart of beef cuts. The cow on it looks very calm.
city.talk.butcher.4: "What a sun today, eh? Even the meat looks rosier," said the butcher, surprised at himself.
city.talk.caretaker.1: The caretaker is mending a stool and says without looking up: "Stairs were mopped on Wednesday. Shuffle quieter."
city.talk.caretaker.2: Keys hang on nails, each with a tag: "Cellar", "Roof", "Fuse room", "Can't remember". The last one is the shiniest.
city.talk.caretaker.3: "I put a bulb in on the fourth, and it's gone again. Must like the dark," the caretaker sighs.
city.talk.caretaker.4: The radio in the cubbyhole mutters the weather report. The caretaker nods at each figure as if greeting old friends.
city.talk.cashier.1: "First the department, they write you a slip, then me, then back to the department. Clear?" "Clear."
city.talk.cashier.2: The cashier clacks the till so fast she seems to be playing a polka on it.
city.talk.cashier.3: "No small change? What if you look?" I looked. Found a button.
city.talk.cashier.4: By the till there's a saucer for change with one sweet in it. Change too, apparently.
city.talk.cloakroom.1: "Don't lose your token," said the attendant, though I had nothing to hand in.
city.talk.cloakroom.2: The hangers sway and chime softly, like wind chimes.
city.talk.cloakroom.3: "In summer we get only umbrellas, and one hat. The hat's been here since the spring before last."
city.talk.cloakroom.4: The attendant is knitting something long and striped. A scarf, she says. Three years now, she says.
city.talk.closed.1: Nobody. A note on the glass: "Gone to the depot. Back at 15:00." No date.
city.talk.closed.2: The counter's bare: an abacus and a glass of pencils. I tapped on the glass. Silence.
city.talk.closed.3: "Stocktaking." The sign hangs crooked, as if it went up in a hurry long ago.
city.talk.closed.4: Looks like they only sell to the neighbours, and the neighbours are all at home.
city.talk.club_lending.1: "The club's books are for circle members only. Join the chess circle and we'll lend you The Caro-Kann Defence. Gripping."
city.talk.club_lending.2: Names in a column on the record card, each marked "returned". Except one. Next to it, a sad little face.
city.talk.club_lending.3: "Take Radio magazine instead," the attendant suggests. "Lots of diagrams, few words. Rests the eyes."
city.talk.club_lending.4: The "Cog Club Library" stamp goes on everything: books, tickets and once, they say, the cat.
city.talk.concierge.1: The concierge looks up from her knitting. "Who for? Oh, just looking… Well, sit a while, there's a good draught here, off the sea."
city.talk.concierge.2: "The lift's thinking again on the seventh. If you get stuck, sing, I'll hear. Everyone who gets stuck sings. We've got a choir here."
city.talk.concierge.3: On the desk, a book for "Letters and parcels received" and a jar of toffees "for those who say hello politely". I said hello very politely.
city.talk.concierge.4: "Forty-two moved out, forty-three moved in, and the cat from forty-one visits both." The concierge knows the house by heart.
city.talk.counter.1: "Can I help you, young man?" "Just looking." "Look all you like."
city.talk.counter.2: Behind the counter someone is writing in a fat ledger and raises a finger: "One moment."
city.talk.counter.3: "Our break's from one to two, but for you, all right."
city.talk.counter.4: They smiled at me as if I came in every day. Maybe I really do.
city.talk.fishmonger.1: "The flounder's this morning's, the herring's yesterday's, and the gobies — don't ask."
city.talk.fishmonger.2: The fishwife weighs fish in her hand more exactly than the scales. The scales don't argue.
city.talk.fishmonger.3: "Catch something yourself, bring it here, I'll buy it," she said with a wink.
city.talk.fishmonger.4: One fish with a golden flank lies on the ice. "Not for sale," they say. "It's for luck."
city.talk.market_office.1: The market manager checks a weight on the control scales. "A hundred grams must be a hundred grams. Even by the sea."
city.talk.market_office.2: On the door: "Complaints book available on request." The book is brand new. Either there are no complaints or nobody requests it.
city.talk.market_office.3: "Tomorrow's pitches are all taken. Want to sell? Come at five in the morning with a crate and a smile."
city.talk.market_office.4: The little office smells of paper, smoked fish and tangerines. So does the whole market, only here it's official.
city.talk.office.1: "Pass? No pass, no entry. Sit on the sofa and think about it."
city.talk.office.2: The porter doesn't look up from his crossword. "Heavenly body, three letters?" "Sun." "Fits."
city.talk.office.3: "Visitors from nine. And whom are you here to see?" "I… nobody yet."
city.talk.office.4: A bell on the desk and a sign: "Ring once." I rang once. That was enough.
city.talk.reception.1: "Are you a guest? No? Then at least have some water, ours is medicinal."
city.talk.reception.2: A bell on the desk and a booking book for treatments. Next to every name, a little drawn sun.
city.talk.reception.3: "Breakfast from eight, dinner till seven, the sea round the clock," the receptionist rattled off.
city.talk.reception.4: "No rooms. But if you really need one, in 204 only one floorboard creaks."
city.talk.records.1: The record man drops the needle and lifts a finger. "Listen. Here, at two minutes, the singer sighed. That's not in the score."
city.talk.records.2: "No new ones, only good ones." He flicks through the sleeves like cards and pulls one out: "For you, this. You'll thank me later."
city.talk.records.3: On the wall, a record broken in half and glued. "My first waltz," says the man. "I danced on it. Literally."
city.talk.records.4: "Records are tinned time," the man said, and blew on the disc as if it were hot.
city.talk.registry.1: "Surname? Year of birth? I can't find your card. That means you're healthy," the registrar decided.
city.talk.registry.2: The appointment slip comes out of a little wooden box. Number 13. "Don't worry, thirteen's the quickest one here."
city.talk.registry.3: Behind the window, thousands of cards in drawers, alphabetical. The whole town, by its aches. Mine isn't among them.
city.talk.registry.4: "First the scales, then the eye chart, then the doctor. In that order, or the doctor gets offended."
city.talk.rentals.1: "Boats till sunset, deckchairs till six, umbrellas till the first rain."
city.talk.rentals.2: "Deposit's a passport. No passport? Then your word of honour. Got one of those?"
city.talk.rentals.3: Oars stand along the wall, numbered in paint. Number seven is missing: it went to sea last July.
city.talk.rentals.4: "The bikes are being repaired," sighed the man. "All of them. At once. A mystery."
city.talk.repair.1: The repairman doesn't look up from the watch. "Leave it, a week." "I've nothing to leave." "Even better."
city.talk.repair.2: On the shelf an iron, a transistor radio and a toy railway wait for their owners. The tag says "Urgent. 1987".
city.talk.repair.3: "You can fix anything but the weather and a mood," the repairman said, and fixed my shoelace.
city.talk.repair.4: It smells of rosin and machine oil. Somewhere in a corner twenty clocks tick at once, all out of step.
city.talk.salon.1: "Half-box, Canadian, or Like Dad's? No dad here? Then Like the Sea: in waves."
city.talk.salon.2: It smells of Chypre cologne and hot tongs. On the table, magazines of hairstyles that exist only in pictures.
city.talk.salon.3: The barber snips the air like a grasshopper. "Booking for tomorrow. Today I'm only cutting clouds."
city.talk.salon.4: An old lady waits on the sofa with a newspaper. "I'm not here for a haircut," she whispers. "I come for the news. Better than the radio."
city.talk.savings.1: "Got a passbook? No? We'll open one when there's something to put in it," the cashier says, so kindly it hardly stings.
city.talk.savings.2: A poster: "Keep your money in the savings bank." On it a piggy bank smiles as if it has saved up everything already.
city.talk.savings.3: They showed me someone's old passbook as an example: a deposit of 3 roubles 40 kopecks, opened in 1961. "He'll be back," they say.
city.talk.savings.4: The stamp thumped the paper so hard the inkwell jumped. "That's not for you, that's for order," the cashier explained.
city.talk.shoes.1: "What size? Forty-one? We've got forty-three, to grow into. Wool socks and they'll fit like a glove."
city.talk.shoes.2: The saleswoman taps a sole. "Our shoes last for ages. You can't wear them out, only outgrow them."
city.talk.shoes.3: On the shelf, lonely galoshes lined in red. "Nobody buys them," they say, "because everyone's waiting for rain, and it doesn't come."
city.talk.shoes.4: They set out a stool and a shoehorn for me. I didn't buy anything, but I sat there like a real customer.
city.talk.sport_reception.1: "The pool needs a doctor's note, the gym a season ticket, table tennis a good mood. Which of those have you got?"
city.talk.sport_reception.2: Trophies above the desk, and under them a box: "Lost swimming caps". There are more caps than trophies.
city.talk.sport_reception.3: The cashier hands over a locker key on an elastic band. "Number seven, a lucky one. Don't mix it up with eight, that's the coach's."
city.talk.sport_reception.4: The club timetable: gymnastics, swimming, "Health after sixty" and "Health before sixteen". The second one's mine.
city.talk.tickets.1: "Tickets are thirty roubles, pay in the hall. Sit anywhere, it's not busy."
city.talk.tickets.2: "Today it's The Man Who Waited for the Lighthouse. They say everyone cries at the end, even the projectionist."
city.talk.tickets.3: The cashier checks the poster against the wall clock, though the clock has stopped.
city.talk.tickets.4: "Under sixteens aren't allowed at the late show. How old are you? Never mind, don't answer."

city.unit.books.name: Book stall
city.unit.cafe.name: Seagull café
city.unit.dumplings.name: Dumpling bar

city.unit.pasty.name: Pasty bar
