city.weather.cloakroom.1: "Wet raincoat on the end hook, over the radiator. It'll be dry by the end of the show."
city.weather.cloakroom.2: "Shake the snow off your collar onto the mat, not onto me. Felt boots can stay under the rack."
city.weather.counter.1: "Put your umbrella in the corner, please, I've got a whole sea on the floor already."
city.xcl.aq.0: A fish, orange as a boiled sweet, drifts unhurriedly from one end of the glass to the other. A little plate under the tank says "Head Doctor".
city.xcl.aq.1: In the morning the fish hangs right against the glass, by the reception side, as if queuing too.
city.xcl.aq.2: After lunch the hall is quiet. The fish stands by the weed, flicking a fin. Thinking.
city.xcl.aq.3: Towards evening the hall is nearly empty and the fish grows bold: out to the middle of the tank, looking at the front door.
city.xcl.aq.4: At night one ceiling lamp is on. The filter bubbles in the tank and the fish sleeps upright. Fish can do that.
city.xcl.aq.5: The children call the fish the Head Doctor: it swims by the reception with the look of someone who already knows everything. Nobody hung the plate, it just appeared, in a child's handwriting.
city.xcl.aq.6: The tank feels roomy. There used to be a second fish with the Head Doctor; now only a clay house is left on the bottom, and it is empty.
city.xcl.aq.7: The water is a little cloudy. A watering can stands beside it with a note: "Top up with settled water. Not straight from the tap, the fish has nerves."
city.xcl.aq.8: There are now two orange flecks in the tank. The Head Doctor keeps stoutly to the middle and pretends to be displeased.
city.xcl.aqw.1: You pour water from your bottle into the can, let it settle and carefully top up the tank. The fish backs away, then returns to check whether you are ashamed.
city.xcl.aqw.2: The water rises two fingers' width. The fish does a lap of honour along the glass and you could swear it nodded.
city.xcl.bl.1: A notice: "Autumn: change your socks, don't lose your scarf, don't chill your throat. Consultation with the district doctor on weekdays."
city.xcl.bl.2: "Next week is Vaccination Week. Sign up at the reception. Bring your card and a good mood." The word "good" is underlined.
city.xcl.bl.3: "VACCINATION WEEK. Room 3, from 9 to 12. The procedure takes a moment, the sweet afterwards is compulsory." A sweet is drawn under the text, impossible to miss.
city.xcl.bl.4: "Thank you to everyone who had their jab! The sheet bears 112 signatures and one nose print."
city.xcl.bl.5: "Winter: walks before lunch, hot tea afterwards. Mind your ears: a hat is not an ornament."
city.xcl.bl.6: "Spring and summer: sun in moderation, water not icy, bicycles with helmets (helmets issued at reception)."
city.xcl.bp.1: The cuff swells, the needle jumps. The nurse listens through the stethoscope, her lips moving, and nods: "Like an astronaut's. Only an astronaut's is a little lower."
city.xcl.bp.2: "A hundred and twenty over eighty." You don't know if that's a lot or a little, but the nurse smiles. So it's good.
city.xcl.bp.3: The cuff lets go of your arm with a long sigh, and you sigh too. The nurse writes the figures in your card and underlines them twice.
city.xcl.cf.1: The card file: little drawers with letters. The cards stand tight as books on a shelf. Each has a surname, a birth year, vaccinations and Galina Petrovna's handwriting, round and quite legible.
city.xcl.cf.2: From the drawer marked K sticks a card with a note: "Fell off his bicycle. For the last time? No, not the last." In another hand beside it: "Helmet issued."
city.xcl.cf.3: The schoolchildren's cards are bound with a red elastic band: height and weight for every year, and in the margins notes like "reads at meals" and "climbs fences".
city.xcl.cf.4: The thickest card belongs to a man who, going by the entries, comes to the clinic to have someone to talk to. The nurse's note: "Listen. Pour tea."
city.xcl.dn.0: A white door without a pane. The plate: "Room 4. Dentist. By appointment." Nobody sits on the chair by the door, but the chair is squared up as if waiting.
city.xcl.dn.1: A drill hums softly behind the door. Everyone in the hall has suddenly become interested in the poster above the bench.
city.xcl.dn.2: The door opens: a boy with red ears comes out, palm pressed to his cheek. "It didn't hurt!" he tells his mum, and sits so that nobody can see his face.
city.xcl.dn.3: Instruments clink in a steel dish behind the door. It sounds like somebody counting out small change for your future.
city.xcl.dn.4: The door is locked. In the dark the "Room 4" plate looks sterner than by day.
city.xcl.dn.5: The room is shut at weekends. A note on the door: "Toothache? Emergencies at the duty nurse's reception desk. Be brave."
city.xcl.ep.1: Rabkin's plates: speckled circles with numbers hidden in them. Some see the number at once, others after a long look. Yesterday one patient saw a cat.
city.xcl.ep.2: A case of trial lenses: thin discs of glass in metal rims. The doctor swaps them one after another: "And this? And this? And now?"
city.xcl.hm.1: The rubber hammer taps below your kneecap and your leg kicks out by itself. The nurse is pleased: "Reflexes fine. Manners, a C."
city.xcl.hm.2: You follow the hammer's shiny tip with your eyes and forget you have another leg. Tap. The leg jumps. You laugh.
city.xcl.ht.1: You stand with your back to the wall, chin up. The slider comes down on your head with a clink. Beside it, pencil marks in the plaster; the lowest ones carry the names of toddlers.
city.xcl.ht.2: A hundred and sixty-something. The "150" mark is worn to a shine: every schoolchild in the district has been measured here, and every one rose a little on tiptoe.
city.xcl.ht.3: A paper by the ruler: "No tiptoes. No heels. No sulking: you will still grow."
city.xcl.in.1: The nurse switches the machine on: alkaline water bubbles in the glass jar. You breathe warm steam. It smells of baking soda and winter.
city.xcl.in.2: Fifteen minutes. Your nose clears, and your thoughts with it. Beside you an old lady sits over the other glass with the face of someone at the baths, not a clinic.
city.xcl.in.3: The nurse times it with an hourglass. The hourglass is small, the steam is large. "One more minute. No, I didn't decide, the sand did."
city.xcl.jar.1: The coin clunks to the bottom of the jar. The paper on the glass says "For the Head Doctor's friend", and someone has drawn a second fish under the words.
city.xcl.jar.2: The nurse nods from her window: "Thank you. The Head Doctor doesn't know yet, but when he does he'll be glad. He'll pretend not to be."
city.xcl.jar.3: The jar is full now. The nurse laughs: "That covers guppies, food and a pretty pebble besides. The rest I put back in the till, don't worry."
city.xcl.mg.1: Last year's "Health" and a cover-less "Ogonyok". The crossword in "Health" is half done: "Part of the ear, five letters" and somebody has written "lobe" in, underlined with pleasure.
city.xcl.mg.2: A magazine piece "How to learn to wait" has been cut out with scissors. What is left is the edge of the page and "To be continued in the next issue".
city.xcl.mg.3: An old newspaper folded in four: telephone numbers jotted on it and a recipe for pickles. The stains suggest the recipe has been tested.
city.xcl.mg.v: A magazine lies open at "A jab isn't scary". Over the picture someone has pencilled a smiling face on the sleeve.
city.xcl.p.bp: E — have my blood pressure taken
city.xcl.p.cards: E — peek into the card file
city.xcl.p.jar: E — drop a coin in the jar
city.xcl.p.mags: E — pick a magazine off the table
city.xcl.p.scale: E — weigh something on the apothecary scale
city.xcl.ph.j1: Jars with Latin labels. Only "Aqua" and "Mel" look familiar. The rest sounds like a spell.
city.xcl.ph.j2: A paper over the jars: "Prescription goods not sold without a prescription. Medicine without a prescription is called a sweet. Sweets are over here."
city.xcl.ph.j3: On the shelf a white mortar with its pestle. They say nobody grinds powders any more, they arrive ready-made. But the mortar is wiped every morning.
city.xcl.ph.r1: "Prescriptions are accepted 8 to 12. Dispensed 2 to 5. An unreadable prescription goes back to the doctor who wrote it. He sometimes cannot read it himself."
city.xcl.ph.r2: "Please do not ask us for honey, raspberries or cherry jam. That is for your grandmother. Thermometers are for measuring, not for biting."
city.xcl.ph.s1: Apothecary scales: two little pans and a brass beam. The nurse puts a five-gram weight on one and a pinch of sugar on the other. They balance. "Just checking," she says. "The scales are honest."
city.xcl.ph.s2: On the scales, foil from a chocolate bar: exactly one gram. "We used to check nobody was being short-changed. Now I check the pharmacy isn't short-changing itself."
city.xcl.pl.0: The plate on the door: "Hours 8 to 17, break 13 to 14." In pencil underneath: "A break is when the doctor eats, not when he can't hear you."
city.xcl.pl.1: "Today the duty nurse sees patients. Doctors from Monday." The paper has yellowed at the edges: it has hung there a long time, weekends do repeat.
city.xcl.qb.1: The board reads "17". Under it a lamp blinks "Room 2". As long as it blinks, somebody inside is telling the long story of their knee.
city.xcl.qb.2: The board shows "CLOSED" and the red digits are dark. A paper under it says: "Surgery over. Tomorrow from 8:00."
city.xcl.qb.3: At weekends the board is silent: one duty nurse sees everybody, and she needs no queue. "Come on up, don't be shy."
city.xcl.rd.1: The loudspeaker softly draws out the morning exercises: "Deep breath in... and deeper still..." Half the queue straightens its back without meaning to.
city.xcl.rd.2: The wall radio quietly gives news of steel output and the weather on the coast. The weather is more interesting.
city.xcl.rd.3: An orchestra is playing. An old woman by the wall taps her toe in time and pretends not to be listening.
city.xcl.rd.4: The evening request show. The announcer reads a letter: "For Mum, who is late at the clinic today. We are waiting at home."
city.xcl.rd.5: The wall radio is silent. In the quiet you can hear the aquarium filter bubbling.
city.xcl.rg.1: "Have you taken a ticket? See the board? Look at that, and at me afterwards."
city.xcl.rg.2: "Surname? Year of birth? No, not mine, yours."
city.xcl.rg.3: "The doctor sees patients until five. Not until five to five, until five. You'll make it if you don't read the whole poster."
city.xcl.rg.4: "After five it is just me and the thermometer. But it's a good thermometer, German, pre-war."
city.xcl.rg.5: "On Saturdays there are no doctors, I'm all of them. What hurts? Tell me, I'll write it down and say who to see on Monday."
city.xcl.rg.6: "Want to help? There's the jar. The money isn't for me, it's for the Head Doctor. The fish, I mean. Don't get ideas."
city.xcl.rg.7: "Thank you for coming in. Take tickets in order, not out of greed. Then there'll be enough for everyone."
city.xcl.tk.1: The machine gives you ticket no. 6. The board shows "3", so a couple of people ahead. Everyone in the hall pretends not to be counting.
city.xcl.tk.2: Ticket no. 41, the board says "17". The old woman beside you sighs and straightens her scarf: "They used to call you by name. At least you knew it was a person being called."
city.xcl.tk.3: Ticket no. 58. After lunch the queue melts away: the board shows "55" and you will be called soon.
city.xcl.tk.4: The roll of tickets has run out and a note is taped to the machine: "No more tickets today. Emergency help is at the reception."
city.xh.case.fri: "Friday. Dance shoes of thirty years." One pair is worn through at the left toe. Caption: "The left foot led."
city.xh.case.mon: A plaque on the case: "Monday. Fishing floats of Lyudmilovsk." Glass ones, blue and green. On the biggest, scratched: "Not mine."
city.xh.case.prompt: E — look into the display case
city.xh.case.sat: "Saturday. What is left after a premiere." A prop key, a dried rose, a programme signed by the whole company. An empty space beside them: "For tomorrow's things."
city.xh.case.sun: The case is being cleaned; the plaque says "Sunday. Resting." The glass shines, and inside it a nose is reflected. Yours, it seems.
city.xh.case.thu: "Thursday. Theatre programmes of different years." The oldest is printed on the back of a cable car ticket. Print run: "as many as friends."
city.xh.case.tue: "Tuesday. School exercise books with views of the town." In one, the lighthouse is drawn three times, from a new side each time. At the bottom, a mark: "Good for a first attempt."
city.xh.case.wed: "Wednesday. Musical instruments: a harmonica, a tuning fork, a cracked guitar top." The fork lies by the harmonica as if it had argued with it and lost.
city.xh.chalk.dance: In chalk, big: "DANCE! Pear lemonade 18, pie 18, tea 15, coffee 30. Napkin free for dancers." The napkin is drawn too.
city.xh.chalk.day: In chalk: "By day: soup from the kitchen, if the kitchen has not changed its mind. Tea 15, coffee 30, pie 18." At the bottom: "Pear lemonade 18, cold and very sweet."
city.xh.chalk.eve: In chalk: "In the evening, the same, only quieter. Tea 15, coffee 30, pie 18, pear lemonade 18." Beside it, a drawn teapot that seems to wink.
city.xh.chalk.morning: In chalk on the board: "Tea 15. Coffee 30. Pie 18. Pear lemonade 18." Below: "Yesterday's pie: discounted, with an honest confession." The last line is underlined.
city.xh.costumes.fri: Dress rehearsal: every costume in place, ironed, smelling of a hot iron. "Echo" and "Second Echo" are identical grey cloaks; the second is tagged "This is the second one."
city.xh.costumes.mon: The rail backstage. Tags on the hangers: "Clockmaker", "Mayor", "Postwoman", "Echo", "Second Echo". The Clockmaker tag is pinned to the caretaker's waistcoat. He objected, but it fits like a glove.
city.xh.costumes.prompt: E — sort through the costume rail
city.xh.costumes.sat: The rail is almost empty: the costumes are on the actors. One hanger is left, tagged "Spare". The spare is nervous too.
city.xh.costumes.sun: The costumes are back on the rail, smelling of the stage and a little of pies. On the Clockmaker's hanger, a card from someone in the audience: "You were better than all the clocks."
city.xh.costumes.thu: The Postwoman's dress is hemmed in a hurry, threads sticking out. Pencilled on the hem: "Hem after the dress rehearsal. If I'm late, nobody will notice. If they do, I'll say it's deliberate."
city.xh.costumes.tue: A pocket-watch chain has joined the waistcoat. There is no watch on it. A note: "The prop master will bring the watch. Prop master, where are you?"
city.xh.costumes.wed: The Mayor's jacket is two sizes too big for the Mayor. Pins beside it and the dresser's note: "Mayor, no pies until Saturday. Or eat them, but quietly."
city.xh.dance.band.1: Live music: a pianist from the next building and a drummer on a stool. You waltz with someone who keeps looking at their feet. Then they look at you, and that is better.
city.xh.dance.band.2: A fast dance. Everyone spins, the mirror ball scatters spots of light over faces and walls. For a second the hall is an aquarium of glowing fish.
city.xh.dance.band.3: Ladies' choice: the girls do the asking. Someone bows to you and you bow back. Your partner says: "Don't look at your feet, they know." They do.
city.xh.dance.fri_idle.1: The empty floor waits for evening. The mirror ball is silent, the pennants stir in the draught, and in the corner the piano remembers a waltz. You take one step, just in case.
city.xh.dance.sun_idle.1: Sunday outside the tea hours: the floor gleams as if just washed. It was.
city.xh.dance.sun_tea.1: Tea dances: elderly couples dance slowly and very beautifully. Your partner whispers: "One-two-three, don't hurry." You don't hurry, and the waltz works.
city.xh.dance.wk_class.1: The dance club: the teacher claps the count and says loudly, "And one, and two!" You try. It comes out nearly like everyone else's.
city.xh.dance.wk_idle.1: The polished floor reflects the vault well. You can move without witnesses: no one sees you trip over your own shadow.
city.xh.dancemirror.prompt: E — stand at the barre mirror
city.xh.dancenight.prompt: E — step onto the dance floor
city.xh.ghost.day.1: A bare bulb on a thin stand at the edge of the stage. By day it is hardly noticeable, but a small plate beside it says: "Do not switch off. Not a whim, a tradition."
city.xh.ghost.day.2: The caretaker says that while the lamp burns, the stage is not empty. Who exactly is on it, he does not say.
city.xh.ghost.night.1: The only light in the dark hall. The bulb lights half a metre of floor and the plate with its name: "On duty". It is on duty always, even when nobody else is.
city.xh.ghost.night.2: In the dark hall the ghost light throws the shadow of its stand up the vaults, huge as a mast. Old actors say: while it burns, the ghosts rehearse and leave the living alone.
city.xh.ghost.prompt: E — look at the ghost light
city.xh.guest.1: The guest book lies open. The first entry on the page: "Good. Only the echo repeated my sneeze twice." Signed: "A lover of quiet."
city.xh.guest.2: "Sang in the choir, sang well. The choir leader said, 'Nearly.' That is the highest praise." Beside it, in another hand: "Confirmed."
city.xh.guest.3: "Danced until eleven. My shoes fell like heroes. Please compensate." Below: "We cannot compensate, but we will give you a pie."
city.xh.guest.4: In a child's hand: "I like the ceiling. It is like a big white palm. If I were a pigeon I would live here."
city.xh.guest.5: "The reading of the play about clocks went well. The director cried because she was laughing, or the other way round." Signed: "The caretaker, a.k.a. the Clockmaker."
city.xh.guest.6: "Remark: the buffet ran out of pies at 19:10. Suggestion: bake more pies. Or start the evenings later." The signature is illegible, but heartfelt.
city.xh.guest.7: A note between the pages: "Who found the chess clock with the crack? It is not a prop, the club is looking for it." A pencilled reply: "Found. On stage, among the props. Will be returned soon."
city.xh.guest.8: "Premiere! We laughed, we clapped, the echo clapped with us. The applause lasted three minutes, two of them echo."
city.xh.guest.9: The last entry, on a clean line: "Come again tomorrow. Write your name here, we have left room." The room is really left, and a pen hangs on its chain.
city.xh.guest.prompt: E — leaf through the guest book
city.xh.lights.day.1: A panel with six switches and handwritten labels: "Work light", "Footlights", "Spots left", "Spots right", "Curtain", "Do not switch on". By day there is little to click, it is bright anyway.
city.xh.lights.day.2: Click, and a pair of spotlights comes on over the stage. Click, and it goes out. The windows are high, the day is stronger, and the spots only turn faintly yellow, like birthday candles at noon.
city.xh.lights.eve.1: In the evening the panel comes alive: "Footlights", and the stage turns gold. "Spots left", and the piano gleams. "Spots right", and the mosaic shows on the wall. Only the "Do not switch on" stays untouched.
city.xh.lights.eve.2: Click-click-click: blue, red, white again. A lone stool on stage in the blue light looks as though it is about to sing.
city.xh.lights.night.1: Only "Standby" is on. The other switches stand in a row like piano keys. None may be touched until morning, the caretaker said.
city.xh.lights.sat.1: The premiere's lighting: "Footlights" at half, "Spots" on cue, blue for the lighthouse scene. A slip on the panel: "Don't forget: in the finale, light on the clock."
city.xh.makeup.day.1: A make-up mirror with bulbs round the frame, most of them blown. In it you are without make-up: ordinary, serious, slightly surprised. While no one is looking, you can pull a face.
city.xh.makeup.day.2: On the table, pots of greasepaint, a powder puff, and boxes labelled "Beard, light" and "Beard, heavy". There is also a nose. Just one, on elastic.
city.xh.makeup.eve.1: The make-up woman draws wrinkles with a pencil. The actor is eighteen and the part is seventy. "Don't breathe," she says, "or the age will run."
city.xh.makeup.eve.2: In the mirror it is no longer you but somebody's grandfather. The eyes are yours, though, and so are the thoughts. Let us hope the grandfather does not let you down.
city.xh.makeup.night.1: At night the mirror is dark, one bulb smouldering. In it another bulb is reflected, the ghost light from the hall. They look at each other and do not blink.
city.xh.makeup.prompt: E — look in the make-up mirror
city.xh.makeup.sat.1: Before the premiere everyone in the mirror looks alike: pale, bright-lipped, whispering their lines. The make-up woman says: "Spit three times over the left shoulder and forget." Someone spits. Someone forgets.
city.xh.mirror.1: A mirror along the wall, a barre before it, polished by palms to a golden shine. In the mirror you are a little taller than in life. Posture, probably.
city.xh.mirror.2: You try three waltz steps in front of the mirror. On the third, the reflection takes one step more. It has clearly been practising longer.
city.xh.mirror.3: A sticker on the frame: "Keep your back straight. Smile if you like. Breathing is compulsory." The last is underlined twice.
city.xh.mirror.4: In the corner of the mirror, the print of a small palm, and at waist height a larger one. It looks as if people here learn to dance from childhood.
city.xh.mixer.day.1: The sound desk under a cover made of an old curtain. The faders are labelled in pencil: "Choir", "Piano", "Microphone", "Do not touch!!!" The last label is the most worn.
city.xh.mixer.day.2: A reel-to-reel recorder. A note on its lid: "Recording of Wednesday's choir rehearsal. Listen after nine in the evening, it sounds better."
city.xh.mixer.eve.1: The amateur sound man nudges a fader and out of the speakers on stage comes the rustle of the hall. Then the fader creeps back and the hall becomes a little quieter, a little farther, a little kinder.
city.xh.mixer.eve.2: The tape clicks into a pause, and the whole hall hears someone tuning the piano on stage. One note, then another. The A turns out to be the most honest of them.
city.xh.mixer.night.1: The desk is under its cover and the lamp is off. Only a red light on the recorder blinks, as if listening to something.
city.xh.mixer.prompt: E — go up to the sound desk
city.xh.mixer.sat.1: The desk on Saturday evening: the faders are up, the lamp is on, the sound man sits straight as at an exam. On a slip of paper: "First bell 18:55. Second 19:00. Third: as circumstances allow."
city.xh.mixer.sat.2: A big sheet lies by the desk: "Echo: do not damp, it is in the company. Clocks: do not forget. Applause: do not interrupt." The last is written bigger than the rest.
city.xh.premiere.prompt: E — watch the stage from the house
city.xh.prog.fri: Friday, 19:00: a dance night in the side hall, with the buffet. A record plays, and with luck a pianist. Dancing until 23:00; a change of shoes is welcome.
city.xh.prog.mon: The Vaults' programme. Monday: no evenings. The hall rests, the caretaker wipes the banisters and scolds the draught. The buffet is open and there are pies.
city.xh.prog.prompt: E — read the programme of evenings
city.xh.prog.sat: Saturday, 19:00: PREMIERE of Time, Forward!, the Wave theatre. Free entry, seats by affection. Dancing after the show.
city.xh.prog.sun: Sunday, 14:00 to 19:00: tea dances for those who like to be home early. Children under twelve free, and welcome until the last waltz.
city.xh.prog.thu: Thursday, 18:00: the Wave amateur theatre rehearses the play Time, Forward! Spectators welcome; remarks accepted in writing, and afterwards.
city.xh.prog.tue: Tuesday, 19:00: a lecture, "Why the echo in the Vaults runs late". Given by an acoustics engineer, free entry. Please do not clap until the end: the echo claps for you.
city.xh.prog.wed: Wednesday, 17:00: the Surf choir, open rehearsal. You may sit in the hall and keep quiet. Singing along is allowed in a whisper only: the choir leader's condition.
city.xh.props.1: The props table: a telephone with no cord, a globe with the Pacific painted over the Baltic, an inkwell of dried ink. All so that a play about time looks like a play about time.
city.xh.props.2: In a box, a chess clock with a crack on the left dial. The tag: "Prop, act one. Return to the club when asked. If asked, we will. If not, we will anyway."
city.xh.props.3: A handwritten script of Time, Forward! with notes in the margins: "Pause here." "A longer pause here." "Pause, and light, please."
city.xh.props.4: An alarm clock with one hand. The director says the second hand is the audience: at the right moment it works out for itself that time is up.
city.xh.props.5: Under the table a crate marked "Echo (do not rattle)": inside, sheets of tin and two spoons. This is how the play sounds the Vaults' echo when the real one is late.
city.xh.rehearsal.fri: Dress rehearsal: costumes and lights. The dance in the side hall goes ahead; please do not come on stage in dancing shoes, and do not dance in the Mayor's scene.
city.xh.rehearsal.mon: A notice from the Wave theatre: "Parts are cast. Clockmaker: the caretaker (he agreed, but only until nine in the evening). Mayor: the pie seller. Postwoman: the girl from the box office. Echo and Second Echo: twin brothers, they talk to each other anyway."
city.xh.rehearsal.sat: Today at 19:00, PREMIERE. Free entry, seats by affection. Please be nervous politely, shout "bravo" if you like, applaud as you see fit: the echo will back you up.
city.xh.rehearsal.sun: Thank you to everyone who came! The hall applauded longer than the play ran. Photos in the foyer, comments in the book. The next production is by request; apply to the caretaker, he knows where the clock is.
city.xh.rehearsal.thu: Urgent! We need a big clock for act one, preferably a working one. Bring it backstage. No need to phone: the echo will hear.
city.xh.rehearsal.tue: The read-through is done. The echo in the Vaults sent every line back late, and the director decided it is even better: a third actor.
city.xh.rehearsal.wed: A request to the cast: the choir rehearses until 19:00, then the stage is yours. The Clockmaker must not die on stage before then: the hall is singing a lullaby.
city.xh.show.sat_day.1: The day run before the premiere. The hall is empty, and on stage everyone is in costume and terribly serious. The director sits in row five repeating: "Just breathe. The vault will say the rest."
city.xh.show.sat_day.2: The actors come out for a bow in front of the empty hall. They bow awkwardly, on a count. Then one of them sticks her tongue out at the echo. The echo, of course, does the same.
city.xh.show.sat_late.1: The play ended long ago. On stage only the ghost light, and the clock ticking quietly, the big one. It was left on stage. It is going.
city.xh.show.sat_show.1: The lights go down. From the wings comes the caretaker in a waistcoat with a chain, surveys the hall as sternly as a clock showing the exact time, and says: "Time... goes on." The hall laughs, the echo laughs a little later.
city.xh.show.sat_show.2: Act two: the Mayor tries to stop the clock and it strikes thirteen. The Mayor is horrified, the hall delighted. Up in the gallery someone whispers, "That is not in the script." The prop master, presumably.
city.xh.show.sat_show.3: The finale. The Clockmaker winds the big clock and it goes. The light slowly warms. Someone on stage forgets a line, the prompter whispers, and the whole hall takes it up in a whisper. Applause for three minutes, two of them echo.
city.xh.show.wk_day.1: A rehearsal without costumes, in whatever they came in. An actor in a sweater plays the Mayor, an actress in a coat the town clock. The director takes off her glasses: "Very convincing. Only louder."
city.xh.show.wk_day.2: They are trying the lights on stage. A spotlight comes on, goes off, and each time someone says, "There you go." It is the most expressive line of the day.
city.xh.show.wk_eve.1: An evening rehearsal: the Clockmaker recalls his monologue, getting half way. The prompter whispers; the Clockmaker answers, "I know, I'm thinking." The director writes in her notebook: "Keep the pause."
city.xh.show.wk_eve.2: The choir sings something quiet behind the scenes while the postwoman's scene plays on stage. It turns out strangely beautiful: a letter read to a lullaby.
city.xh.show.wk_late.1: At night one ghost light burns on stage. The hall is empty, and the emptiness under the vaults seems a very attentive listener.
city.xk.1_crossword.1: Under the glass hangs yesterday's crossword, solved in pencil. The hand is even, the letters square, like a draughtsman's.
city.xk.1_crossword.2: A note beside it: "Right answers on Fridays. Wrong ones every day."
city.xk.1_crossword.3: Less than half is filled in. But "wind" is written in ink, so firmly that the author seems to be arguing with the printer.
city.xk.1_crossword.4: Six more words today. During the night, probably: the seller came to a shut kiosk and the crossword was already different.
city.xk.1_crossword.5: The seller has seen the solver: "Someone who waits for the last bus. In no hurry, knows everything except one word."
city.xk.1_crossword.6: One clue is left: "Eight letters: what a bus stop has most of." The pencil on its string waits on the bench.
city.xk.1_crossword.7: The seller whispers: "He sat on the bench till morning, thinking. They say you're quick. Take a look: there's a paper and a pencil."
city.xk.1_pencil.1: On the bench lies a paper with the crossword and a pencil stub on a string. Nobody is solving: the bus isn't coming and the squares are few.
city.xk.1_pencil.2: I solved a short one: "wind." It fit. My handwriting is worse, but confident.
city.xk.1_pencil.3: Thinking about the last clue: "what a bus stop has most of." "Buses"? No, there are hardly any. "Benches"? No.
city.xk.1_pencil.4: I sat, looked at the timetable, the clock, the road. The word kept turning but wouldn't fit the squares.
city.xk.1_pencil.5: I wrote it in: P-A-T-I-E-N-C-E. Eight squares, and every crossing fit. I put the pencil down and heard someone in the kiosk say quietly: "At last."
city.xk.1_phone.1: I dialled my own number, which doesn't exist here yet. Polite silence picked up.
city.xk.1_phone.2: I rang the information line: "What do you know about the weather?" "Everything except tomorrow." I hung up pleased.
city.xk.1_phone.3: The evening tone is softer than the day's. I dialled the number from the stop's notice: engaged. That is an answer too.
city.xk.1_phone.4: At night the payphone hums alone. I dialled the speaking clock: "Twenty-three fifty-nine," said a voice, and added: "Go to bed."
city.xk.1_phone.5: At the weekend you can hear farther down the line: somebody across town is laughing and doesn't pick up.
city.xk.2_bell.1: I rang. Someone looked out of the hatch, saw there was no rain, and smiled anyway: "All right. A scoop at half price, for persistence."
city.xk.2_bell.2: The bell chimed thin, like a spoon on a glass. A hand held a cone through the hatch: "This is for you. Cheaper only in daydreams."
city.xk.2_bell.3: A morning chime. "You're the first today," said the hatch. "The first gets a cherry. No cherries, so here's a double smile."
city.xk.2_cone.1: On the pole a waffle cone with three scoops: pink, white and yellow. The top one has slipped a little and holds on out of stubbornness.
city.xk.2_cone.2: A slip of paper is taped to the pole in a child's hand: "I want two scoops. Mum said when I grow up. I've grown 2 cm."
city.xk.2_cone.3: Under it a reply: "Until you grow another 3 cm, one. But I'm trying very hard not to notice."
city.xk.2_cone.4: The slip is smoothed out and boxed in a frame: "Grown." A tick beside it and a note: "Checked with a tape measure."
city.xk.2_cone.5: Each morning a sparrow sits by the pole waiting for a dropped wafer. It's already called Sundae. It doesn't mind.
city.xk.2_cone.6: A new line on the slip: "Two scoops for whoever rings the bell on the hatch first." Ringing is allowed.
city.xk.2_flavours.1: In chalk on the board: "Today: plain, crème brûlée, plain with jam. No chocolate; it was eaten at the weekend."
city.xk.2_flavours.2: Added: "Two scoops are allowed, but don't make a fuss." The scoops are drawn as circles; one is winking.
city.xk.2_flavours.3: "Weekend: chocolate! Two scoops for the price of one and a half. The queue is on the far side of the rubbed-out chalk."
city.xk.2_flavours.4: At the bottom, in a child's hand: "Is there ice cream with a mood?" Below, in an adult's: "There is. With a good one, any kind."
city.xk.2_flavours.5: Early on the board: "Ice cream before noon is not weakness but privilege."
city.xk.2_fountain.1: The fountain water smells of iron and summer. The jet leaps higher if you press with two fingers.
city.xk.2_fountain.2: In the evening the fountain gurgles lower. The water is lukewarm, as though it, too, had been left out in the sun.
city.xk.3_jar.1: A jar of matchboxes from the whole coast: "Amber," "Lighthouse," "Summer '71." The lid is tight: looking is fine, opening is not.
city.xk.3_jar.2: A card: "Whoever quits brings a box. There are 31 in the jar. The 32nd is up to you, if you are one of those."
city.xk.3_jar.3: Now 33 boxes. One from a man who quit on Thursday, the other "just in case."
city.xk.3_jar.4: There are 36 in the jar. The seller admits that three are their own: "holidays, once a year. That doesn't count."
city.xk.3_jar.5: The jar is full. The seller counts the boxes and says: "Enough. This isn't a jar now, it's a testimony."
city.xk.3_pipes.1: Six pipes on the rack: a cherrywood one, a chewed one, one carved with a gull. It smells of cherry and old polish.
city.xk.3_pipes.2: A plate: "Not for sale. Belongs to Grandfather T. and his grandfather. Looking is allowed, breathing on the varnish is not."
city.xk.3_pipes.3: A seventh pipe lies apart in a case. "Its owner hasn't smoked for three years," says the seller. "But he comes on Wednesdays and sniffs it."
city.xk.3_pipes.4: An old man stands by the kiosk sniffing an empty pipe. The seller pretends to count change.
city.xk.3_pipes.5: A note on the rack: "Thank you. Quit for real. I leave the pipe in the row." The seventh now stands next to the gull.
city.xk.3_weigh.1: The scales shuddered. A ticket: "Morning. Weight: slightly less than it seems. You are alert."
city.xk.3_weigh.2: A ticket: "Weight: reliable. Advice: ice cream is at the next kiosk; it weighs more than it seems."
city.xk.3_weigh.3: A ticket: "In the evening everyone is a little heavier. That's normal. That's the day."
city.xk.3_weigh.4: A ticket: "One doesn't weigh at night. But since you're standing here: the same weight, a thoughtful look."
city.xk.4_lilac.1: A note on the pink board: "Ales, buckets of lilac into the shade." "Please" is crossed out, above it: "PLEASE."
city.xk.4_lilac.2: A new note from Anait: "The lilac bloomed ahead of time. Don't blame it, it's in a hurry to live."
city.xk.4_lilac.3: Ales's reply: "I put it in the shade. But the lilac is hot anyway. That's how it is."
city.xk.4_lilac.4: Beside it a cross sunflower is drawn: "I want shade too." Someone signed under it: "You get the sun."
city.xk.4_lilac.5: Anait left Ales a sprig: "Smells like Mum when she was happy." The sprig has drooped, but the scent holds.
city.xk.4_lilac.6: On the back, a note for me: "If you come in the evening, water the sunflowers by the kiosk. Can on the left. Ales left early and they sulk without water."
city.xk.4_watering.1: I watered the sunflowers by the kiosk with the can. They seemed to turn to me. Or to the sun. Or they were dizzy.
city.xk.4_watering.2: Evening watering is the right kind: the water doesn't evaporate, the flowers don't object. The can is empty, the buckets are full.
city.xk.4_watering.3: At night it's better not to touch the can: it clinks. But one sunflower got its water anyway.
city.xk.4_wrap.1: I held the kraft paper while the ribbon was tied. "A bow isn't decoration, it's a promise the bunch won't fall apart," I was told.
city.xk.4_wrap.2: I cut paper along a ruler. It came out crooked, but "crooked means by hand, and flowers like hands."
city.xk.4_wrap.3: I was trusted to tie three daisies and an ear of wheat. It came out like a first-grader's. "That's called tender."
city.xk.4_wrap.4: I tied the ribbon in a bow, then a double knot, then once more for luck. The bunch lasted all day. That's not my talent, that's the knot.
city.xk.5_diagram.1: The diagram on the wall: the red line, Akademgorodok and Aton; the blue, Amber Shore and Zenith; the green, the Lighthouse. A dotted one is labelled: "Only in dreams so far."
city.xk.5_diagram.2: Beside it the arrow "You are here." It has been moved twice: first it was in the wrong place, then right, but nobody believed it.
city.xk.5_diagram.3: Someone has added a station by hand: "Bakery." It doesn't exist, but everyone rides there.
city.xk.5_diagram.4: A yellow line marks the one that only rumours run on. They say it has the loveliest view.
city.xk.5_fountain.1: The fountain water by the cable car smells of mountains, though there are none here. It must have dripped from the cabins.
city.xk.5_fountain.2: The night fountain babbles loudly, as if it wanted to be noticed.
city.xk.5_ledger.1: In the "Passengers' Questions" book I wrote: "Where do the cabins go at night?" I signed legibly so the answer could find me.
city.xk.5_ledger.2: I leafed through: "May I bring a dog?" "The dog will decide." "Why don't the cabins meet in the middle?" "You just blink."
city.xk.5_ledger.3: I wrote a question about the mitten. Right below, someone answered: "It isn't lost. It's on a business trip."
city.xk.5_ledger.prompt: E — write a question in the book
city.xk.5_lost.1: The case "Left in the cabins": a red mitten (one), a blue thermos, somebody's hat with a feather.
city.xk.5_lost.2: A tag on the mitten: "Cabin no. 7, Monday. Owner not found. Rides back and forth since Monday and seems to have learned the timetable."
city.xk.5_lost.3: A second mitten in the case! "Brought from cabin no. 3. A pair. Now we look for whoever lost both."
city.xk.5_lost.4: Both mittens are stitched together: "So they don't get lost again." No owner yet. The clerk keeps a request book.
city.xk.5_lost.5: A note in the case: "Owner found: a girl with a plait. She said she lost them on purpose so somebody would ride. Took them. The case is empty for the first time in a year."
city.xk.5_punch.1: The punch clinked. The ticket kept a hole shaped like a cabin. I wasn't going anywhere, but I kept the ticket.
city.xk.5_punch.2: I punched a ticket for an imaginary trip: "The stop to Zenith, 12 minutes, no changes." Nice when the route is short.
city.xk.5_punch.3: The hole came out slanted, like a cabin in the wind. An inspector would approve.
city.xk.6_clocks.1: The clocks on the board show different times, yet all of them are morning: the hands are stopped in different seconds of the same morning.
city.xk.6_clocks.2: The clocks show different things. The mender: "Each about its own. These about childhood, those about tomorrow."
city.xk.6_clocks.3: In the evening you can hear the clocks ticking out of step, like an orchestra whose conductor has gone to supper.
city.xk.6_keycut.1: The mender clamped a blank and said: "A key with no lock is just a metal hint." A minute later a new key lay on my palm. To what, they didn't say.
city.xk.6_keycut.2: The machine squealed and stopped. The key smells of hot metal. "For whatever you will need," said the mender, and was hardly joking.
city.xk.6_keycut.3: The key came out with wave-shaped teeth. "A rare pattern. It will fit doors that don't exist yet."
city.xk.6_radios.1: Brisk morning exercises on the radio. The mender whispers: "This set doesn't need mending. It's like this only in the mornings, then it spoils."
city.xk.6_radios.2: A bulletin: "Wind north, sea calm, mood moderate."
city.xk.6_radios.3: A pioneer song crackles out of the set, as if through time.
city.xk.6_radios.4: An evening request concert. The request: "For the mender, from L." The mender pretends not to hear but mends more slowly.
city.xk.6_radios.5: The set hisses softly, catching something far off: an announcer in Norwegian, music, silence, the announcer again.
city.xk.6_shoes.1: On the rack, pairs without owners: a child's strapped sandal, a size-43 boot, one red bootee. Each waits for someone's feet.
city.xk.6_shoes.2: A tag on the red bootee: "Heels replaced, sole glued. Running allowed. Running away not."
city.xk.6_shoes.3: The size-43 boot is heavy and polished. The owner said: "I'll come after my shift." The shift was three weeks ago.
city.xk.6_watch.1: On a velvet pad lies a pocket watch. It ticks loudly, slightly unevenly, like a heart after running.
city.xk.6_watch.2: The lid is engraved "L. from L." The mender: "Brought in March, wanted for May. Mended by May. May has passed."
city.xk.6_watch.3: Each morning the mender winds it and puts it back. "So it doesn't get bored. Idle watches spoil first."
city.xk.6_watch.4: Inside the lid in tiny letters: "If found, return it. If not found, wind it." The mender didn't show me; I saw by chance.
city.xk.6_watch.5: Today the watch keeps exact time, second for second. "See? They waited. Now to wait for whoever comes for them."
city.xk._bin.1: In the bin: tickets, an ice-cream cup and a newspaper folded in four. Somebody didn't finish it.
city.xk._bin.2: A flyer sticks out of the bin: "Silence for rent. Cheap." Someone added: "Cheap, how cheap?"
city.xk._bin.3: In the morning the bin holds fresh wrappers and one whole loaf. The crows pretend it has nothing to do with them.
city.xk._bin.4: By day the bin fills before your eyes: sweet wrappers, lollipop sticks. A sparrow sits beside it, an expert in the field.
city.xk._bin.5: In the evening there is a glass of half-drunk tea beside the bin. Somebody left it for later.
city.xk._bin.6: At night the bin rings hollow if you drop a coin in. I didn't try.
city.xk.k1notice.1: Torn from a notebook and pinned: "Lost: a pocket watch. Silver, engraved 'L. from L.' Finder gets tea and a talk. Ask at kiosk no. 6."
city.xk.k1notice.2: Under the notice, in another hand: "Saw something like it on the mender's tray. Running fast, as usual."
city.xk.k1notice.3: In the notice "lost" is crossed out and "forgotten" written above. Below: "Forgotten very long ago. L."
city.xpl.closed.any: A closed library is quiet. Everything stands in its place and is in no hurry.
city.xpl.closed.board: Monday, the library is closed. A card on the door: "We open on Tuesday at ten. The returns box works at any hour."
city.xpl.closed.counter: Nobody at the desk. A note with a tea-ring on it: "Tuesday from ten. Do not lose your reading diaries."
city.xpl.closed.shelf: On Mondays the shelves rest. The spines look straight ahead, and I do not disturb them.
city.xpl.diary.fri: Theme of the day: our town. Find the house you live in on the old map by the book wall. If you cannot, the house is newer than the map. That earns a stamp too.
city.xpl.diary.full: A new slip is pinned to the stand: "Diary completely filled? Then drop in on the librarian. She knows what to do with readers like you."
city.xpl.diary.half: At the bottom of the sheet, in pencil: "Eight stamps already. That is not a grade, it is a route."
city.xpl.diary.mon: Reading diary. Today is Monday and the pages are clean: it is the books' day off. Not laziness, just the order of things.
city.xpl.diary.sat: Theme of the day: anything at all. On Saturdays you may hop from shelf to shelf. At 11 a story is read in the children's corner.
city.xpl.diary.sun: Theme of the day: the sun. At 11 the Sunday story, and tea afterwards. Diaries are accepted for a stamp right up to closing time.
city.xpl.diary.thu: Theme of the day: poems. Reading aloud is allowed in a half-voice. Loud reading earns no stamp, but a good face does.
city.xpl.diary.tue: Theme of the day: the sea. Read a page on the Sea shelf, then get your stamp at the lending desk. On Tuesdays the kettle in the staff room is put on for two.
city.xpl.diary.wed: Theme of the day: birds. Find out from the field guide how a great tit differs from a blue tit, then go outside and check. A stamp for an honest check.
city.xpl.leave.1: I wrote one line on the postcard: "We are waiting here. The kettle is on on Tuesdays." I slipped it between the ticket and the clock without numbers. From the pile by the shelf I took another one to keep: they always leave a few here.
city.xpl.leave.2: I did not sign it: he will know who it is from. I laid the postcard with the other bookmarks and held my palm on it as on a warm mug. From the pile I took a clean one to keep.
city.xpl.leave.prompt: E — slip a postcard into the guide
city.xpl.ledger.1: The 1968 loan ledger, in a blue folder. Entry of 14 May: "Guide to Sundials, lent until 28 May. Reader: G. N." The due date is crossed out and written again, many times, in different inks.
city.xpl.ledger.2: At the bottom of the page, fresh ink: "Returned." Today's date. Below, a second hand: "Received. Do not worry. The kettle is hot."
city.xpl.ledger.3: A second entry in another hand: "Came on Tuesday. Did not come behind the desk, drank his tea standing by the window. Left before I turned round. Left a daisy."
city.xpl.ledger.4: A sheet is pinned to the ledger: "A messenger is needed. Somebody young, whom he will not be afraid of. Let them slip a postcard into the book, the rest is my business."
city.xpl.ledger.5: The ledger is closed, with a fresh line on the cover: "Reader: G. N. Status: comes on Tuesdays." Beside it, on a saucer, an empty cup and a daisy.
city.xpl.notice.1: The reading room is open from 10 to 8, except on Mondays. On Mondays the library rests: shelves need to breathe out now and then.
city.xpl.notice.10: Over the New Year days a tree made of books stands in the reading room. The top ones may be taken down only by two people, and only to be read.
city.xpl.notice.2: Please do not stack more than five books on the tables. A falling tower is not reading, it is gym class.
city.xpl.notice.3: Lost a scarf, a mitten or a thought? Scarves and mittens are in the box at the lending desk. Thoughts are harder, but we try.
city.xpl.notice.4: To the reader from 1968. Your loan card has turned up: no. 3-217, lovely handwriting, the surname blurred by time. The fine for all these years: zero roubles, zero kopecks. We counted twice.
city.xpl.notice.5: A small lamp has appeared by the Returned shelf. We did not put it there. Please leave it on: somebody finds it easier to read that way.
city.xpl.notice.6: A second bookmark was found in the Sundial Guide: a drawn clock without numbers, only a shadow. Signed: "If it is cloudy I will come all the same." A spare lamp for cloudy days has been bought.
city.xpl.notice.7: To our young readers: one quiet story needs a messenger. Postcards are at the lending desk, four roubles. Slip one into the Guide on the shelf by the window. We expect a reply on Tuesdays, at tea time.
city.xpl.notice.8: On Tuesday both cups were empty. That is a good sign: it means they were drunk. The book has been lent to the reader again, due date: "when he has finished". Thank you, all messengers.
city.xpl.notice.9: There is a festival in town today. The lending desk closes at six: the librarian wants to go to the square too, and we are letting him.
city.xpl.piano.1: I lifted the lid two fingers' width and play as if the keys were cotton wool. From the next capsule somebody tapped the wall softly: once, approvingly.
city.xpl.piano.2: I play very softly, a lesson in whispering. The capsule answers with all its concrete and, oddly enough, it sounds beautiful.
city.xpl.piano.3: Evening, few readers. I played everything I remember. From the hall below somebody applauds: pages rustle, one by one, like small palms.
city.xpl.pressA.fri: Friday: the weekend listings. An old film at Rassvet, a chess evening at the Cog club, a story for the smallest at the library. A note below: "Come with your parents, parents listen too."
city.xpl.pressA.mon: The bound run of the Town Herald for last week. There is no fresh issue: on Mondays the print shop rests together with the library.
city.xpl.pressA.sat: Saturday, the thick issue: a half-page crossword. Somebody has pencilled in "lighthouse" where "sea" was wanted, and it turns out both fit.
city.xpl.pressA.sun: The Sunday supplement, readers' letters. One begins: "I should like to find the person who borrowed a library book in May 1968 and took it away for a long while." Signed: "The Library."
city.xpl.pressA.thu: Thursday: an interview with the lighthouse keeper. Asked whether he gets bored, he answered: "I have people to talk to: thirty-three lamps, and all different."
city.xpl.pressA.tue: The Town Herald, Tuesday. On the front page the cable car, which has a new cabin again. Below in small print: the tide table and a yellow umbrella lost near the department store. A reward is promised to the finder.
city.xpl.pressA.wed: Wednesday: a report from the fishermen's pier on how to wean a gull off stealing from the tray. The editors' conclusion: you cannot. The recipe for pasties on page three is given without gulls.
city.xpl.pressB.fs: A chess magazine: a game played by post between two towns over four years. The last move was sent on a postcard. No winner is named: both insist they lost.
city.xpl.pressB.mt: The magazine Sky Above Us: a table of sunrises and sunsets for the week. One sunset is circled, with a note beside it: "The best one is the one you can see from the reading room."
city.xpl.pressB.su: A children's magazine: how to make an hourglass from two glasses and one patient week. Beside it, in somebody's pencil, a clock without numbers, only a shadow.
city.xpl.pressB.wt: Sky Above Us, an article on sundials: the shadow is shortest at noon, then stretches until it becomes night. The author calls it the most honest way to count time.
city.xpl.returned.1: The Returned shelf: books with no loan slips and no readers, but with neat bookmarks. All the spines face the window as if waiting for weather.
city.xpl.returned.2: On top lies the Sundial Guide, lent on 14 May 1968. The cover is worn soft. On the first page in pencil: "I read slowly. Forgive me."
city.xpl.returned.3: Between the pages is a cable-car ticket to the Lighthouse station. The date has rubbed off, but the stamp is the kind only people who treasure tickets have.
city.xpl.returned.4: A new bookmark: a clock without numbers, only the shadow of a gnomon. Signed: "If it is cloudy I will come all the same." I looked out of the window. The sky is just like that.
city.xpl.returned.5: On the shelf a card in the librarian's hand: "If you are reading this and have a postcard, slip it into the Guide. I will pass it on. Do not ask to whom: he will come himself."
city.xpl.returned.6: There are now three bookmarks in the Guide: the ticket, the clock without numbers and a daisy. The daisy is dry but does not crumble: it was carried carefully in a pocket.
city.xpl.returned.prompt: E — look at the Returned shelf
city.xpl.returned.rain: Rain. The lamp by the Returned shelf burns brighter than usual, and I see it is not here by chance: cloudy days are his days.
city.xpl.returns.1: The returns box. Its slot is exactly the thickness of a book: no thinner, no thicker. Inside it is muffled and warm, like a mailbox in winter.
city.xpl.returns.2: A card is stuck on the lid: "Books may be returned at any hour. We will not ask why it took so long."
city.xpl.returns.3: Under the slot there is a faint pencil mark on the metal: somebody checked whether a book would reach the bottom. It did.
city.xpl.returns.4: A corner of an envelope sticks out of the slot. Address: "The library, to the shelf by the window." I did not pull it out: it is not mine. But I can almost see the bookmark inside: a clock without numbers.
city.xpl.returns.5: The box is empty. That is news too: for the first time in many days nothing was returned and nothing was taken. The librarian says that happens when everything is in its place.
city.xpl.returns.6: On Monday the library is shut, but the box works round the clock. A corner of paper shows white in the slot: "To the reader from 1968. The kettle is on Tuesday, as usual. The librarian."
city.xpl.returns.prompt: E — look into the returns box
city.xpl.stamp.1: The librarian takes an ink pad from a drawer, breathes on the stamp and presses a round mark into my diary: a lamp with a green shade. "For quiet hours," she says.
city.xpl.stamp.2: At weekends the stamp is different: an open book with wings. "For reading with no use at all," the librarian explains. "The most valuable kind."
city.xpl.stamp.3: Four stamps in the diary. The librarian leafs through it and nods: "You can tell you are not reading for a grade."
city.xpl.stamp.4: Eight stamps, and the diary has swollen. She holds the cover down with a finger: "One day people will read it instead of you. Do not take offence, it is a compliment."
city.xpl.stamp.5: Twelve. The librarian takes out a red pencil and underlines my name on the cover: "This is not a mark, it is a bookmark."
city.xpl.stamp.6: The diary is full: a mark for every shelf, even the Returned. The librarian is silent for a long moment, then presses the last, big stamp: a clock without numbers. "I put that one in one reader's card. Long ago." Now you may come on a Tuesday for tea.
city.xpl.stamp.prompt: E — ask for a diary stamp
city.xpl.story.1: The librarian settles into the armchair by the round rug, and the little ones swoop down on the bean bags like sparrows on crumbs. Today's story is about a Little Lighthouse that was afraid of the dark. Every evening it lit its lamp so the ships would not be frightened, and the ships sailed off without saying thank you. But one day a small boat came back and blinked in reply. Since then the Lighthouse has not been afraid of the dark: it knows someone is sailing toward it in there.
city.xpl.story.2: A story about the Torn Page, which told everyone it came from the most important book. The page was picked up from the floor, smoothed out and held against another book. It fitted as if it belonged. It turns out that the right page sometimes simply gets lost on the way. The little ones argued for a long time about which book it came from. They agreed: a future one.
city.xpl.story.3: Today the story is about a Cat who lived in the reading room and followed those who had dropped a bookmark. He brought the bookmarks back in his teeth, carefully, by the corner. The readers thought that was how things were done. The Cat did not object. The children swore never to lose a bookmark again, just in case, so as not to teach the cat to work.
city.xpl.story.4: A Sunday story about the Kettle that boiled for two on Tuesdays. Once the one it boiled for was half an hour late, and the Kettle kept boiling all that time so the tea would not cool at once. The children listened very quietly. Then they asked whether the latecomer arrived. The librarian smiled: "You will tell me that when you grow up."
city.xpl.story.title: Story hour
city.xpl.tea.1: On Tuesdays the kettle is put on for two. The librarian nods at the second cup: "Have it. If he comes, I will pour again." The tea is strong and smells of thyme.
city.xpl.tea.2: The second cup is already warm: somebody was here before me. The librarian does not raise her head: "He asked me to say he got the postcard. And that our tea is too strong." I drink and stay quiet so as not to scare anyone off.
city.xpl.tea.prompt: E — take a cup of tea

dev.tp.city.q.home_girma.2: A sun on the night chart: 2
dev.tp.city.q.home_girma.3: A sun on the night chart: 3
dev.tp.city.q.store_umbrella.1: The Yellow Umbrella with the Duck: 1
dev.tp.city.q.store_umbrella.2: The Yellow Umbrella with the Duck: 2
